title: Advisor/Sr Advisor/Director – Manufacturing Science
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Company Overview

At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.


Position Brand Description

How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.

In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.

Responsibilities

As an individual contributor, you will work side by side with colleagues in Product Development, Manufacturing Operations, Quality, EHS, and Supply Chain, as well as with external manufacturing organizations. You will be a visible technical presence in cross-functional teams, mentor junior technical associates, and escalate significant technical, quality, safety, and supply risks to management with clear assessments and recommended actions.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Serve as Global Product Steward and subject matter expert for lyophilized, ADC and parenteral products, holding end-to-end technical accountability for process performance, product quality, and supply across all manufacturing sites, and serving as the primary technical interface between Product Development and commercial manufacturing.
  • Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
  • Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
  • Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
  • Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
  • Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
  • Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.
  • Author and review technical sections of global regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and responses to regulatory questions, and support inspection readiness at commercial sites.
  • Lead process improvement and lifecycle management projects, including introduction of new lyophilization, filling, and containment technologies and qualification of vials, stoppers, and other critical materials.

Basic Qualifications

  • A degree in a relevant area such as Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, or Chemistry with one of the following:
  • PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
  • Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
  • Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
  • Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
  • Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
  • Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.


Additional Skills/Preferences

We want you to bring your lyophilization and biologics expertise, commercial manufacturing experience, and technical influence to help launch and supply ADC and other lyophilized medicines.

Preferred experience includes:

  • Direct ADC drug product experience, including handling of cytotoxic or highly potent payloads and the stability and process sensitivities of conjugated antibodies.
  • Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.
  • Analytical characterization of lyophilized biologics and ADCs
  • Experience with container closure and critical material qualification, including vial and stopper selection, container closure integrity, and the interaction of materials with processing equipment.
  • Product stewardship experience, such as serving as technical owner or product lead for a commercial or late-stage product, authoring annual product reviews or technical risk assessments, and managing multi-site process harmonization.
  • Demonstrated leadership, influence, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret complex technical data, troubleshoot manufacturing issues, and clearly escalate risks and recommendations to management.
  • Preparation, review, and response to global regulatory submissions (e.g., BLAs, NDAs, or equivalent), post-approval changes, and support of regulatory inspections.
  • Working knowledge of statistical design of experiments and analysis, and of containment strategies and occupational exposure limits for potent compounds.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across Development, Operations, Quality, EHS, and external manufacturing partners.

We’re also excited if you bring an insatiable desire to learn, to innovate, and to challenge yourself for the benefit of patients.


Additional Information

  • Recognition and future promotion on the Technical Ladder
  • 10–20% domestic and international travel to commercial manufacturing sites and partners (to be confirmed by leadership)
  • Lilly is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Lilly is dedicated to helping individuals with disabilities to actively engage in the workforce, ensuring equal opportunities when vying for positions. If you require accommodation to submit a resume for a position at Lilly, please complete the accommodation request form () for further assistance. Please note this is for individuals to request an accommodation as part of the application process and any other correspondence will not receive a response.


Lilly is proud to be an EEO Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.


Our employee resource groups (ERGs) offer strong support networks for their members and are open to all employees. Our current groups include: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia (AMECA), Black Employees at Lilly (BE@Lilly), Chinese Culture Network (CCN), EnAble, Evolve, Lilly Indian Network (LIN), Organization of Latinx at Lilly (OLA), Pride (LGBTQ+ Allies), Veterans Leadership Network (VLN) and Women’s Initiative for Leading at Lilly (WILL).


Actual compensation will depend on a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. The anticipated wage for this position is

$130,500 - $211,200

Full-time equivalent employees also will be eligible for a company bonus (depending, in part, on company and individual performance). In addition, Lilly offers a comprehensive benefit program to eligible employees, including eligibility to participate in a company-sponsored 401(k); pension; vacation benefits; eligibility for medical, dental, vision and prescription drug benefits; flexible benefits (e.g., healthcare and/or dependent day care flexible spending accounts); life insurance and death benefits; certain time off and leave of absence benefits; and well-being benefits (e.g., employee assistance program, fitness benefits, and employee clubs and activities).Lilly reserves the right to amend, modify, or terminate its compensation and benefit programs in its sole discretion and Lilly’s compensation practices and guidelines will apply regarding the details of any promotion or transfer of Lilly employees.

title: Radiologic Tech FT Nights
description:
LOCATION: BAYLOR SCOTT & WHITE MEDICAL CENTER, WAXAHACHIE TX

DEPT: RADIOLOGY

SCHEDULE: FULL TIME NIGHTS

About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.

Job Summary

The Radiologic Technologist, supervised by a Radiologist, performs radiology procedures on patients. These procedures are requested by a physician or licensed provider to diagnose disease and injury, following established protocols.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Performs high-quality radiology procedures according to exam protocol in a timely manner. Maintains production and quality of imaging procedures by following established standards and procedures.
  • Demonstrates an understanding of radiation dose reference levels and monitoring. Takes action if the estimated dose exceeds set reference levels. Takes action when the reference level is exceeded, which may include patient follow-up.
  • Utilizes AIDET to communicate with patients. Identifies patient service needs, ensures the correct exam is performed, and builds rapport. Instructs and communicates with patients and their families about the test. Assesses the patient's ability to tolerate the exam.
  • Prepares the patient and area for the procedure. Positions the patient, adjusts immobilization devices, and moves equipment into position. Adjusts equipment controls to set exposure factors.
  • Protects patients and employees by following safety, infection-control, drug, and radiation policies. Uses proper sterile techniques for invasive procedures and maintains hand hygiene.
  • Maintains equipment and work area to meet quality and cleanliness standards. Works with engineers and physicists to ensure optimal equipment operation.
  • Reports issues to management or appropriate department. Assists in maintaining supplies inventory.
  • Ensures people are safe to enter the department by screening them according to approved policies and procedures.
  • Obtains, verifies, and maintains all relevant documentation like requisition/chart, patient history, pregnancy status, shielding precautions, consent forms, policies, and procedures.
  • Maintains medical imaging records in appropriate system and according to department policies and standards for interpretation in a timely manner.

Key Success Factors

  • Able to perform high quality radiology procedures according to exam protocol in a timely manner.
  • Able to explain the procedure and put patients at ease.
  • Provide services promptly, accurately, and cost-efficiently, following System and regulatory standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Able to perform tasks autonomously without need for routine oversight.
  • Able to stay calm and helpful during stress and take reasonable steps to resolve issues.
  • Able to effectively administer first aid and use emergency cart.
  • Ensure customer satisfaction by limiting wait times and providing courteous service. Remain professional, review patient satisfaction scores, and develop action plans when needed.
  • Demonstrates and maintains current knowledge, education, and skills for newborn, pediatric, young adult, adult, and geriatric care.
  • Able to serve as preceptor by providing quality training to new team members and on new services and initiatives.
  • Able to take call, if required.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.

CERTIFICATION/LICENSE/REGISTRATION

  • ARRT-R Radiography (ARRT-R)

title: Program Supervisor
description:
Mentor Community Services, a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.


Program Supervisor

Freeport, IL

Full Time Position: Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday 7a to 3pm, Tuesday 9am to 3pm

$21.45/hr


Are you looking for a career opportunity where you can make a difference in the lives of others? Look no further! This role is critical to our success. As a mission-driven organization, we are intensely focused on expanding access to services and developing new and more effective ways of delivering supports and services to individuals with a range of intellectual and developmental disabilities.

  • Facilitate the implementation of Individual Service Plans (ISP) and participate in a range of administrative duties including staff hiring, training, scheduling, and oversight.
  • Supervise a team of Caregivers supporting individuals we serve in the program.

  • Facilitate community involvement by accompanying individuals on outings in the community or providing transportation to work or other activities.

Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or equivalent.
  • One year related work experience.
  • Must be 18 years or older.
  • Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
  • Other licensure or certification where required by regulatory authority.
  • Excellent communication skills with an ability to establish rapport with team members and those we serve.
  • Strong organizational abilities to ensure staffing and schedules are maintained.
  • This is a great opportunity to gain supervisory skills and experience while still directly making a difference in the lives of the people we serve on a daily basis.

Why Join Us?

  • Full, Part-time, and As Needed schedules available.
  • Full compensation/benefits package for full-time employees.
  • 401(k) with company match.
  • Paid time off and holiday pay.
  • Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
  • Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.
  • Employee Referral Program bonus opportunities for eligible roles

Come join our amazing team of committed and caring professionals. Apply Today!



Sevita is a leading provider of home and community-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.

title: MD IDS - Product Delivery - Lead AI Data Engineer
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.



Lead AI Data Engineer

eCTS · CTI-MD · Path/Level: R3

At Lilly, we believe in the talent of our workforce. One of the best ways to utilize and develop that talent is to use our existing workforce to fill new and/or open positions. If you are looking for a new position within Lilly, you can view and apply to open roles posted in the internal job posting system. You must meet the minimum qualifications outlined in the job description and have/obtain work authorization in the country the position is located in order to be considered. When applying internally for a position, your current supervisor will receive notification that you have applied to the position. We encourage employees to discuss the opportunity with their supervisor prior to applying.

Path/Level: R3

Note: Roles are posted at the lowest level of a band, however, employees should search across all levels of the band to identify all opportunities. Employees hired on banded positions (ex: P1–P3, R-path, B1–B3, etc.) transfer at their current level, despite the level indicated on the job posting. For example, if an R2 candidate is selected for an R1–R3 banded position, the candidate will remain an R2 in the new role.

At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We're looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.

Role Overview

eCTS is a core clinical supply product within CTI-MD, helping make sure the right investigational medicine reaches the right patient at the right time. Over the next few years, clinical systems will evolve from a database-centric application into an intelligent, cloud-native clinical supply data platform: one where critical business logic is explicit and tested, data is served as governed products, and AI agents work safely alongside people to plan, monitor, and resolve supply events.

We are seeking a hands-on Data Systems Lead to drive that evolution. This role owns the data foundation of eCTS today, including the stored procedures and database objects that carry critical business logic, and leads its transformation into AI-enabled, full-stack flows, including the external facing site modernization. You will shape how data is structured, migrated, secured, served, and made AI-ready in a regulated pharmaceutical environment, while staying deeply hands-on with schema design, query optimization, migration, and troubleshooting, and setting standards the wider team can follow.

The person in this role will help build the following future state. It is the lens for every responsibility below.

Logic made explicit

Business rules held in legacy stored procedures are documented, covered by automated tests, and progressively re-platformed, with AI accelerating analysis and conversion under validated controls.

Data as a Service

eCTS data is published as governed, well-documented data products and APIs with clear contracts and SLAs, serving the application, analytics, adjacent clinical systems, and AI consumers.

AI-ready and agent-enabled

Data is structured, described, and exposed so AI agents can reason over it and act on it safely, with least-privilege access, human-in-the-loop approvals, and full auditability.

Cloud-native and as-code

Database changes, infrastructure, and quality checks flow through automated pipelines, with observability that moves operations from reactive to proactive.

What We're Really Looking For (Core Needs)

Two things matter most in this role:

  • Ability to lead and technically execute agentic solutions independently. We have a strong and growing pipeline of agentic AI opportunities across eCTS, ranging from AI-assisted conversion of legacy logic to agents that surface, explain, and help resolve clinical supply and data issues. We need this person to lead and drive that space: to challenge and align platform-level teams, set technical direction, and execute hands-on without hand-holding. This is an autonomous, get-it-done technical leadership role, not a coordination-only one.
  • Genuine passion for the core database work. eCTS's stored procedures and database objects encode years of clinical supply know-how and remain a key contributor to the product today. This role owns that work end to end: enhancing it, continuously improving it, and actively using AI to convert these legacy flows into future-state full-stack and AI-enabled flows. We need someone who values this foundation, takes pride in keeping it healthy and reliable, and is energized by both mastering the existing logic and leading its transformation, not just by greenfield modernization.

What You Will Do

Database Design & Development

  • Own, maintain, and continuously improve eCTS's existing stored procedures and database objects, which carry critical business logic today, while leading their conversion into full-stack and AI-enabled flows using AI-assisted approaches.
  • Make embedded business logic explicit: document rules, build automated unit and regression tests for stored procedures and data logic, and create the safety net that makes confident, rapid change possible.
  • Own the design, development, and evolution of relational and non-relational data models supporting eCTS and IWRS.
  • Write, review, and optimize complex SQL, stored procedures, functions, and scripts, with the depth and care to keep long-standing logic correct and performant.
  • Translate product and engineering requirements into robust, scalable database designs.
  • Establish and enforce data modeling standards, naming conventions, and design patterns across the team.

Database Modernization & Migration

  • Lead the technical execution of the eCTS database modernization strategy, moving from legacy databases to a modern, cloud-native data platform.
  • Design and deliver migration approaches (schema conversion, data mapping, ETL/ELT pipelines, and cutover plans) that minimize disruption to global trial operations.
  • Apply AI-assisted tooling to schema conversion, code translation, and data reconciliation, with evaluation and human review built into the process.
  • Design for decoupling, using event-driven and change-data-capture (CDC) patterns so IWRS and downstream consumers can evolve independently.
  • Partner with architects to evaluate target database technologies, trade-offs, and integration patterns.
  • De-risk migration through prototypes, dry runs, reconciliation, and rollback planning.

Data Products & AI Readiness

  • Design eCTS data as reusable data products with clear ownership, documentation, data contracts, and SLAs, in line with the CTI-MD Data as a Service (DaaS) direction.
  • Build the metadata, lineage, and semantic context that let people and AI systems find, understand, and trust eCTS data.
  • Expose governed data access for applications and AI agents through APIs and agent tooling (for example, Model Context Protocol servers), with least-privilege and auditable access patterns.
  • Apply retrieval and vector search patterns (for example, embeddings in PostgreSQL) where they add real value to search, support, and decision-making.

Agentic AI & Technical Innovation

  • Lead and drive the exploration and delivery of agentic AI solutions across eCTS, working from a strong and growing opportunity pipeline.
  • Set technical direction, prototype, and execute agentic solutions hands-on, independently and without hand-holding.
  • Build the evaluation, guardrail, and observability practices that make agents trustworthy in a regulated setting: test sets, quality metrics, human-in-the-loop approval for consequential actions, and full traces of agent behavior.
  • Challenge, influence, and align platform-level teams to unblock and advance agentic initiatives.
  • Bring a builder's bias: turn ideas and POCs into working, production-ready capabilities, and keep pace with fast-moving AI practices and tools.

Technical Leadership

  • Act as the technical point of reference for all database and data platform matters on eCTS.
  • Guide engineers on data design decisions, performance tuning, and best practices, including how to work effectively with AI coding and data tools.
  • Review database changes and pull requests, ensuring quality, consistency, and maintainability.
  • Balance long-term data architecture health against near-term delivery needs.

Engineering Excellence

  • Treat the database as code: version-controlled schema and logic, automated migrations, and database changes delivered through CI/CD with automated quality gates.
  • Use infrastructure as code and repeatable environments to make development, testing, and validation faster and more consistent.

Performance, Reliability & Operations

  • Monitor, diagnose, and tune database performance: indexing, query plans, partitioning, and capacity.
  • Ensure high availability, backup/recovery, and disaster-recovery readiness for eCTS data.
  • Define service-level objectives and data observability so issues are detected and addressed before they affect trial operations.
  • Partner with support and operations teams to resolve production data issues and prevent recurrence.
  • Build AI-enabled monitoring and operational tooling, such as anomaly detection and assisted root-cause analysis, that improves database observability and support.

Data Integrity, Security & Compliance

  • Ensure database solutions meet GxP, data integrity (ALCOA+), validation, and audit requirements.
  • Apply risk-based assurance approaches, including Computer Software Assurance (CSA), and support the risk-proportionate data governance expected under ICH E6(R3).
  • Define how AI-assisted changes and agent actions are validated, reviewed, and recorded, and stay current with emerging regulatory expectations for AI in GxP environments.
  • Implement data security, access controls, encryption, and data-retention practices in line with Lilly policy and regulatory expectations.
  • Maintain documentation and traceability required for validated, regulated systems.

Collaboration & Delivery

  • Partner with the eCTS Product Manager, engineers, architects, and quality teams throughout the delivery lifecycle.
  • Contribute to backlog refinement, estimation, and sprint delivery in an Agile environment.
  • Support incremental, release-based delivery, contributing database work across successive releases without regressions.

Knowledge Sharing & Mentoring

  • Coach and mentor engineers on database design, performance, modernization, and AI-enabled engineering practices.
  • Share domain and technical knowledge to raise the overall data and AI capability of the team.
  • Bring a no-ego, team-first mindset, prioritizing shared success over individual recognition.

Your Minimum Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline.

Experience

  • 6+ years of hands-on database engineering / development experience.
  • Experience leading database design and development on non-trivial software products.
  • Experience delivering data migration or database modernization efforts.
  • Experience working with engineering teams in Agile environments.

Technical Skills

  • Strong SQL and relational database expertise (e.g., SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, or equivalent), including performance tuning and query optimization.
  • Deep, hands-on comfort with stored procedures and complex database logic, and a genuine willingness to own and improve long-standing legacy objects.
  • Solid data modeling skills across transactional and analytical use cases.
  • Experience with ETL/ELT and data migration tooling and patterns.
  • Working knowledge of cloud data platforms (Azure and/or AWS) and modern managed database services.
  • Understanding of database security, high availability, backup/recovery, and monitoring.
  • Hands-on experience building AI- or LLM-enabled solutions (for example, agents, retrieval, or AI-assisted code and data workflows), including at least one used by others beyond a personal prototype.
  • Experience with database-as-code practices: source control, CI/CD, automated migrations, and database change management.
  • Ability to read and reason about application code well enough to partner effectively with engineers on data-related issues.

Leadership Behaviors

  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, driving technical initiatives end to end and influencing other teams without relying on close direction.
  • Comfort making sound decisions with incomplete information in a fast-moving technology space, and learning quickly as tools and practices evolve.

What You Should Bring

  • Experience in Pharmaceutical, Life Sciences, Clinical Development, Supply Chain, or Regulatory / Quality domains.
  • Understanding of GxP, validation, data integrity, and regulated environments, including risk-based approaches such as Computer Software Assurance.
  • Experience with clinical, manufacturing, or laboratory systems (e.g., IWRS / clinical supply systems).
  • Experience with agent frameworks, Model Context Protocol, LLM evaluation, or AI observability tooling.
  • Experience with automated database testing and migration tools (e.g., tSQLt, pgTAP, Flyway, Liquibase) and infrastructure as code.
  • Familiarity with event streaming and CDC, NoSQL, vector databases, lakehouse platforms (e.g., Databricks), or analytics platforms.
  • Relevant database, cloud, or AI certifications are a plus.

The role serves as a strategic solution leader for enterprise access transformation, bringing deep knowledge of healthcare access operations, scheduling workflows, Epic capabilities, digital solutions, automation, and industry best practices to improve how patients identify, navigate, schedule, and receive care.

The Enterprise Access Solution Architect evaluates current-state access workflows and translates operational challenges and strategic priorities into scalable future-state solutions. Areas of focus may include scheduling optimization, digital and self-service access, guided scheduling and decision support, template and capacity management, contact center workflows, referral pathways, automation, and emerging technologies.

Working across Medical Group operations, clinical leadership, Enterprise Platforms/IS, Digital, analytics, and other enterprise partners, this role bridges access strategy, operational workflow, and technology delivery to ensure solutions are scalable, standardized, measurable, and aligned with enterprise access priorities.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Evaluates current-state patient access workflows and identifies opportunities to improve standardization, efficiency, scheduling accuracy, patient experience, provider experience, and operational performance.
  • Leads solution exploration, workflow design, and future-state planning sessions with operational leaders, clinical stakeholders, Enterprise Platforms/IS, Digital, and other enterprise partners.
  • Designs scalable enterprise access solutions that balance patient needs, clinical appropriateness, provider continuity, operational requirements, organizational standards, and technology capabilities.
  • Knowledge of interdependencies of healthcare landscape and its influence on portfolio
  • Supports the development and optimization of scheduling pathways, decision support tools, guided scheduling, self-service capabilities, and other solutions designed to connect patients with the appropriate provider, location, visit type, and level of care.
  • Evaluates opportunities to leverage automation, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and existing enterprise platform capabilities to simplify workflows and improve patient access.
  • Partners with and runs teams towards the identification of problems/opportunities from a Digital Innovation perspective
  • Oversee or perform the development and documentation of business requirements, goals, deliverables, and specifications with customers, employees, and help staff.
  • Supports testing and validation of access solutions to ensure technology configuration accurately reflects approved operational requirements, scheduling standards, and intended patient workflows.
  • Collaborates with Epic analysts, technical specialists, solution architects, digital teams, analytics partners, and managed service partners to ensure access solutions are technically feasible, scalable, supportable, and aligned with enterprise standards.

Key Success Factors

  • Epic certification(s) or accreditation(s), particularly within applications supporting patient access, scheduling, referrals, or ambulatory operations strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting a large, complex, multi-market healthcare system or medical group strongly preferred.
  • Experience with enterprise patient access strategy, scheduling optimization, template and capacity management, contact center operations, digital scheduling, or patient navigation.
  • Advanced leadership, problem solving, team building, and judgment-making skills.
  • Skilled project manager with ability to articulate business needs.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and social communication skills.
  • Proficient computer software and database skills.
  • Ability to focus and prioritize strategic targets and work in a growing and challenging environment.

  • Knowledge of interdependencies of healthcare landscape and its influence on portfolio.
  • Establishes external relationships with other thought managers in the enterprise.
  • Maintains a broad knowledge of state-of-the-art technology, equipment, and systems.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • EDUCATION - Bachelor's or 4 years of work experience above the minimum qualification
  • EXPERIENCE - 7 Years of Experience

title: Electrical Technician
description:
Location: Den Helder, Netherlands

Over het team:

In de huidige wereld van dreiging is de operationele beschikbaarheid van onze klanten van groot belang en daarmee het verlenen van een goede service. Binnen Thales Hengelo is Services een domein wat sterk groeit en is één van de speerpunten voor de toekomst. De services worden geleverd op de geleverde radarsystemen, waaronder technische assistenties, reparaties, overhauls en modificaties/ upgrades. De totale Services-afdeling bestaat uit ongeveer 100 mensen.


Over jouw toekomstige baan:

In de functie van elektromonteur maak je deel uit van een team van monteurs en test engineers die werkzaam zijn namens Thales bij de onderhoudsorganisatie van de Koninklijke Marine (DMI) in Den Helder. De Marine heeft meerdere schepen die zijn uitgerust met high tech radarsystemen van Thales en gedurende de gehele levenscyclus ondersteuning nodig hebben. Daarnaast wordt in Den Helder ook voor de Koninklijke Landmacht de radarsystemen onderhouden. Je bent met het team verantwoordelijk voor de uitvoer van verschillende services activiteiten.


Het onboardingstraject voor de functie vindt plaats bij Thales in Hengelo voor een periode tussen de 6 en 12 maanden afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring. Gedurende deze periode zul je diverse trainingen volgen en inwerken op de GM200-systeem. In Den Helder zul je daarnaast inwerken op andere systemen van Thales.


Na de eerste 6 tot 12 maanden werk je hoofdzakelijk op het terrein bij de Marine en eventueel op klantlocaties over de hele wereld om onze services aan de klanten te leveren om ervoor te zorgen dat de systemen operationeel beschikbaar blijven. Incidenteel zul je bij Thales in Hengelo werken.


Belangrijkste taken en verantwoordelijkheden zijn:

  • Monteren van mechatronische (sub)systemen en kabinetten met zowel statische als dynamische delen.
  • Aanbrengen en afwerken van bedrading en bundels in radarsystemen.
  • Het uitlijnen van radarsystemen.
  • Voert preventief en correctief onderhoud uit op de (sub)systemen.
  • Voert diagnoses en reparaties van (sub)systemen.
  • Voert alle werkzaamheden volgens de richtlijnen uit, op tijd en gestelde kwaliteit.
  • Documenteert alle uitgevoerde werkzaamheden in een bijbehorende rapportage.
  • Voert inspecties uit van de (sub)systemen op locatie en brengt advies uit voor verbetering werking van het systeem.
  • On-the-job trainingen uitvoeren.
  • Zorgt voor een veilige werkomgeving (HSE-richtlijnen).
  • Continue verbeteren van processen en leveringsresultaten.
  • Rapporteren aan het de Team Leider en Afdelingsmanager van de voortgang van de werkzaamheden.

Waarom ben jij een goede match:

  • MBO niveau 3 of 4 in de richting van Elektronica of Mechatronica.
  • Enige werkervaring in de machinebouw is een pre.
  • Oog voor detail.
  • Technische tekeningen lezen.
  • Een teamplayer.
  • Beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal.
  • Stressbestendig en probleem oplossend vermogen
  • Klantgericht en professionaliteit in omgang met de externe klant.
  • Beschikbaarheid tot (internationale) reizen.

Wat krijg jij er voor terug:

  • Een uitdagende baan in een leuk team binnen onze high-tech, innovatieve werkomgeving. Inclusief alle ruimte voor eigen initiatief en goede ideeën.
  • Mogelijkheden voor persoonlijke en professionele ontwikkeling binnen de organisatie, bijvoorbeeld op technisch, commercieel of internationaal vlak.
  • Waardevolle internationale samenwerkingen met collega’s en klanten.
  • Een comfortabele werkplek in een moderne omgeving, met aandacht voor flexibiliteit en de juiste werk-privé balans.
  • Een goed salaris, passende reiskostenvergoeding en de mogelijkheid om jaarlijks jouw arbeidsvoorwaarden te personaliseren: je kunt bijvoorbeeld vrije dagen ruilen voor internetkosten, ons fietsenplan, bedrijfsfitness en verhuiskosten.
  • 40 vakantiedagen per jaar.


Interesse?

Solliciteer nu door hieronder op ‘Apply now’ te klikken! Voor vragen kan je contact opnemen met onze Talent Acquisition Partner Victor ter Avest via victor.teravest@thalesgroup.com.


Of solliciteer direct door op onderstaande link te klikken.

Dat betekent dat gelijke kansen, inclusiviteit en een informele cultuur een essentieel onderdeel uitmaken van ons succes. Maar ook dat jouw gezondheid en geluk voor ons erg belangrijk zijn! title: Data Scientist -AI Drug Discovery
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


About Lilly

At Lilly, everything we do starts with patients. We unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our global team of over 50,000 employees work with urgency and purpose to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. We bring our best to this work because people depend on it. If you're driven by purpose and determined to make a meaningful difference for patients, we invite you to bring your skill and your commitment to Lilly.

About Technology@Lilly

At Lilly, technology is not a support function. It is how a global medicine company operates, innovates, and delivers. Lilly in Bengaluru builds the capabilities that make this possible, cloud platforms, AI systems, and automation at enterprise scale, all in service of a purpose that makes this technology work genuinely distinctive, from advancing drug discovery to enabling connected clinical trials to keeping a global medicine company running at the standard patients deserve.

About the Role

As a Data Scientist in AI Drug Discovery, you will use data science and machine learning to help answer consequential questions in drug discovery: which targets to pursue, which perturbations to test, and how cellular systems may respond.

Competency :

Data Scientist, AI Drug Discovery

A core focus of this position is single-cell biology and virtual cell modelling. You will develop and evaluate in silico models of cellular state and response, connect predictions to biological evidence, and translate results into clear recommendations for experimental scientists. You will join a multidisciplinary environment spanning biology, chemistry, computational science and engineering. The role is ideal for someone who enjoys turning an ambiguous scientific question into a rigorous computational problem, challenges their own conclusions, and delivers reusable work that scientists can trust and apply.

Key Skills Required:

  • Strong Python skills and practical experience with a machine learning and deep learning networksf.
  • Solid grounding in machine learning, model validation, and experimental design.
  • Working knowledge of transformers or graph neural networks and of sound train/validation/test design.
  • Experience working with large, noisy or heterogeneous scientific and biomedical datasets.
  • Experience with single-cell omics, genetics, chemistry or imaging data.
  • Experience running training and analysis on HPC, GPU or cloud infrastructure.
  • Ability to communicate technical findings, uncertainty, and limitations to collaborators from different disciplines.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Develop and validate models. Build, train, benchmark and validate machine learning models for scientific data, including single-cell omics, genetics, chemistry and imaging. Select methods based on the scientific question, from classical machine learning to deep learning and foundation models.
  • Advance virtual cell modelling. Develop and evaluate models that predict cellular state and response to genetic or chemical perturbations. Use them for in silico screening and prioritise high-value experiments.
  • Support target identification. Combine model outputs, perturbation evidence and prior biological knowledge to nominate and rank candidate targets. Communicate strength of evidence, uncertainty, limitations and proposed experimental validation.
  • Create analysis-ready data. Build reproducible workflows to ingest, harmonise, quality-control and document public and internal datasets across formats and modalities.
  • Integrate scientific knowledge. Incorporate regulatory and interaction networks, ontologies, pathways and other biological or chemical priors into models, and quantify the contribution of each information source.
  • Scale and operationalise work. Run training and analysis on HPC, GPU and cloud infrastructure using versioned code, containers, automated testing and reusable software components.
  • Collaborate and influence. Partner with scientists and engineers to frame questions, define decision criteria, and interpret findings. Present clearly to technical, scientific, and leadership audiences.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computational Chemistry, Computational Biology, Physics, Statistics, or a closely related quantitative field
  • 3+ years of experience applying machine learning in industry or academia, including delivering end-to-end projects and contributing to research or technical direction within a team
  • Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, with hands-on experience developing and evaluating models

Desirable Skills:

  • Experience with single-cell and perturbation data (e.g., Perturb-seq, CRISPR screens) and virtual cell or foundation models.
  • Familiarity with statistical genetics methods (GWAS, fine-mapping, colocalization) and multi-omics integration.
  • Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, pathway databases, or other structured biological priors.

    • Controlar y monitorizar los cambios del proceso.
    • Mejorar de forma continua el proceso en fiabilidad y eficacia

  • Soporte a los proyectos de la planta:

title: Consultant Neurosurgeon (Functional Neurosurgery) - Abu Dhabi
description:
Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced and highly qualified Consultant Neurosurgeon specializing in Functional Neurosurgery to join our multidisciplinary neuroscience team in Abu Dhabi. The successful candidate will provide comprehensive evaluation, surgical management, and long-term care for patients with complex neurological disorders requiring functional neurosurgical interventions. The role includes expertise in Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS), epilepsy surgery, neuromodulation, and other advanced functional neurosurgical procedures, working collaboratively with neurologists, neurophysiologists, neuroradiologists, rehabilitation specialists, and allied healthcare professionals to deliver evidence-based, patient-centered care.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and manage patients requiring functional neurosurgical interventions for movement disorders, epilepsy, chronic pain, spasticity, and other neurological conditions.
  • Perform advanced functional neurosurgical procedures, including Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS), lesioning procedures, spinal cord stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation, and other neuromodulation therapies as appropriate.
  • Conduct comprehensive pre-operative assessments and determine patient suitability for surgical intervention through multidisciplinary case discussions.
  • Collaborate closely with movement disorder neurologists, epileptologists, neurophysiologists, neuroradiologists, and rehabilitation teams to optimize patient outcomes.
  • Perform intraoperative planning, neuronavigation, stereotactic procedures, and image-guided neurosurgical techniques.
  • Provide comprehensive post-operative care, follow-up assessments, and management of surgical outcomes and complications.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary neuroscience clinics, case conferences, tumor boards (where applicable), and departmental meetings.
  • Maintain accurate clinical documentation and operative reports in accordance with hospital policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Supervise and mentor junior neurosurgeons, residents, fellows, and medical students.
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives, clinical governance activities, and patient safety programs.
  • Contribute to clinical research, publications, and academic teaching within the department.
  • Participate in on-call neurosurgical services and emergency neurosurgical care as required.
  • Ensure compliance with international standards of neurosurgical practice, infection prevention protocols, and hospital accreditation requirements.

Qualifications

  • Medical degree (MBBS or equivalent) from a recognized institution.
  • Completion of an accredited Neurosurgery Residency Program.
  • Fellowship training in Functional Neurosurgery, Stereotactic Neurosurgery, or Advanced Neurosurgical Techniques from a recognized international center.
  • Board Certification in Neurosurgery.
  • Eligibility for or possession of DOH (Department of Health – Abu Dhabi) Consultant License or eligibility to obtain one.

Experience

  • Minimum of 8–10 years of post-specialization clinical experience in neurosurgery, including significant experience in functional neurosurgery.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS), stereotactic neurosurgery, and neuromodulation procedures.
  • Experience managing patients with movement disorders, epilepsy, chronic pain, and other functional neurological conditions.
  • Experience working within multidisciplinary neuroscience teams.
  • Academic, research, and teaching experience is desirable.

Skills & Competencies

  • Advanced surgical expertise in functional and stereotactic neurosurgery.
  • Strong clinical judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Expertise in neuronavigation, stereotactic systems, and image-guided surgical techniques.
  • Excellent operative, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary clinical teams.
  • Commitment to evidence-based practice, patient safety, and continuous professional development.
  • Strong leadership, mentoring, and teaching abilities.
  • High ethical standards and patient-centered approach.
  • Proficiency in electronic medical records and clinical documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Fellowship from internationally recognized institutions in North America, Europe, Australia, or equivalents.
  • Experience with advanced neuromodulation technologies and minimally invasive functional neurosurgical procedures.
  • Active involvement in clinical research, peer-reviewed publications, and international neurosurgical societies.
  • Membership or fellowship in recognized neurosurgical organizations.

title: HHD Redeployment Specialist, Resident (Part Time)
description:
Posting Date

10/26/20261300 Morris DrSte 100, Chesterbrook, Pennsylvania, 19087-5559, United States of America

This is a part-time in-person role at the North Wales Dialysis center located at 1551 S Valley Forge Rd in Lansdale, PA. There could be occasional shifts to Huntingdon Valley Dialysis at 769 Huntingdon Pike, in Huntingdon Valley, PA. This would be shifts Monday-Thursday during regular business hours.


GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Part-Time HHD Redeployment Specialist - Resident is responsible for hands-on equipment management and redeployment services for NxStage HHD delivery systems and associated water treatment equipment. This is a physically demanding, inventory and equipment focused role that involved continuous material handling, lifting and maneuvering heavy dialysis machines (weighing 85+ lbs), performing chemical disinfections and functional testing, managing hub inventory and staging, vendor coordination, scheduling with clinic teammates and patients, troubleshooting logistics issues, and maintaining effective communication with leadership. This part-time position operates under the direct supervision and guidance of the local Redeployment Hub Lead.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs redeployment procedures (decontamination and testing) on dialysis delivery systems to prepare them for storage and redeployment
  • Communicates with clinic teams, patients, machine vendor, and transportation services regarding normal equipment order operations
  • Organizes orders in tracking files and inventory systems. Communicates reporting to supervisor
  • Troubleshoots order issues by communicating with patient/clinic and asking questions to machine vendor and transport services
  • Demonstrates a commitment to learning and seeks opportunities to expand knowledge and skills in redeployment operations
  • Other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Required

  • 0-2 years of related experience
  • High School Diploma or equivalent (GED)
  • Typing/Computer Skills
  • On-Phone Communication Skills
  • Organizational Skills

Preferred

  • Logistics Coordination Experience
  • Equipment Manufacturing/Repair/Maintenance Experience
  • Healthcare Experience
  • Operational Experience

TIME AND TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

Part-time hours ~3 days a week Monday – Thursday during regular business hours

In-person work at North Wales Dialysis with 1-2 visits a month to Huntingdon Valley Dialysis

LANGUAGE SKILLS & WORK ENVIORNMENT

Language Skills

  • Fluent in written and verbal English skills necessary to successfully perform the essential functions, duties, and responsibilities of the position, including reading equipment manuals, safety data sheets (SDS), and communicating with vendors and clinical staff.

Work Environment

  • Environment Level: Warehouse / Equipment Processing Hub / Clinical Support environment. Moderate noise levels (e.g., equipment testing systems, packaging tools, light traffic).
  • Hazard & Biohazard Exposure: Job-required tasks involve handling returned clinical equipment with potential exposure to chemical disinfectants, cleaning agents, and mucous membrane or skin contact with blood, body fluids, or dialysate fluids (Level II/III). TEAMMATE USE OF APPROPRIATE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) IS MANDATORY (including gloves, eye protection, gowns/aprons, and closed-toe safety footwear as required).

Physical Demands & ADA Requirements

Physical requirements can vary and must be reviewed with management. However, due to the nature of equipment redeployment and inventory operations, this role has substantial physical demands.

Heavy Physical & Material Handling Demands

  • Heavy Lifting & Moving (85+ lbs): Constantly required to lift, move, maneuver, position, push, and pull bulky NxStage HHD dialysis machines and heavy equipment weighing 85 lbs or more, utilizing material handling devices (dollies, two-wheel hand trucks, pallet jacks, ramps) and team-lift procedures where appropriate. Regularly lifts and carries supplies and components weighing up to 45–50 lbs unassisted.
  • Body Mobility & Posture: Frequent to continuous standing and walking on concrete/hard floor surfaces throughout scheduled shifts. Frequent bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, squatting, twisting, and reaching (both overhead and below waist level) to inspect, clean, connect, and stage equipment on pallets or shelving.
  • Strength & Manual Dexterity: High upper-body strength, grip strength, and manual dexterity required to manipulate heavy, awkward equipment, assemble parts, handle tubing/fittings, operate handheld tools, and utilize computer peripherals.
  • Visual Demands: Vision adequate to perform essential job duties, including reading serial numbers, digital screens, diagnostic test readouts, and the ability to differentiate colors on chemical/disinfection test strips.

ADA Statement

More than just pay, our DaVita Rewards package connects teammates to what matters most. Teammates are eligible to begin receiving benefits on the first day of the month following or coinciding with one month of continuous employment. Below are some of our benefit offerings.

  • Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, paid time off, PTO cash out
  • Support for you and your family: Family resources, EAP counseling sessions, access Headspace®, backup child and elder care, maternity/paternity leave and more
  • Professional development programs: DaVita offers a variety of programs to help strong performers grow within their career and also offers on-demand virtual leadership and development courses through DaVita’s online training platform StarLearning.

Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. 2027 Hardware Engineering Apprentice – Level 6 Electro-Mechanical Engineering Degree Apprenticeship

Start Date: Monday 6 September 2027

Employee Type: Permanent

Location: Crawley

Working Schedule: 37 hours a week, Monday – Thursday 8 hours a day, Friday 5 hours (Flexible start time between 07:00 and 09:30)

Turn your curiosity into a career. If you’re passionate about engineering, eager to learn, and looking for a degree apprenticeship that blends academic study with hands-on experience, we’d love to hear from you….

We’re currently recruiting an apprentice to join our Hardware Engineering team, while also completing an Electro-Mechanical Engineering Degree Apprenticeship. It’s a fantastic opportunity to grow, as well as develop your skills.

Benefits of the Programme:

  • Earn a salary while studying for your apprenticeship
  • Gain hands-on experience in a real engineering environment
  • Receive job-specific training and development
  • Achieve a recognised engineering qualification
  • Secure a permanent role from the start of your apprenticeship
  • Have your university tuition fees fully paid

About the Role:

This exciting Hardware Apprentice role will develop your skills by the designing and implementation of the engineering solutions in accordance with programme and product requirements. Typical tasks will range from requirements management via the design and development cycle, to test, integration and validation of complex products and systems.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, implement and test engineering solutions in accordance with Thales procedures
  • Attendance at project reviews
  • Creation of functional and physical system architectures
  • Preparation of engineering specifications, interface control documents & test documentation
  • Deliver tasks on time and to the required quality
  • Work as a team-player asking for guidance and direction where necessary
  • Develop knowledge and skills within the engineering discipline
  • Effectively communicate engineering issues related to own tasks
  • And much more….

Through our degree apprenticeship you’ll be making the most of your talents, getting to understand engineering from the ground up; and doing so with the help of one of the biggest and best names in the industry. We are looking for enthusiastic individuals who are motivated, committed and keen to learn. A self-starter who can manage their time, show initiative and have a genuine interest in engineering and Thales. Successful candidates will show self-discipline and an aspiration to achieve a degree qualification.

Apprenticeship Programme:

You'll work towards a Level 6 Electro-Mechanical Engineering Degree Apprenticeship with the University of Nottingham while gaining valuable hands-on experience in the workplace.

The programme lasts 5.5 years and combines:

  • On-campus learning
  • Online study
  • Practical, work-based learning

You'll typically attend the university for around four weeks each year, delivered in one-week blocks. Throughout the programme, you'll develop both your technical knowledge and practical engineering skills.

On successful completion of the apprenticeship and End Point Assessment, you'll achieve:

  • A fully funded BEng (Hons) in Electro-Mechanical Engineering
  • A Level 6 Electro-Mechanical Engineering Degree Apprenticeship qualification.

The programme is accredited by the Institute of Mechanical Engineers for those wishing to progress towards Chartered Engineer status later in their career.


Entry Requirements:

To apply, you will need:

  • 3 A Levels (BBB) including Mathematics (Citizenship Skills, General Studies and Critical Thinking are not accepted), Alternative Level 3 qualifications will be accepted, subject to passing a Maths assessment. Alternative Level 3 qualifications include Engineering and Manufacturing T Level (Merit), BTEC Extended Diploma in Engineering discipline (MMD) or a preceding engineering apprenticeship
  • 5 GCSES grade 9-4 (A-C) including English and Maths

Please note that applicants who already hold a relevant degree will not be eligible for this programme.

  • Performance-related pay uplifts

Monitors attendance of team members and schedules breaks and shifts as necessary. Accountable for overseeing daily operations and workflows. Ensures customer and department satisfaction. Ensures timely follow-up and escalation recovery is performed.

Performs account research to assist with system-level initiatives or requests. Examples include customer complaints, incorrect estimates, and administrative write-offs. Immediately reports any performance, productivity, and behavioral issues regarding staff to management for review.
  • Monitors financial performance by ensuring financial conversations and collection attempts. Assists Access Services Director and Manager with adjusting staff to volumes.
  • Motivates and mentors team members to maintain a positive work environment. Creates and implements goals, action plans, and incentives to drive production results.
  • Performs call monitoring, coaching, training, and feedback and disciplining. Coaches, counsels and motivates employees.
  • Serves as a role model for staff in maintaining effective communication. This includes communication with employees, patients, guests, insurance companies, employers, doctors, and hospital personnel.
  • Acts as an information source to ensure resolution of customer inquiries and complaints. Handles escalations on an as needed basis.
  • Administers and handles escalation requests for system and Revenue Cycle policies. These include Cash Handling, Financial Assistance, Point of Service, Out of Network, Limited Plan, and Outpatient Valid Orders.
  • Participates in the hiring process and manages performance, recognition, and disciplinary actions. Assists with interviewing applicants, hiring, and performance reviews.

Key Success Factors

  • Requires knowledge of general insurance terms, including governmental and commercial payers. Requires basic knowledge of medical and coding terms.
  • Proficient typing and keyboarding skills. Basic computer skills and Microsoft Office.
  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously.
  • Proven written and verbal communication skills.
  • Works unsupervised and self-starter.
  • Proven ability to problem-solve, perform critical thinking.
  • Requires excellent listening and communication skills, and professional telephone etiquette.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor in stressful and emotional environments. This includes crime, behavioral health, suffering patients, and life or death situations.

title: Cargiver
description:
Mentor Community Services, a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.


SUMMARY

  • Position Type: Non-exempt, full-time or part-time, hourly role.
  • Scope of Role:
    • Responsible for providing direct support within a single program or unit within a program, typically supporting 4 - 6 individuals in residential settings, or up to 10 individuals in periodic programs.
  • Key Responsibilities:
    • Deliver support per individual service/program plans, including socialization, health maintenance, medication administration, skill/behavioral development.
    • Assist with daily activities: Personal care, housekeeping, recreational activities, transportation, community integration, shopping, citizenship, and other activities of daily living.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.

Services and Supports:

  1. Direct Support: Provides direct support or assistance in accordance with individual service or program plans; assists with socialization and behavioral development, personal care, housekeeping, recreational activities, transportation, community orientation, shopping, financial management, citizenship, and other activities of daily living.
  2. Records: Accurately documents progress and activity; reviews records and logs to stay abreast of changes in service plans; maintains confidentiality.
  3. Management of Individuals’ Assets: Makes cost-effective and appropriate purchases within the budget of the individual served and according to their choice / preference
  4. Relationships: Maintains healthy and professional relationships with individuals, friends, families, guardians and case managers; greets family members and other visitors; implements Sevita Customer Service Standards.
  5. Reporting: Reports any instance of alleged abuse or neglect according to internal and external standards; reports medical, behavioral and other incidents in accordance with Sevita policy and external requirements.
  6. Rights: Maintains confidentiality, respects the rights of persons being served, according to applicable the bill of rights; practices universal precautions; assists individuals in exercising their rights.

Health Care:

  1. Appointments: As needed, may accompany individuals to medical appointments; relays orders and information to and from medical providers as required.
  2. Medications: If assigned, accurately administers or supports self-administration of medication and documents delivery of medications and treatments; promptly reports administration errors; maintains appropriate security of controlled medications and other medications and supplies.
  3. General Health Care: Monitors individual’s health; documents health concerns; communicates with nurse or supervisor as appropriate; calls 911 in the event of emergency; follows individual health care directives.
  4. Medical Supplies and Equipment: Correctly follows procedures in utilizing medical equipment; reports malfunction or disrepair.
  5. Meal Preparation: Prepares or supports individuals to prepare food in accordance with planned menus and individual choice; knows special diets and prepares individual meals accordingly; monitors mealtime and correctly implements any dining plans.

Employment Responsibilities:

  1. Training: Attends orientation and on-going training as directed; participates in monthly staff meetings.
  2. Employee Scheduling: Works scheduled hours; arrives for work on time; stays on shift until replacement arrives; notifies supervisor in advance when unable to work as scheduled or as soon as possible after the designated start time; may fill in for other shifts where required without causing unapproved overtime, or in the event of emergency.
  3. Teamwork: Works together with others, values others contributions; is courteous; communicates openly; listens; and shows respect to others.
  4. Workplace Safety: Every employee plays a role in developing and maintaining a safe workplace; complies with all established safety policies, procedures, and rules; reports unsafe hazards to their supervisor and participates in safety related training or activities.

Maintenance:

  1. Vehicles: May transport individuals into the community; drives safely and according to local laws; ensures proper use of safety equipment including seat belts, lifts and wheelchair ties; reports accidents to appropriate authorities immediately; reports accidents and safety concerns immediately to supervisor or maintenance personnel.
  2. Housekeeping: Performs daily and seasonal housekeeping as directed; maintains neat, clean and safe environment; reports hazards or safety concerns.
  3. Maintenance and Repair: Monitors environmental safety and may make minor repairs, change light bulbs, etc.; may perform yard maintenance including keeping walkways safe and snow removal; reports equipment or facilities requiring repairs to supervisor or maintenance personnel as required.
  4. Safety: Checks water temperature as required when assisting with bathing; participates in safety drills and protects persons being served in the event of emergency.

Other:

  • Performs other duties and activities as required.
  • MPA = Mobile Punch Authorized for timekeeping.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • None

Minimum Knowledge and Skills required for the Job

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job.

Education and Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred
  • Six months of experience in human services preferred.
  • Must be 18 years of age.
  • Working knowledge of computers

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:

  • Valid driver’s license in good standing.
  • Car registration and vehicle insurance if providing transportation for individuals receiving services.
  • All state-required training(s) and certification(s) completed in mandated timeframes.
  • Maintain valid driver’s license, meet all insurance requirements, and be approved by management to be a driver for the company. If an employee is determined to have lost their driving privileges by failing the company MVR driving record requirements per company policy, the employee will be required to sign a Non-Driver form and restricted from driving on behalf of the company until their MVR report satisfies the company requirements for a good driving record.

Work Environment:

  • Works at the program location and may accompany individuals into the community.

Physical Requirements:

  • Heavy Work. Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 50 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

Addendum:

    • Employees must cooperate with the licensee and Department of Human Services staff in any inspection, inquiry, or investigation.
    • Must have a valid driver’s license in good standing in The State of New Jersey; however, in the event the person lives in another state and is commuting, they must have a valid driver’s license in good standing for the state in which they live.
    • At minimum, a High School Diploma/Equivalent is required
    • All employees hired after 6/15/2018 shall submit to drug testing prior to employment. All employees shall submit to drug testing randomly and for cause/suspicion.
    • Employees must submit to criminal background checks, and be determined not to be disqualified by the Department of Human Services prior to working with individuals served. In addition to this, it is a requirement that all employees agree to have their name checked against the Central Registry of Offenders Against Individuals with Developmental Disabilities, as well as completing an application to have their name checked against the Child Abuse Registry Information (CARI).

title: Senior Advisor - Medical Affairs – Oncology & Hematology, Türkiye
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Job Summary


The Senior Advisor – Medical Affairs is an integral member of the Oncology/Hematology medical team and the cross-functional brand team. Through the application of scientific and clinical expertise, the role provides medical leadership to support launch and commercialization activities, local clinical research and scientific exchange, with the aim of meeting patients’ needs and enhancing the customer experience. Customers include patients, healthcare professionals (HCPs) and payers.


The role is open to both physicians (Clinical Research Physician, CRP) and pharmacists (Clinical Research Scientist, CRS). All activities are conducted in compliance with local and international regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCP) and Lilly policies and procedures.


Job Responsibilities


Brand Team & Launch Support

  • Serve as a key medical point of contact for the brand team and contribute clinical, scientific and strategic input to the cross-functional team.
  • Provide medical leadership for launch readiness and launch execution of new products and indications.
  • Develop and/or contribute to the local medical plan and strategy, aligned with global and regional priorities.
  • Contribute to the development and review of promotional and medical materials.
  • Support the medical training needs of internal partners such as sales and marketing.
  • Provide clinical input to pricing, reimbursement and access (PRA) activities and patient support programs.

Customer Engagement & Scientific Exchange

  • Respond to unsolicited requests for medical information from HCPs in line with company requirements.
  • Build and maintain relationships with thought leaders, scientific experts and relevant professional societies.
  • Plan and implement advisory boards, symposia, scientific exchange and educational meetings.
  • Deliver scientific and educational presentations internally and to customers, and provide congress support.
  • Gather and share scientific insights from customer interactions to inform Lilly’s strategy.

Clinical Research & Regulatory Support

  • Support the planning, start-up, conduct and reporting of local and global clinical trials (Phase 3b/4, and Phase I–II where applicable).
  • Serve as a scientific resource to study teams, investigators and ethics committees; support investigator selection and review IIT proposals.
  • Monitor patient safety and ensure appropriate follow-up of adverse events in line with corporate patient safety procedures.
  • Contribute to local labeling, regulatory submissions and risk management planning.
  • Support data analysis and the development of slide sets and publications (abstracts, posters, manuscripts).

Scientific Expertise

  • Keep up to date with medical and scientific developments, the competitive landscape and clinical practice trends in Oncology/Hematology.
  • Partner with other medical affairs roles to deliver a seamless and exceptional customer experience.


Job Qualifications


Education

  • Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree

Experience


Required

  • Minimum 3 years of pharmaceutical industry experience in an international company

Preferred

  • Oncology experience
  • Launch experience

Competencies

  • Strong communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to translate scientific data into clear and compliant content for customers
  • Ability to partner and influence across multiple functions
  • Strong planning, organization and project management skills
  • Business acumen and ability to balance scientific and business priorities

Other Qualifications

  • Fluent in English, verbal and written
  • Domestic and international travel required
  • May require evening/weekend work

description:

  • Key Responsibilities:

Hires Program Directors in consultation with the Regional Director and Talent Acquisition teams. Consults with the Program Director and Talent Acquisition teams on hiring Program Supervisors.

  2. Individuals’ Served Funds Management: Safeguards individuals' served funds and ensures compliance within area; verifies monthly financial ledgers for completeness and itemized receipts for purchases on behalf of individuals served.

Census Management:

  1. Marketing: Identifies collateral, social media, virtual tours, and other marketing needs within area and escalates to Regional Directors.

Health and Safety Management:

  1. Health and Safety Programs: Oversees development and implementation of area health and safety programs for individuals and employees; and supervises area nurses as applicable.
  2. Environment: Maintains area compliance with Sevita and regulatory standards for clean, neat, safe living and working environments; and assures pleasant, age-appropriate, well- decorated home-like residential living environments; and directs area maintenance.

Other:

  • Performs other duties and activities as required, including backfilling roles under your supervision.

Makes decisions on employee transfers, promotions, salary changes, discipline, terminations, and similar actions. Resolves employee problems within position responsibilities.
