description:
BSW Austin Oak Hill Medical Center Multimodality Tech

PRN: Sat-Mon Mid-shift or Overnights

About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.

Job Summary

The Multimodality Technologist is supervised by a Radiologist, performs imaging in two or more disciplines. At least 25% of their work focuses on advanced areas like CT, MR, Nuc Med, or IR. They work with ambulatory and hospital patients as requested by a physician or licensed provider for diagnosing disease and injury, following established protocols.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Performs high-quality multimodality procedures according to exam protocol promptly. Maintains production and quality of imaging procedures by following established standards.
  • Demonstrates an expertise of radiation dose reference levels and monitoring. Takes action if the estimated dose exceeds set levels. Takes action when the reference level is exceeded, which may include patient follow-up.
  • Demonstrates and knows about proper use of iSTAT point of care testing for obtaining creatinine levels.
  • Utilizes AIDET to communicate with patients. Identifies patient service needs and ensures the correct exam is performed on the correct patient. Establishes rapport with patients and others. Communicates clearly and calmly with patients and their families about the test. Assesses the patient's ability to tolerate the exam.
  • Prepare the patient and area for the procedure. Position the patient, use immobilization devices, and move equipment into position. Use appropriate settings and exposure factors.
  • Protects patients and employees by following safety, infection-control, drug, and radiation policies. Uses sterile techniques for invasive procedures and maintains hand hygiene.
  • Maintains equipment and work area to meet quality and cleanliness standards. Works with engineers and physicists to ensure optimal equipment operation. Reports issues to management or the appropriate department. Assists in maintaining the supplies inventory. Ensures people are safe to enter the department by screening them according to approved policies and procedures.
  • Obtains, verifies, and maintains all relevant documentation such as requisition/chart, patient history, pregnancy status, policies, and procedures, etc.
  • Maintains medical imaging records in appropriate systems, according to department policies and procedures.

Key Success Factors

  • Able to perform high-quality multimodality procedures according to exam protocol in a timely manner.
  • Able to explain the procedure and put patients at ease.
  • Able to provide services timely, accurately, and cost-efficient in compliance with established System and regulatory standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Able to perform tasks autonomously without need for routine oversight.
  • Able to stay calm and helpful during stress. Take reasonable steps to resolve issues.
  • Able to effectively administer first aid and use emergency cart.
  • Ensure customer satisfaction by limiting wait times and providing courteous service. Remain professional, review patient satisfaction scores, and develop action plans when needed.
  • Demonstrates and maintains current knowledge, continued education, and skills appropriate care for all age groups.
  • Able to serve as a preceptor by providing quality training to new team members. Also, train current teams about new services and initiatives.
  • Able to take call, if required.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • EDUCATION - Graduate of an Accredited Program
  • EXPERIENCE - Less than 1 year of Experience

CERTIFICATION/LICENSE/REGISTRATION

  • Basic Life Support (BLS): BLS within 30 days of hire or transfer.
  • Medical Radiologic Tech (MRT): Licensed by the State of Texas Medical Board as a Medical Radiologic Technologist (MRT), unless the role is MRI or Ultrasound.
  • American Reg MRI Tech (ARMRIT), ARRT-Bone Density (ARRT-BD), ARRT-BS Breast Sonography (ARRT-BS), ARRT-CT Computed Tomography (ARRT-CT), ARRT-M Mammography (ARRT-M), ARRT-MR Magnetic Res Imaging (ARRT-MR), ARRT-N Nuclear Medicine Tech (ARRT-N), ARRT-R Radiography (ARRT-R), ARRT-S Sonography (ARRT-S), ARRT-VI Interventional Rad (ARRT-VI), Cert Nuclear Med Tech (CNMT), Reg Diag Med Sono-Abdomen (AB) (RDMS-AB), Reg Diag Med Sono-Breast (BR) (RDMS-BR), RDMS Fetal Echocardiography (RDMS-FE), Reg Diag Med Sono-OB/GYN (OB) (RDMS-OB), RDMS-Pediatric Sonography (PS) (RDMS-PS), Registered Vascular Tech (RVT): Certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists or the American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonography in two imaging modalities. Works 50% of the time in the second modality. Approved modalities are: ARRT-R, ARRT-CT, ARRT-CV, ARRT-M, ARRT-MR, ARRT-N, ARRT-S, ARRT-VI, ARRT-BS, ARRT-BD, ARRT-CI, RDMS-AB, RDMS-BR, RDMS-FE, RDMS-OB, RDMS-PS, RVT, CNMT, or ARMRIT.
  • ARRT-CI Cardiac-Interventional (ARRT-CI), ARRT-CV Cardiovasc-Inter Rad (ARRT-CV).

title: AVP, Oncology Pharmacology
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Position Summary:


As the Oncology Pharmacology senior leader, you will lead a dynamic group of scientists conducting research to identify medicines that effectively treat various forms of cancer. You will oversee several portfolio projects simultaneously and be responsible for the ultimate delivery of clinical candidates. As part of the portfolio leadership team, you will guide the strategic focus of our Oncology portfolio to balance delivery of medicines with the innovation necessary for next-generation, differentiated products across various modalities, including small and large molecules. As the pharmacology leader, you will integrate cross-functional information to set program priorities, portfolio decisions, and innovation. You will lead a team of project leaders, senior scientists, and junior scientists to ensure efficient program execution and decision making and mentor the next generation of scientific and project leaders. Working with peer leaders and project teams, you will regularly update senior leadership and engage with clinical colleagues to guide target product profile (TPP) alignment and product differentiation to ensure our best medicines advance into clinical development. Collaboration across functional areas within Lilly is required. You will continue to build strong relationships with colleagues in Indianapolis and at other sites including CMC, toxicology, and clinical departments to strengthen collaborations key to our discovery program success. You will be a key member of the Oncology organization, responsible for maintaining its scientific quality and efficiency and helping guide the company’s strategic direction.



Roles and Responsibilities of the Position:

Scientific roles and responsibilities

  • Oversee several teams of scientists who lead individual portfolio programs and actively mentor our next-generation project leaders.
  • Synthesize complex, cross-functional information, including target biology, clinical opportunity, product differentiation, and competitive landscape to support our Oncology strategy and portfolio priorities.
  • Serve as a key member of the Oncology portfolio leadership team, working with peer leaders in New York and South San Francisco to execute our pipeline strategy and advance molecules from early Discovery to IND.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams across Lilly to drive the execution of Oncology programs. For example, work with project teams across functions and sites to provide the expertise, resources, and infrastructure to efficiently progress all Oncology candidates.
  • Integrate newly acquired technologies and scientific teams into our portfolio projects to deliver differentiated, innovative medicines.
  • Oversee the design and execution of key mechanistic and preclinical experiments involving diverse oncogenic mechanisms (e.g., oncogenic signaling pathways, tumor-specific targets, biologic mechanisms of tumor inhibition) across multiple tumor indications.
  • Contribute to business development strategy and recommend novel modalities, targets, and platforms that add value to our existing Oncology portfolio. Contribute to the assessment of external opportunities, formal diligence, and recommendations to leadership.
  • Assemble documents and present at leadership meetings (including Discovery portfolio reviews, Clinical review meetings, and Candidate advancement reviews).
  • Deliver IND sections related to preclinical development as well as supporting preclinical reports.
  • Partner with Translational and Clinical colleagues to define biomarker, patient selection and indication strategy, and to develop PK/PD-based dose projections, so preclinical data packages support first-in-human readiness and the TPP.

Leadership roles and responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, develop, and manage teams of project leaders and scientists
  • Liaise with internal teams and provide guidance on key strategic business decisions
  • Build and execute on roadmaps that deliver on specific targets and overall strategic projects
  • Align with senior leaders around portfolio decisions, priorities, and resources
  • Cross-site leadership: Lead and influence across sites, aligning INDY, NYC and SSF teams on shared priorities and ways of working.
  • Talent development: Develop project leaders and future scientific leaders, and foster an inclusive, high-performing team culture.
  • Support and communicate difficult portfolio decisions, including stopping/prioritizing programs, using data-driven criteria and a transparent rationale.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD in pharmacology, cancer cell biology, or allied disciplines with a minimum of 15 years’ experience (at least 10 years of direct drug development experience)

Additional Preferences:

  • Demonstrated success in developing Oncology medicines across modalities (experience in large molecules including ADCs desired but not required)
  • Experience in IND submission and preclinical data package generation
  • Hands-on, direct drug-hunting experience with a track record of progressing multiple programs to Phase 1
  • Ability to collaborate with translational functions (PK/PD, toxicology, antibody discovery)
  • Deep understanding of drug discovery and development through Phase 1 (or beyond)
  • Proven success leading, managing, and coaching large cross-functional teams in dynamic organizations
  • Demonstrated ability and track record in overseeing work performed by third parties/vendors/strategic partners
  • Demonstrated experience working collaboratively across scientific disciplines to meet business goals
  • Demonstrated business acumen
  • Demonstrated excellence in making key strategic decisions in support of broader business goals
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Physical Demands/Travel: TBD; estimated ~20%

Additional Information: The successful candidate for this position will transfer laterally into the role at their current level. For example, an R9 employee who applies for and is selected for this position, posted as R10, would transfer laterally at the R9 level. level.

Work Environment: You will work in our state-of-the-art laboratories in our Indianapolis headquarters facility.

description:
Description - External

Status: PRN

Shift: 1 Variable Shift per Week

About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401 (k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement

  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

    Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level

Job Summary

The Nuclear Medicine Technologist (NM Tech) performs nuclear medicine, PET, and theranostic procedures. They work under a Radiologist's supervision. These procedures are for ambulatory and hospital patients. A physician or licensed provider requests them for diagnosing disease and injury. They follow established protocols.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Quality Assurance: Performs high-quality nuclear medicine, PET, and theranostic procedures according to exam protocol. Evaluates the quality of imaging procedures and follows established standards. Maintains equipment by performing quality control as required by imaging manufacturers, RAM, or ACR. Works with engineers and physicists to ensure optimal equipment capabilities.
  • Caring Practices: Communicates with patients to identify service needs, ensure the correct exam is performed, and establish rapport with patients and others. Instructs and communicates with patients and their family, following HIPAA, about the test and assesses the patient's ability to tolerate the exam.
  • Patient Safety: Explains the procedure thoroughly to put patients at ease. Protects patients and team members by following safety requirements, infection-control, protocols, and techniques. Prepares patient and area for procedure by positioning patient, adjusting immobilization devices, and moving equipment into position. Uses proper aseptic or sterile techniques when setting up and performing invasive procedures. Maintains hand hygiene requirements.
  • Radiation Safety: Safeguards patients, team members, and themselves by following all radiation safety rules, policies, and techniques. Verifies the correct radioactive drug for the exam or treatment. Screens patients for pregnancy status before the exam or treatment. Safely administers radiopharmaceuticals and medications per protocol. Educates patients on radiation safety techniques before and after the exam or treatment. Safely follows radiation disposal guidelines.
  • Collaboration: Reports issues to leadership or the appropriate department. Assists in maintaining supplies inventory and ordering radiopharmaceuticals for patient care and Q.C. Works with colleagues, nursing partners, medical staff, and Radiologists. Ensures accurate transfer of patient images to the BSWH PACS for clinical review and dictation by physician partners.

Key Success Factors

  • Observe changes in patients' medical conditions and communicate them to nursing partners, physicians, and emergency teams. Administer first aid and use the emergency cart.
  • Demonstrates and maintains current knowledge, education, and skills for caring for these age groups: newborn, pediatric, young adult, adult, and geriatric.
  • Able to provide services timely, accurately, and cost-efficiently in compliance with established system and regulatory standards, policies and procedures.
  • Able to perform tasks autonomously without need for routine oversight.
  • Able to stay calm and helpful during stress. Takes reasonable steps to resolve issues.
  • Ensure customer satisfaction by limiting wait times and providing courteous service. Remain professional, review patient satisfaction scores, and develop action plans when needed.
  • Able to serve as trainer by providing a quality education to new team members and students from BSW approved programs.
  • Adhering to policies, procedures, and workflows. These include PACS, EMR, image exchange systems, modality worklist integrity, record management, and Biomedical services.
  • General computer skills, including Microsoft Office, information security, electronic medical documentation, and email.
  • Able to take call, if required.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued, and supported.

Qualifications - External

QUALIFCIATIONS

CERTIFICATION/LICENSE/REGISTRATION

  • ARRT-N Nuclear Medicine Tech (ARRT-N), Cert Nuclear Med Tech (CNMT): Certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists in Nuclear Medicine - ARRT (N). Certified by the NMTCB (Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board) as a Certified Nuclear Medicine Technologist (CNMT).

QUALIFCIATIONS

CERTIFICATION/LICENSE/REGISTRATION

  • ARRT-N Nuclear Medicine Tech (ARRT-N), Cert Nuclear Med Tech (CNMT): Certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists in Nuclear Medicine - ARRT (N). Certified by the NMTCB (Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board) as a Certified Nuclear Medicine Technologist (CNMT).

title: PRA & Corporate Affairs Lead Baltics
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


PRA & Corporate Affairs Lead – Baltics


Make an impact where science, policy and patient access come together


This is a unique leadership opportunity to shape Pricing, Reimbursement & Access (PRA) and Corporate Affairs across Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia.


In this role, you will shape the external environment to help create sustainable access to innovative medicines. Working at the intersection of healthcare policy, market access, reimbursement, advocacy and business strategy, you will build strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders and translate healthcare-system insights into strategies that support patients and the business.


You will work closely with Baltic leadership and cross-functional teams, as well as colleagues across the broader cluster, regional and global organization.


Pricing, Reimbursement & Access Leadership

You will:

  • Lead, inspire and develop the Baltic PRA team, setting clear strategic direction, priorities and expectations across Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia.
  • Shape and execute pricing, reimbursement and market access strategies that support sustainable patient access and business objectives.
  • Lead reimbursement and pricing processes with national health insurance funds, reimbursement authorities and other relevant stakeholders, including negotiation and re-negotiation strategies.
  • Ensure timely, high-quality and compliant reimbursement applications and pricing submissions through strong cross-functional collaboration.
  • Oversee the development and localization of pharmacoeconomic analyses, including cost-effectiveness, cost-utility and budget impact models.
  • Lead pricing and reimbursement business cases related to changes in maximum or selling prices, partnering with relevant regional and international stakeholders to secure required approvals.
  • Contribute subject-matter expertise through the review of cost-effectiveness modelling outputs and recommendations.
  • Lead the PRA components of annual Customer Plans for key products, ensuring strong connection between access strategy, reimbursement priorities and business objectives.
  • Anticipate changes in the legislative, regulatory and healthcare-policy environment, translating emerging opportunities and risks into clear strategic actions.
  • Establish strong governance to ensure compliance with local legislation, industry standards and company policies.

Corporate Affairs & External Engagement

You will:

  • Define and drive the Corporate Affairs strategy for the Baltics, aligned with business priorities, patient access objectives and the evolving external environment.
  • Build trusted, strategic relationships with government officials, healthcare policymakers, healthcare budget holders, patient organizations and other influential external stakeholders.
  • Lead environment-shaping and advocacy initiatives designed to advance healthcare-system priorities and improve patient access.
  • Build and mobilize external coalitions and stakeholder networks, including multi-stakeholder alliances, parliamentary groups, patient advocacy partnerships and relevant scientific organizations.
  • Identify opportunities for meaningful collaboration with patient organizations, scientific associations, professional societies and other influence groups.
  • Partner with Medical on relevant scientific and expert engagements, including Advisory Boards, and strengthen meaningful engagement with patients and patient organizations.
  • Translate company, therapeutic-area, PRA and business priorities into compelling healthcare policy and advocacy strategies.
  • Ensure commercial and launch plans are supported by robust Corporate Affairs strategies and tactics linked to access and business objectives.
  • Develop and execute external communication strategies with relevant partners to enhance awareness of the company’s scientific contribution, innovation and impact on patient care, in full compliance with applicable requirements.
  • Strategically leverage participation in trade and industry associations across the Baltic states.
  • Collaborate closely across the Baltic organization and the broader cluster to ensure strong alignment between PRA, Corporate Affairs, Medical and Commercial strategies.

What will help you succeed

We are looking for someone who combines strategic thinking with the ability to turn strategy into action. You will thrive in this role if you can navigate complex healthcare systems, build credibility with senior external stakeholders and bring different perspectives together around a common goal.

You are likely to bring:

  • Strong experience in market access, pricing and reimbursement, health policy, government affairs or Corporate Affairs within healthcare or the pharmaceutical industry.
  • Solid understanding of reimbursement processes, healthcare systems and the external policy environment.

title: Senior Advisor, Separation Science — Analytical Development
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Position Summary

We are seeking an accomplished Senior Advisor, Separation Sciences to provide scientific leadership for analytical development (AD) supporting next-generation mRNA-LNP-based in vivo CAR-T therapies within the Advanced Delivery Systems (ADS) organization. This individual will lead all chemistry assay effort, spanning multiple separation platforms, and serve as the technical SME for characterization and stability testing of the mRNA, protein, and lipid components of LNP-based drug substance/product.


The successful candidate will combine deep, hands-on separations expertise with strategic leadership, partnering closely with Lilly Genetic Medicines, Process and Formulation, Cell and Gene Therapy, and Quality teams to drive phase-appropriate analytical strategies and assay execution. The successful candidate will be self-motivated, independent, have hands-on bench skills, and able to lead and develop other scientist.


Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the technical lead and group leader for the separation science function within Analytical Development, defining and executing chemistry assay strategy and roadmap for RNA-LNP-based programs.
  • Lead end-to-end development, optimization, pre-qualification, and technical transfer of chemistry assays across separation platforms (e.g., IP-UPLC, RP-UPLC, CGE, LC-MS, SEC, SEC-MALS, IEX) to characterize and quantify mRNA, protein, and lipid components of drug product.
  • Represent the separation science function on cross-functional project teams and in technical review settings, and act as the primary analytical SME.
  • Ensure assay data, methods, and practices comply with ICH guidelines and industry best practices for cell and gene therapies.
  • Design, develop, and execute stability-indicating methods and forced-degradation studies to support product characterization, shelf-life determination, and ongoing stability programs.
  • Establish assay comparability and bridging strategies across process/formulation changes, scale-up, and method transfers; apply sound statistical design (e.g., DOE) to reduce variability and improve assay robustness.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure integrated, phase-appropriate analytical strategies, define CQAs, and assess assay suitability and readiness for the transition from research through development to manufacturing.
  • Manage external collaborations to enhance internal capabilities and drive analytical innovation.
  • Evaluate and implement innovative separation science technologies and platforms to address emerging scientific and regulatory challenges.
  • Author and review assay protocols, technical reports, and relevant sections of regulatory submissions.

Basic Qualifications

  • PhD or MS in chemistry, biochemistry, or a related scientific discipline with 4+ years (PhD) or 10+ years (MS) of industry experience in separation science/chemistry assay development.
  • Extensive, hands-on experience developing, optimizing, qualifying, and validating chemistry assays across multiple separation platforms (e.g., IP-UPLC, RP-UPLC, CGE, LC-MS, SEC, SEC-MALS, IEX).
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience characterizing mRNA, protein, and/or lipid components using these platforms.
  • Knowledge of ICH/FDA guidelines and industry best practices related to analytical methods for cell and gene therapies.
  • Proven experience defining and executing phase-appropriate assay strategies, including stability program design and method transfer.

Additional Skills and Preferences

  • Prior experience characterizing RNA-LNP based genetic medicines, process- and product-related impurities.
  • Experience with LC-MS-based characterization of proteins, lipids, and/or oligonucleotides.
  • Experience authoring regulatory submission sections and supporting health authority interactions.
  • Strong critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills, with an ability to influence scientific direction and deliver in a matrixed, fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to manage external collaborations and deliver quality results within a stringent timeline.

title: Advisor - Analytical Chemistry
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Organization Overview:

The Synthetic Molecule Design and Development (SMDD) organization is responsible for the development of synthetic drug substances and drug products from the pre-clinical phase through commercialization. Our scientists and engineers develop innovative technical solutions to advance an exciting portfolio that includes small molecules, peptides, oligonucleotides, and other emerging therapeutic modalities spanning oncology, immunology, neuroscience, and metabolic diseases. By cultivating a hardworking, culturally diverse workforce that exhibits deep technical expertise, SMDD delivers on these responsibilities and helps bring the next generation of life-changing medicines to patients. This is an exceptional time to join SMDD and help shape the future of pharmaceutical development.

About This Opportunity:

SMDD has an exciting opportunity for an Advisor, Analytical Chemistry to join our collaborative team as an individual contributor in a primarily laboratory-based role. This position uniquely positions you at the forefront of pharmaceutical innovation, working hands-on across multiple cutting-edge modalities (oligonucleotides, peptides, and small molecules) while directly impacting patient lives through medicines that advance from bench to bedside.

As a lab-based scientist empowered by access to state-of-the-art analytical platforms, structured mentorship programs, and extensive pharmaceutical development experience spanning the entire drug lifecycle, you will conduct hands-on experimental work while shaping analytical strategies for some of the most promising therapeutic advances in the industry. SMDD scientists gain versatile technical expertise highly valued throughout pharmaceutical development—experience that accelerates career growth and opens doors to senior scientist roles and technical leadership opportunities. Our collaborative team values diverse perspectives, supports work-life integration, and celebrates both scientific rigor and creative problem-solving.

Position Responsibilities:

As an individual contributor, analytical scientists in SMDD enable the comprehensive characterization of materials and processes necessary to ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of Lilly's medicines through direct laboratory work. This responsibility requires hands-on contribution to the development of analytical methodology, execution of experiments to generate key data, and support of regulatory documents (e.g., IND, NDA).

Scientists in this position are expected to:

  • Perform hands-on laboratory work to support the design, development, and implementation of product control strategies for oligonucleotide, peptide, and/or small molecule programs, directly enabling clinical milestones and regulatory submissions.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in multiple analytical technologies through daily laboratory work, with an emphasis on chromatography and mass spectrometry. Operate cutting-edge instrumentation and apply emerging analytical techniques.
  • Execute analytical method development, generate data to justify specifications, conduct stability studies, perform starting material testing for synthetic processes, identify and characterize impurities, and test drug product performance characteristics (e.g., dissolution/disintegration).
  • Conduct hands-on laboratory research to support internal process development in a fast-paced environment. This includes experimental design, sample preparation and analysis, instrument operation and troubleshooting, and data interpretation.
  • Provide technical input for analytical activities executed within the external network. Review methods to ensure they are technically sound, well developed, and fit for purpose. Support technology transfer to CRO/CMO organizations and Lilly manufacturing sites.
  • Identify and implement innovative laboratory solutions to development challenges, monitor emerging trends in analytical chemistry, and maintain familiarity with applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills; effectively convey technical results and implications of laboratory data; collaborate with development partners across regulatory, clinical, and manufacturing functions; contribute to internal technical reports and regulatory submission documents.
  • With experience, provide informal mentorship to junior scientists and contribute technical expertise to cross-functional project teams while maintaining focus on individual contributor laboratory responsibilities.

Basic Qualifications

  • PhD in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or closely related STEM discipline
  • Master’s degree in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or closely related STEM discipline with at least 8 years of pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical development experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or closely related STEM discipline with at least 12 years of pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical development experience

Additional Skills/Preferences

  • Experience across multiple analytical techniques (e.g., HPLC, mass spectrometry, NMR, etc.) and demonstration of strong hands-on laboratory skills and technical problem-solving abilities.
  • PhD Candidates with >2 years of post-PhD hands-on laboratory experience in pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical development or closely related analytical chemistry roles.
  • Experienced candidates should demonstrate a track record of hands-on laboratory contributions to pharmaceutical development projects, including support of regulatory submissions (IND/NDA), method development and validation, and analytical testing strategies.
  • Previous hands-on laboratory experience in the pharmaceutical industry or with analytical techniques directly applicable to pharmaceutical development (e.g., HPLC, MS).
  • Deep fundamental understanding of and hands-on experience with reversed-phase, ion exchange, size-exclusion, chiral, and/or gas chromatography.
  • Working knowledge and practical laboratory experience with optical spectroscopy (e.g., Raman, FTIR), NMR, structure elucidation, and powder characterization techniques (e.g., XRPD, particle size distribution).
  • Strong hands-on technical skills, learning agility, ability to prioritize laboratory workload, and aptitude in navigating experimental challenges.
  • Motivated to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic laboratory environment.
  • Passion for applying analytical chemistry through hands-on laboratory work to solve real-world pharmaceutical development challenges and improve patient outcomes.

Additional Information

  • Laboratory-based position with daily hands-on experimental work
  • Possible exposure to chemicals, allergens, and loud noises
  • Occasional travel (0 to 10%)
  • Position Location: Indianapolis, IN Lilly Technology Center - North (LTC-N)

title: Clinical Liaison
description:
About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.

Job Summary

The Clinical Liaison builds relationships with current and potential referral sources. The liaison evaluates patients for post-acute care services. The liaison performs pre-admission assessments to establish if patients qualify for the inpatient rehabilitation center. The liaison collaborates with physician and nurse managers to ensure compliance with Medicare guidelines. Proper documentation is maintained both on pre-admission and throughout the patient's rehab stay.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Completes preadmission assessments timely, thoroughly, and with sufficient detail to justify a rehab admission.
  • Coordinates admission process with referral source, patient/family and rehab team through effective communication and documentation.
  • Educates potential patients and families, as well as referral sources on inpatient rehabilitation and the benefits of the program.
  • Develops and maintains positive business relationships with key referral sources.
  • Develops and implements strategies to grow market share in the core business line in the assigned hospital.
  • Promotes BSW services and programs to the external community. Is available to assist with health fairs and educational programs as needed.
  • Works closely with service line leadership and Clinical Liaisons. Promotes rehab services by participating in educational programs, meet and greets, and interdisciplinary meetings in hospitals or other care levels.
  • Ensures compliance with Medicare guidelines and proper IRF documentation both on pre-admission and throughout the patient's rehab stay.
  • Understanding of the IRF-PAI (Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility-Patient Assessment Instrument).
  • Provides exceptional customer service by ensuring patient referrals are managed and completed in a timely manner.

Key Success Factors

  • Knowledge of care management and resource utilization management.

title: Advisor - Project Planning & Scheduling
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Role Summary

The Advisor - Project Planning & Scheduling serves as GFD's enterprise process owner for planning and scheduling across the global capital portfolio. The role is accountable for establishing, governing, and continuously improving standards, methodologies, systems, and performance measures that support schedule development, forecasting, and execution throughout the project lifecycle. Through technical leadership, governance, and assurance, the role ensures consistent application of planning and scheduling requirements across projects, contractors, and business partners while improving schedule quality, predictability, compliance, and project delivery outcomes.


Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as GFD's enterprise process owner for planning and scheduling, establishing standards, governance requirements, methodologies, and performance expectations across the capital portfolio.
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise planning and scheduling standards, procedures, work instructions, templates, and assurance frameworks.
  • Establish scheduling requirements for all phases of project delivery, including project development, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, qualification and validation (CQV), startup, operational readiness, and operational handover.
  • Define and govern schedule quality requirements, including schedule development, logic integrity, critical path methodology, progress measurement, forecasting, schedule risk analysis, and schedule performance management.
  • Lead planning and scheduling assurance activities across the portfolio to verify compliance with enterprise standards and drive corrective actions where deficiencies are identified.
  • Establish planning and scheduling requirements for contractors, consultants, and delivery partners and ensure consistent implementation across projects and regions.
  • Serve as GFD's senior technical SME for schedule recovery, acceleration planning, scenario analysis, forecasting, and schedule risk mitigation.
  • Govern enterprise KPIs and performance measures related to schedule quality, forecasting accuracy, schedule predictability, and project delivery performance.
  • Partner with project teams, contractors, and business partners to improve scheduling capability, strengthen project execution strategies, and promote adoption of best practices.
  • Build organizational capability through training, mentoring, communities of practice, and continuous improvement initiatives that advance planning and scheduling excellence across the portfolio.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Business, Supply Chain, or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in planning and scheduling for large, complex capital projects, including development, governance, and assurance of integrated schedules, application of critical path methodology, forecasting, schedule risk analysis, and establishment of enterprise scheduling standards and best practices.
  • Proficiency with Primavera P6
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 25%.
  • Position is based in Indianapolis, Indiana.
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Professional certification from AACE International, PMI, CMAA, or a similar professional organization.
  • Experience serving as a planning and scheduling lead, center-of-excellence lead, or process owner supporting large capital project portfolios.
  • Experience supporting integrated project delivery across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, qualification and validation (CQV), startup, operational readiness, and operational handover.
  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, or other complex industrial capital programs, including contractor scheduling governance and assurance.
  • Proficiency with enterprise planning, scheduling, project controls, and project information management systems, including application of integrated master scheduling, schedule assurance, schedule recovery, scenario analysis, KPI management, and portfolio performance reporting.

The Multimodality Technologist, supervised by a Radiologist, performs imaging in two or more disciplines. At least 25% of their work focuses on advanced areas like CT, MR, Nuc Med, or IR. They work with ambulatory and hospital patients as requested by a physician or licensed provider for diagnosing disease and injury, following established protocols.

Essential Functions of the Role

Reports issues to management or the appropriate department. Assists in maintaining the supplies inventory. Ensures people are safe to enter the department by screening them according to approved policies and procedures.

description:

This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


At Lilly, we believe in the talent of our workforce. One of the best ways to utilize and develop that talent is to use our existing workforce to fill new and/or open positions. If you are looking for a new position within Lilly, you can view and apply to open roles posted in the internal job posting system. You must meet the minimum qualifications outlined in the job description and have/obtain work authorization in the country the position is located in order to be considered. When applying internally for a position, your current supervisor will receive notification that you have applied to the position. Path/Level:

P1-P3


Note: Roles are posted at the lowest level of a band, however, employees should search across all levels of the band to identify all opportunities. Employees hired on banded positions (ex: P1-P3, R1-R2, B1-B3, etc.) transfer at their current level, despite the level indicated on the job posting. For example, if a P2 candidate is selected for a P1-P3 banded position, the candidate will remain a P2 in the new role.


Position Overview:

The Consumer Services Hub (CSH) is a center of excellence for US patient services and customer support. Our responsibilities include the design and execution of industry-leading, multi-channel customer support solutions and services that enable better patient outcomes and help Lilly achieve business objectives. Members of CSH should deeply understand customer needs and the healthcare ecosystem, and all are expected to contribute to our purpose of connecting people to Lilly products and solutions. Together, we are accountable for an end-to-end support ecosystem of solutions that minimize abandonment, increase adherence and persistency, and deliver industry-best customer experiences.


The Consumer Capabilities Analyst is responsible for translating business needs into effective capabilities that advance the organization’s consumer priorities. The role builds practical expertise in assigned capabilities by drafting and refining requirements, developing and executing test scenarios, and socializing change. Through this work, the role helps improve patient outcomes, strengthen end-user experiences, enhance execution quality, and increase efficiency across supported platforms and capabilities.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the business subject matter expert (BSME) for assigned capabilities, bringing day-to-day process knowledge and utilization expertise to technology and operations teams.
  • Groom and draft business requirements that translate a business problem into clear, testable statements that can be approved without extensive follow-up.
  • Translate complex business and technical concepts between stakeholders, ensuring requirements are understood clearly enough on both sides that what gets built meets the actual business need without compromising quality or compliance standards
  • Build test scenarios and support the coordination and execution of user acceptance testing, documenting results for formal acceptance.
  • Support change management activities tied to capability enhancements, helping end users adopt new functionality.
  • Execute ongoing monitoring and measurement of capability performance, surfacing trends and issues.
  • Support Capability Leads in preparing documentation for governance, change control, and quality and validation activities.
  • Maintain a working understanding of the data an assigned capability creates and depends on, escalating data quality or integrity concerns to the Capability Lead.
  • Support Capability Leads' response to audit and inspection questions by providing operational context and evidence for assigned capabilities.
  • Apply established capability expertise and process fluency when moving into new domains as business priorities evolve.

Partnership, Leading Through Influence, and Flexibility:

  • Partner closely with the Capability Leads, Technical Leads, and business stakeholders to keep requirements, testing, and change activities moving.
  • Facilitate alignment among business and technology stakeholders by clarifying decisions, constraints, dependencies, and next steps throughout delivery.
  • Coordinate with team members supporting other capability domains when work intersects, keeping handoffs clean and issues from stalling between teams.
  • Approach new capability assignments with curiosity and learning agility, building relationships with new stakeholders as oversight shifts.
  • Foster a collaborative, safe-to-speak working environment consistent with Lilly Values and applicable Quality, Legal, Ethics and Compliance, and Privacy requirements.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree required;
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.

  • A degree in Business, Information Systems, Product Management, Healthcare Administration, or similar. A concentration in product management, innovation, customer experience management, or technology management within a Business or related degree also applies.
  • Experience gathering, drafting, or testing business requirements within an enterprise platform or shared capability, such as Customer Relationship Management platforms (CRM), case management, master data management, or digital engagement tools
  • Experience in Pharma, Healthcare, or other highly regulated environment
  • Familiarity with requirements gathering and business analysis techniques, such as those in the BABOK model or similar (IIBA, ISO, etc.)
  • Familiarity with process modeling and diagramming techniques, such as BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation), swimlane diagrams, and as-is/to-be flowcharts, to visually capture current and future state workflows
  • Experience building and executing test scripts or supporting user acceptance testing
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex process detail for business and technical audiences alike
  • Experience operating in a matrixed environment, coordinating across teams or functions without direct supervisory authority
  • High learning agility to navigate changing capability assignments over time

Full Time

10p-8a Tuesday, Friday with 8p-8a every other weekend, following week is 10p-8a Wednesday,Thursday

title: Associate Designer, Outlet
description:
Associate Designer, Outlet

About us:

vineyard vines is a highly successful, privately held, American clothing and accessory retailer founded in 1998 on Martha’s Vineyard by brothers, Shep & Ian Murray. With Shep & Ian still at the helm today, vineyard vines has experienced exponential year over year growth and now operates over 120 retail locations including an outlet division, a successful e-commerce business, domestic distribution center, and expanding corporate headquarters. In addition, vineyard vines is carried in major department stores such as Nordstrom and Bloomingdales as well as numerous specialty boutiques across the US.

vineyard vines was founded on a state of mind that Every day should feel this good.

You don’t need to be on a beach, by the ocean or on vacation to have Every day should feel this good moments. It’s a state of mind that we all experience, and one where everyone is invited. At vineyard vines, we don’t just live an #EDSFTG life away from our desks—we bring it to work with us, too.

In our stores, at our Harbor Drive headquarters or working remotely, our company culture is fun, encouraging and welcoming to all. We work hard and play harder, and we never take ourselves too seriously. And while we have many company goals, our number one priority is making vineyard vines a great place to work for all employees.

Our team is our family, and we’d never have grown to where we are today without them.

We’re committed to building an inclusive team across all channels, departments and stores within our community. We hope you’ll join us and see what the smiling pink whale is all about.

Overview:

The Associate Designer, Outlet, is responsible for the design and development of seasonal apparel collections that align with the vineyard vines brand and the unique needs of the Outlet business. This role focuses on translating seasonal concepts into innovative, brand-appropriate products while collaborating with cross-functional teams to bring collections to life. The Associate Designer will play a key role in executing seasonal line plans, leading the creation of original artwork, and ensuring timely product development. This includes maintaining design consistency, adapting to shifting consumer preferences, and delivering products that resonate with the target customer.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the development of seasonal product concepts, ensuring they align with brand identity and consumer trends.
  • Create, update, and present concept boards that reflect seasonal direction, color palettes, and styling.
  • Execute seasonal line plans and ensure alignment with the product development calendar.
  • Design and develop innovative seasonal apparel, collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive execution from concept to final product.
  • Play a key role in product creation through original artwork and layout development under the Senior Designer.
  • Organize and maintain seasonal design books, fabric swatches, and trim books.
  • Assist in all aspects of daily follow-up with external and internal partners.
  • Create flat sketches and renderings using Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.
  • Develop and maintain BOMs in Centric PLM.
  • Attend all proto and bi-weekly fittings to ensure design intent is maintained.
  • Participate in trend shopping, fabric shows, and group meetings to stay ahead of market trends and innovations.
  • Work closely with Product Development and Merchandising teams to identify and resolve production challenges, ensuring smooth execution of seasonal collections.

What You Bring:

  • Degree in Fashion Design
  • At least 3 years of Design experience
  • Proficient in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop
  • Strong understanding of the apparel design process from concept to product
  • Self-Starter and creative thinker with ability to interpret seasonal concept
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills
  • Ability to work in a fast paced, rapidly changing environment
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills with an ability to work under tight timelines while managing multiple priorities
  • Must be willing to commute to Stamford, CT Headquarters

Every day will feel this good because:

  • We have a fun-spirited entrepreneurial culture filled with truly “good” people
  • We have flexible working hours and work from home days to accommodate your personal life
  • We offer a generous employee discount so you can rep our lifestyle on-and-off the boat
  • We offer a competitive salary package, 401-K, commuter benefits, and paid-family leave, health savings , flex spending accounts, life & disability insurance
  • We have an onsite gym as well as health & financial wellness programs to keep you active
  • We offer 2 summer Fridays to take off in addition to a competitive vacation policy & holiday calendar

title: Quality Improvement Consultant 1 - Maternal Program / OB Services
description:
About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.

Job Summary

Provides consultant expertise and leadership to teams for better outcomes. Supports BSWH strategy to deliver high-quality, safe care. Achieves excellence by following regulatory statutes, policies, and procedures.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Serves as an internal consultant for quality and patient safety initiatives and small to medium scale projects through BSWH.
  • Facilitates, coordinates, and manages projects for quality improvement teams, strategic planning sessions, and other meetings and committees as needed.
  • Coaches and mentors teams and managers in the provision of quality, patient safety and other regulatory issues.
  • In partnership with teams and managers, develops indicators and finds improvement opportunities. Monitors and evaluates care quality based on evidence, regulations, and data testing.
  • Identifies regional, system, and industry best practices, providing feedback to managers and team members.
  • Provides subject matter expertise and comprehensive measurement testing for quality improvement initiatives across the organization.
  • Prepares and submits timely reports on work team progress to stakeholders. These reports include progress, potential barriers, lessons learned, and related topics for all strategic improvement priorities.
  • Works with staff to use audit strategies, data extraction, observation, surveys, focus groups, or other tools to improve care and service quality.
  • Participates in design, development, and implementation of facility learning forums.
  • Participates in unit and/or facility huddles.
  • Helps the ZERO Harm rounding process as directed by leadership.
  • Stay aware of the latest developments, advancements, and trends in quality improvement reporting and testing. Attend seminars and workshops, read professional journals, and participate in professional organizations.

Key Success Factors

  • Must be a Registered Nurse with acute care OB experience
  • Ability to complete chart abstractions, data analysis, participate in quality improvement projects, quality outcome monitoring, and patient safety event monitoring.
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft office suite products including Excel, Forms, and OneNote, etc.
  • Extensive knowledge of tools and techniques of quality performance measurement and data testing
  • Extensive knowledge of Texas, Joint Commission and CMS standards specifically maternal outcomes of care certification
  • Extensive knowledge of trends, developments, and research in providing high-quality safe care
  • Skilled facilitator, coach, consultant, influencer, management and strategic thinking skills
  • Skilled in the use of computers, and related software applications
  • Exceptional verbal, social and written communication skills
  • Able to mentor, train and develop instructional materials to educate leadership and staff in quality, patient safety, regulatory issues
  • Able to work collaboratively and effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, and across organizational lines and teams
  • Able to identify and deploy required project management processes, tools, and templates needed to successfully drive initiatives
  • Able to partner with key stakeholders to identify impediments to success and recommend and implement corrective actions and/or mitigation
  • Able to work alone or with varying levels of direct or indirect supervision and guidance
  • Able to appropriately prioritize tasks to meet desired deadline
  • Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ), Certified Professional in Patient Safety (CPPS), or role-appropriate certification preferred
  • Licensed clinician such as nurse, physical therapist, occupational therapist, dietitian, respiratory therapist, etc. preferred.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • EDUCATION - Bachelor's or 4 years of work experience above the minimum qualification
  • EXPERIENCE - 4 Years of Experience
  • Registered nurse with a minimum of 2 years acute care OB experience

title: Case Manager
description:
REM Community Services, a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.


OUR MISSION AND PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

At Sevita, we believe that everyone deserves to live well. For more than 50 years, our team members have provided home and community-based health care for adults, children, and their families across the United States. Our extraordinary team offers innovative, quality services and support that lead to growth and new opportunities for the people we serve and for our employees.

SUMMARY

Social Workers are responsible for the evaluation and treatment of clients admitted for treatment. The Social Worker adheres to specific scope of service for activities related to the evaluation and treatment of clients in the home and community.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below:

  • Evaluation including gathering data from client records, interviews, observation and dialogue with other team members
  • Development and implementation of a treatment plan according to physician orders which includes establishing client goals, continuous re-evaluation of progress and appropriate modification of the plan
  • Timely preparation of written documentation of client progress including initial evaluations, progress reports, discharge summaries and other requested reports
  • One to one counseling with client/and or family members in their home or other appropriate setting
  • Increases awareness of client and caregivers about brain injury to better facilitate adjustment and understanding of the process of recovery.
  • Attends team conferences and reports on client’s progress and current status in therapy as well as collaboratively assisting the team in identifying realistic goals
  • Completes and turns in billing information in a timely manner
  • Communicates effectively with internal case manager
  • Performs other related duties and activities as required.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

None

Minimum Knowledge and Skills required by the Job

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job:

Education

  • Master’s Degree in Social Work from an accredited school of social work
  • Membership in NASW and related clinical experience in a rehabilitation setting with focus on traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury.

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:

  • In MI, certified by the State of Michigan as a social worker
  • Valid Michigan Driver’s license for employees in state of Michigan

Other Skills and Abilities:

  • Motor Vehicle in operating condition
  • Ability to operate a motor vehicle
  • Able to travel distances exceeding 45 minutes

Other Requirements:

  • Travel as needed

Physical Requirements:

  • Medium Work. Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT STATEMENT

External and internal applicants, as well as position incumbents who become disabled, must be able to perform the essential job functions either unaided or with assistance of a reasonable accommodation to be determined on a case by case basis via the interactive process.



Sevita is a leading provider of home and community-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.

title: Director Customer Experience, Follow-Up Journey
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Director, Customer Experience – Follow-Up Journey plans, develops, and implements customer experience programs and initiatives for BSWH, which may include customer strategy, customer journeys, customer brand campaigns, customer data analysis, customer satisfaction and retention, and other customer-focused activities. Responsible for customer experience and its impact to overall customer satisfaction of BSWH healthcare services. Ensures that customer policies and practices align with overall organizational direction and BSWH business objectives. Instills a strong customer-centric culture that demonstrates healthcare industry best practices. Leverages customer data, analytics, and insights to continuously design and improve customer experience journeys and strengthen BSWH customer-centric capabilities. title: LillyDirect Pharmacy Master Data Technical Lead
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. As Technical Lead for the LillyDirect Pharmacy Covered Entity Master Data team, you will own the technical direction and delivery of the data platform that creates trusted, consented customer and partner profiles. You will set engineering standards, guide a team of data engineers, and be the go-to expert on how Reltio (profile master data) and Transcend (consent management) work with our AWS and Databricks data platform. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. Your work ensures the right data, used with the right consent, reaches patients and the business, supporting Lilly's mission to deliver life-changing medicines.


What you’ll be doing:


Master data and consent

  • Define and own the technical architecture for profile master data, including Reltio integration, match and merge logic, survivorship rules, and golden record delivery to downstream consumers.
  • Design how consent and preference data from Transcend flows through the platform, so consent status is enforced consistently in pipelines, profiles, and downstream use.
  • Design how data subject requests (for example access and deletion) are carried out across profile data and downstream systems, so requests are honored consistently and can be evidenced.
  • Partner with Privacy, Legal, Quality, and business teams to translate consent and regulatory requirements (for example HIPAA and applicable privacy laws) into technical controls.
  • Define technical controls for protecting sensitive data (PII/PHI), including access control, masking, encryption, and retention, in line with Lilly standards.
  • Build data quality, lineage, and reconciliation checks that prove profile and consent data is accurate, complete, and auditable.

Data engineering delivery

  • Lead design and delivery of batch and near-real-time pipelines in Python and PySpark on Databricks and AWS.
  • Design Delta Lake and lakehouse (medallion) structures with sound partitioning, schema evolution, and Unity Catalog governance.
  • Build observable pipelines with error handling, retries, alerting, and clear SLAs.
  • Set standards for CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code for data workloads, working with the DevOps engineer, so environments are repeatable and reviewed.
  • Tune SQL, Spark jobs, and data models for performance and cost.
  • Own production support for data pipelines, including escalation, incident response, and root cause analysis, in partnership with the DevOps engineer.

Technical leadership

  • Set coding standards, code review practices, and documentation (architecture decision records, runbooks, data contracts).
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, pair programming, and knowledge sessions.
  • Partner with product owners, architects, and vendor teams to turn business needs into a clear technical roadmap, and influence vendor resources so delivery matches our data and technical direction.
  • Represent the team in architecture reviews, security reviews, and platform governance forums.

How You Will Succeed:


  • You turn business and privacy needs into technical outcomes that stakeholders understand and trust.
  • You set standards that others adopt, and you mentor engineers to raise the team’s technical bar.
  • You treat consent as a design principle, not an afterthought, and you catch risks before they reach production.
  • You improve systems continuously through automation, performance tuning, and proactive issue resolution.
  • You communicate with clarity to technical and non-technical audiences.

Basic Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
  • 8+ years of professional experience in data engineering or software engineering, including 3+ years as a tech lead, principal engineer, or senior individual contributor.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with Reltio (or a comparable MDM platform) for profile or customer master data, including match rules, survivorship, and integration patterns.

Additional Skills & Preferences:


  • Working understanding of consent and preference management (for example opt-in and opt-out, purpose, and channel), and how consent must be enforced in data pipelines and downstream use.
  • Hands-on experience with Transcend (or a similar consent platform) for consent, preference, or data subject request workflows.
  • Expert-level Python and PySpark, with production-grade code, automated testing, and performance tuning, and advanced SQL, including window functions, CTEs, and query optimization.
  • Strong hands-on experience building data pipelines on AWS (for example S3, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions, Athena or Redshift, IAM) and Databricks, including Delta Lake.
  • Experience with data modeling (dimensional and lakehouse medallion patterns) and data governance, security, and quality practices, including protection of sensitive data (PII/PHI).
  • Experience with CI/CD, Git, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CDK, or CloudFormation).
  • Ability to lead technical design, mentor engineers, and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Pharmaceutical, healthcare, or pharmacy industry experience, and experience in regulated environments with privacy and compliance requirements.
  • Experience partnering with and influencing vendor resources on solution development and delivery.
  • Experience with orchestration tools such as Apache Airflow or Databricks Workflows.
  • Familiarity with data quality frameworks (for example Great Expectations or dbt tests) and with streaming platforms (Kafka, Kinesis, or MSK).
  • Familiarity with data catalog and governance tools such as Unity Catalog or AWS Lake Formation.
  • AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate, AWS Solutions Architect, or Databricks Certified Data Engineer (Associate or Professional).

  • Maintains medical imaging records in appropriate system and according to department policies and standards for interpretation in a timely manner.

title: Scientist - Analytical Method Development SMDD Foundry Readiness
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Synthetic Molecule Design and Development has an exciting opportunity for an analytical chemist to join our development group. In this hands-on laboratory role (>70% bench work), you will develop analytical methods and characterize chemical processes to advance drug candidates from early development through manufacturing readiness. You will expand and apply your expertise in chromatographic method development and leverage complementary techniques (mass spectrometry, NMR) while partnering closely with synthetic chemists and process engineers to solve critical process development challenges. The ideal candidate brings practical chromatography experience, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to translate analytical data into actionable insights for project teams.


Position Responsibilities:

  • Develop and optimize analytical methods to accurately measure purity, potency, and other critical quality attributes of small molecule drug substances and synthetic intermediates.
  • Select and implement appropriate analytical techniques (HPLC, GC, NMR, MS) to support chemical process development—independently generating data that elucidates reaction mechanisms, characterizes kinetic behavior, and identifies process-related impurities.
  • Collaborate with synthetic chemists and process engineers to ensure analytical methods are suitable for guiding development activities and can be successfully transferred to GMP laboratories for routine testing and manufacturing support.
  • Perform laboratory activities with a strong emphasis on safety and technical rigor, while adhering to local policies and procedures.
  • Identify and apply new scientific concepts, exhibit strong problem-solving skills, and be self-motivated to contribute across multiple projects.
  • Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills to represent both the technical aspects and business-related implications of your work.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemistry, or a related field with 2+ years of relevant experience
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Additional Skills/Preferences:

  • Experience with chromatographic (LC, GC, IC) method development or validation in pharmaceutical, chemical, or regulated industry setting
  • Working knowledge of mass spectrometry (LC-MS, GC-MS) and NMR spectroscopy
  • Familiarity with chemical process development, synthetic organic chemistry, and rationales for establishing material specifications and testing plans.
  • Experience troubleshooting and maintaining analytical instrumentation.
  • Demonstration of scientific leadership and the ability to influence others.
  • Ability to balance multiple responsibilities, prioritize activities, and navigate ambiguity.

Additional Information:

  • Potential exposure to chemicals, allergens, and loud noises
  • Travel: 0 to 10%
  • Position Local: Indianapolis, IN; Lilly Technology Center-North (LTC-N)
