title: Associate Director/Director, S2P Contracting COE
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our more than 50,000 employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.


Job Description

The Associate Director leads the S2P Contracting COE (“S2P CCOE”), reports to the Sr. Director, S2P COE, and implements Global Procurement’s contracting strategy. The role manages and develops a team of Contract Managers supporting Global Procurement and owns the Master Procurement Template (MPT) contract inventory, Procurement’s Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) processes, and contract knowledge management. The role works closely with partners such as Lilly Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity, Corporate Risk Management, Tax, and Import/Export to manage risk through approved negotiation playbooks, keeps templates current with new laws and regulations, and ensures that CLM AI Redline Models reflect MPT inventory changes and CLM processes meet the needs of the S2P organization. The role also provides contracting subject matter expertise to S2P COE colleagues.


Key Responsibilities:


Personnel Management and Development

  • Lead, supervise, coach, and develop the S2P Contracting COE team to deliver on its mission. This includes a mix of direct reports and an M1 supervisor.
  • Attract, develop, and retain a diverse team, including onboarding new staff.
  • Model Lilly values and foster an environment where results are recognized and team members feel comfortable speaking up and sharing ideas.
  • Hold regular development conversations: share feedback, identify strengths and growth areas, coach, support mentoring, and manage performance.
  • Manage and forecast team resource needs so projects are completed on time.

Master Procurement Templates

  • Own the MPT contract inventory.
  • Oversee change control for new and updated MPT clauses, templates, and playbook guidance.
  • Manage and oversee ad hoc specialty projects, such as amending large volumes of contracts to comply with applicable law or internal policy updates.
  • Represent MPT standards and the negotiation playbook in audits.
  • Partner with cross-functional and Procurement colleagues to identify needed changes to the MPT inventory and Work Order Templates.
  • Analyze frequently negotiated terms and recommend MPT updates to Lilly Legal/SMEs and Procurement leadership.

Contract Training

  • Partner with S2P Learning & Development to build role-specific CLM and MPT training and onboard Global Procurement on their use.
  • Create and maintain onboarding and training resources and materials for the S2P Contracting COE.
  • Oversee MPT-related content on the Supplier Resources Portal on Lilly.com.

Contract Lifecycle Management Program

  • Partner closely with leaders across Procurement, IBU Procurement and Lilly Legal to define and implement a shared CLM program strategy, driving progress to agreed budget and timelines.
  • Report progress, proactively identify risk, and escalate in a timely manner to leadership.
  • Lead pre-implementation discovery efforts with project team to identify gaps, elicit requirements, develop process maps, and identify contract management reporting needs, KPIs and SLAs.
  • Ensure the CLM solution and training program comply with Lilly policies and procedures.
  • Partner with Tech@Lilly to guide the CLM vendor on requirements, development, legacy contract migration, integrations, and validation testing, and to manage the vendor relationship for performance, security, and compliance.
  • Benchmark CLM practices and recommend opportunities for innovation and improvement.
  • Lead project team as the contracting SME to deliver program key objectives to meet Lilly’s tactical and strategic objectives inclusive of:
    • Transformation of Procurement’s contracting process and use of CLM technology solutions.
    • Tracking and reporting relevant CLM SLAs, KPIs, and contract terms and conditions.
    • Accelerating delivery of contracts to business partners.
    • Enablement of self-service contracting within acceptable risk profiles.

Basic Requirements:


- BS/BA degree in related discipline (e.g., Legal, business, project management)

- Significant experience in people management; ability to motivate teams and achieve results through others.

- Strong interpersonal and teambuilding skills; able to deliver effective coaching and feedback; positively manage and resolve conflict and demonstrate strong leadership and influence skills.

- Strategic mindset with the ability to define strategy and drive implementation.

- Minimum of 10 years’ of progressive work experience that clearly demonstrates contract drafting, contract negotiation, and/or legal experience.


Additional Skills/Experiences

- Proven experience with global project implementations

- Proven problem solving, critical thinking and decision making

- Proven ability to author and negotiate complex MSA’s in a highly regulated environment

- Ability to network and influence across all levels of management and across organizations.

- Ability to work independently and prioritize multiple projects.

- Procurement/Professional sourcing experience

- CLM Technology experience

- MBA


Travel Percentage: Occasional international travel (up to 10%)

title: Program Management Program Director
description:
REM Community Services, a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.


SUMMARY

  • Position Type: Full-time, exempt, salaried supervisor role.
  • Scope of Role:
    • Responsible for managing the services delivered to a designated program or set of programs, and the operation of programs.
  • Key Responsibilities:
    • Oversee organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, staffing, training, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.

Staff Management:

  1. Recruitment & Hiring: May participate in hiring events as needed and partner with Talent Acquisition to identify hiring needs for Direct Support Professionals and Program Supervisors in consultation with the Area Director.
  2. Meetings & Training: Organizes and implements on-site orientation and training for assigned programs and monitors training compliance and documentation; conducts monthly staff meetings; attends monthly regional meetings and additional meetings as needed.
  3. Employee Scheduling: Designs and monitors schedules to ensure that all shifts are covered; monitors and minimizes overtime.
  4. Performance Evaluation: Conducts rotating performance snapshots and evaluations for direct reports in consultation with the PD’s manager; reviews and approves Direct Support Professional and other staff member’s performance evaluations.
  5. Coaching, Discipline and Termination: Coaches employees, correcting or directing employee behavior where required; may remove employees at their sole discretion in the event of emergency; may recommend and participate in decisions regarding discipline and termination in consultation with the PD’s manager and Human Resources; manages the termination of Direct Support Professionals or other staff members, as necessary.
  6. Employee Safety: Responsible for employee safety and workers’ compensation programs; monitors compliance; and assists in returning employees to work; implements, oversees, and trains employees about safety.

Program Management:

  1. Program Planning: Acts as the QIDP (if required), writes and approves individual program plans; trains and assists appropriate staff members with implementation of plans across all shifts.
  2. Records: Periodically audits individual records and other program documentation for accuracy and completion.
  3. Program Team Meetings: Conducts progress meetings and (quarterly, annual, and/or other) reviews as appropriate or determined by the interdisciplinary team; provides and approves written and progress reviews.
  4. Compliance: Oversees licensing compliance for program services and supports; ensures timely and accurate program documentation; implements the Sevita compliance plan and manages individual rights implementation while maintaining confidentiality and adhering to individual rights standards.
  5. Management of Individuals’ Assets: Implements system and oversees management of individual’s funds and property, assuring safety and accuracy; audits, monitors, and reviews individual’s financial accounts.
  6. Program Stakeholder Relations: Maintains productive and professional relations with individuals, families, case managers and other stakeholders; provides regular communication to stakeholders; and acts as point of contact for all stakeholders; implements satisfaction improvement plans.
  7. Government Relations: Engages in government and community relations; participates in advocacy efforts and ensures preparedness for home visits (e.g., staff, families, legislators).
  8. Incidents: Implements proactive strategies to reduce or eliminate serious incidents; takes immediate steps to correct potential safety concerns and limit the potential for continued concern or incident; reviews all incidents and directs appropriate response; ensures timely incident reporting; and signs and submits all incident reports as required.

Health Care:

  1. Appointments: Oversees coordination of health care appointments and monitors individual attendance.
  2. Medications: Oversees system for medication administration, documentation, and security; reviews documentation for accuracy and completeness; ensures all applicable employees are certified or trained in medication administration.
  3. Medical Supplies and Equipment: Approves purchases of medical supplies and equipment; and ensures training in proper use to all employees.
  4. Dietary planning: Monitors food service in accordance with dietary plans and to meet regulatory compliance; ensures consideration for special needs, occasions, and individual choice; ensures all applicable employees are certified or trained in meal preparation and/or dietary planning.

Financial Management:

  1. Purchasing: Approves purchase of food, supplies and equipment; and reviews and monitors monthly invoices for accuracy and budgetary compliance; attests to company credit card statements and monthly invoices in accordance with company policy.
  2. Billing and utilization: Oversees census, attendance information or other required documentation to assure accurate billing; ensures program documentation is accurate, complete, and compliant; monitors utilization between authorization and provision of services and supports.
  3. Staffing: Monitors staffing hours for budgetary compliance.
  4. Growth: Develops understanding of program growth strategy and supports implementation of growth initiatives within the program

Census Management:

  1. Census Performance: Monitors census performance for their location(s) and escalates potential service disruptions that impact census to the Area Director and Regional Director.
  2. Referrals: Reviews referrals to validate fit for specific locations and identifies and escalates potential barriers to serving individuals to the Area Director and Regional Director; coordinates and prepares for in-person site visits at locations during referral process.
  3. Placements: Coordinates preparations required for expected placements including staffing, funding, home set-up, and safety requirements.

Maintenance:

  1. Vehicles: Ensures vehicles are properly maintained, clean, and safe by consulting with maintenance personnel; implements training procedures for maintenance and safe operation of company-owned vehicles, including reviewing checklists on a regular basis; addresses known safety concerns with employee vehicles or other means of transportation, for the safe transport of individuals.
  2. Housekeeping: Monitors and implements strategies to assure neat, clean, and safe program environments (internal and external); ensures age appropriate and esthetic decoration.
  3. Maintenance and Repair: Oversees environmental safety program; establishes preventive maintenance schedule; maintains furnishings, equipment, and facilities in good repair and compliant with regulatory standards.

Other:

  • Performs other duties and activities as required, including backfilling roles under your supervision.
  • Must be available on-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.
  • Performs other related duties and activities as required.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Manages the Direct Support Professionals, Program Supervisors and other direct or indirect staff members of the program. Completes performance evaluations, orientation, and training. Makes decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, discipline, terminations, and similar actions. Resolves employee problems within position responsibilities.

Minimum Knowledge and Skills required for the Job

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree
  • Two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience which provides proficiency in the areas of responsibility listed above may be substituted for the above education and experience requirements.
  • Other education and experience as required by applicable regulations.

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:

  • Current driver's license, car registration and auto insurance if driving on behalf of the Company or providing transportation to individuals receiving services.
  • Licensure(s) as required by state.
  • Medication Management Certificate issued with the completion of Company provided training.
  • Mandatory Reporter Certificate issued with the completion of Company provided training.
  • Other training(s) and/or certification(s) per state requirements and/or service line.
  • For specific programs:
    • AZ Behavioral Health programs must meet BHT requirements.

Key Metrics:

  • Individuals' Served Funds Compliance
  • Customer Satisfaction
  • Documentation Compliance
  • Licensing Compliance
  • Quality (% participation)
  • Program Visits
  • Overtime
  • Job Requisitions
  • Program Training Compliance

Work Environment:

  • The Program Director works at the program location(s) they oversee.
  • Oversees services or supports in residential, vocational, or in-home settings.

Other Requirements:

  • Travel as needed

Physical Requirements:

  • Medium Work. Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

title: Associate Director - Senior Case Manager
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Job Position Overview:


The Associate Director, Senior Case Manager, Case Management Operations is the senior hands-on practitioner for Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) work across the three operational pillars of Case Management Operations: intake, case processing and regulatory submission. The role settles the hardest case-level questions and keeps case execution consistent across Lilly and vendor sites. It is a working-level authority that Case Management Operations leadership and process SMEs rely on for case decisions.


Responsibilities:

ICSR Intake, Processing and Submissions

  • Act as the key operational decisionmaker on complex ICSR validity questions, including the four minimum criteria, unidentifiable reporters or patients, counterfeit and product-quality reports, and reports with no suspect Lilly product, as well as case versus non-case determinations.
  • Monitor operational metrics and trends to identify emerging risks, and ensure timely resolution or escalation of concerns, including those identified through quality review or raised by leadership.
  • Resolve difficult, complex, duplicate and linked-case scenarios (for example parent–child and pregnancy cases, or the same patient reported through several sources) and confirm the correct master case.
  • Provide audit and inspection support for case management operations, including case-level evidence and case walk-throughs when requested, including performing the root cause investigations and CAPA implementations.
  • Coach case managers and vendor trainers on difficult case scenarios.
  • Help create and deliver shared learnings, as needed.
  • Serve as the escalation point for complex E2B acknowledgment rejections and submission failures that sites cannot resolve and decide the root cause and correction approach at the case level.
  • Advise Case Management Operations leadership on the case-level drivers behind backlog, throughput or timeliness trends, and highlight concerns to strategic vendor management team with recommendations of operational response.
  • Support the calibration of ICSR quality reviewers so that the same quality error is scored the same way at every site.
  • Escalate systemic quality or compliance risks to the Case Management leadership team, as applicable.

Escalation Support and Working-Level Guidance

  • Be the escalation point for process SMEs and Case Management Operations managers on case decisions they cannot resolve.
  • Review Shared Learnings content prepared by product SMEs and case managers for accuracy and consistency before release.
  • Represent the case processor's view of the safety database and intake tools in user testing, defect triage and change requests, as needed.
  • Identify manual, repetitive steps in case processing (for example repeated lookups or manually written narratives) and document the requirements for tooling or automation.

Cross-Functional Partnering

  • Work with Clinical and Commercial Liaisons on intake channels and product-specific case handling conventions.
  • Give operational input to Standards & Compliance when procedures that affect case processing are revised.
  • Partner with internal and external stakeholders on process and system updates, as needed.

Perform other related duties, as assigned

  • Provide case-level information requested by the EU QPPV office, such as case status and submission evidence.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on ICSR processing experience covering intake, data entry and submission, including at least 2 years reviewing or quality-checking the work of other processors.
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Preferences:

  • Experience coaching and calibrating case processors across more than one site or vendor.
  • Applied knowledge of ICSR reporting requirements (for example ICH E2B(R3), ICH E2D, EU GVP Module VI, FDA 21 CFR 314.80 and 600.80) at the level of individual case decisions.
  • Hands-on proficiency with a safety database (for example Argus or Veeva Vault Safety) and with MedDRA and WHO Drug coding.
  • Track record of resolving complex validity, duplicate and coding questions and explaining the rationale clearly to processors.
  • Working proficiency in Excel for case volume and quality tracking (for example pivot tables and lookups).
  • Previous experience in/ with an outsourced or multi-vendor case processing model.
  • Prior work with case processing capacity and throughput analysis.
  • Previous experience in/ with handling device, combination product or clinical trial serious adverse event (SAE) cases, including SAE reconciliation.
  • Pior work with intake or case processing automation tools.
  • Proven ability to deliver case processing work through a site transition or product routing change.

Additional Information:

  • Location: US: Indianapolis, Indiana
  • Travel Percentage (%): 0-10%
  • Language Requirements: Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to write clear case guidance for multinational teams.

title: Workplace Tech Microsoft Platforms Manager
description:
Job Summary

The Workplace Tech Microsoft Platforms Manager is responsible for managing the delivery, governance, and continuous improvement of enterprise Microsoft platforms that support patient care and healthcare operations. This role combines a strong engineering background, people leadership, and ethical decision-making in a highly regulated, mission-driven environment.

The Workplace Tech Microsoft Platforms Manager owns the Microsoft Tech stack including Microsoft collaboration platforms (Teams non-voice, SharePoint, OneDrive), Power Platform solutions, and analytics capabilities using Microsoft Fabric/Power BI and Active Directory and Group Policy Management. The role contributes to platform architecture, executes roadmaps, and leads multiple delivery teams—including offshore resources—to deliver secure, scalable, and user-centered solutions.

Working closely with clinical, operational, cybersecurity, and enterprise architecture partners, this position ensures technology platforms are reliable, compliant, and designed to reduce clinician burden, protect patient data, and support high-quality care across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

People Leadership & Delivery

  • Lead and manage multiple onshore and offshore teams, including engineers, analysts, and developers.
  • Set clear expectations, delivery standards, and performance goals.
  • Coach and develop team members with a focus on engineering rigor, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure predictable, high-quality delivery across multiple workstreams.

Architecture & Roadmap Execution

  • Contribute to platform and solution architecture in alignment with enterprise standards.
  • Participate in the development and execution of platform roadmaps across identity, collaboration, automation, and analytics.
  • Balance innovation, technical debt reduction, and operational stability.
  • Identify risks, dependencies, and improvement opportunities early.

Platform & Service Ownership

  • Lead collaboration platforms including Microsoft Teams (voice & non-voice), SharePoint Online, and OneDrive.
  • Manage Power Platform delivery, including functional solution design & development task.
  • Oversee analytics solutions using Microsoft Fabric and Power BI to support operational, quality, and performance reporting.
  • Apply UI/UX principles to ensure solutions are intuitive and aligned to healthcare workflows.

Active Directory & Group Policy Management

  • Contribute to Active Directory Services, including domain structure, OU design, governance, and lifecycle management.
  • Lead Group Policy Management (GPM) design, standardization, and lifecycle governance.
  • Ensure AD and GPO configurations support:
    • Secure access to clinical and business systems
    • Endpoint configuration and security baselines
    • Performance, usability, and reliability standards
  • Partner with endpoint, security, and compliance teams to meet HIPAA and audit requirements.
  • Oversee AD and GPO operations through teams (not hands-on administration).

Governance, Ethics & Risk Management

  • Execute governance models across identity, collaboration, automation, and analytics platforms.
  • Demonstrate ethical leadership in technology decisions, delivery, and vendor management.
  • Ensure responsible handling of patient and workforce data.
  • Partner with cybersecurity and compliance teams to support regulatory, privacy, and audit readiness.
  • Establish and monitor KPIs, service health indicators, and quality metrics.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with clinical, operational, and administrative leaders to understand priorities and constraints.
  • Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor for platform capabilities, risks, and roadmap decisions.

AI & Emerging Technology Leadership

  • Enable and govern the responsible use of AI and emerging technologies across Microsoft platforms, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Power
  • Platform AI capabilities, and Fabric/Power BI analytics.
  • Ensure platforms are AI-ready through proper identity, access, policy, and data controls (Active Directory, Entra ID, Group Policy).
  • Partner with cybersecurity, compliance, and legal teams to deploy AI solutions that are secure, ethical, explainable, and aligned with healthcare regulations.
  • Identify and evaluate emerging Microsoft capabilities to improve clinician experience, operational efficiency, and insight generation.
  • Promote innovation while enforcing guardrails that protect patient data, privacy, and organizational trust.

This role balances innovation with responsibility, ensuring AI enhances healthcare delivery without compromising safety, ethics, or compliance.

Qualifications

Preferred Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 7–10 years of progressive IS/IT experience with a strong engineering foundation.
  • 2–4 years of people management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience with:
  • Active Directory and Group Policy Management
  • Microsoft 365
  • Azure AD / Entra ID
  • Microsoft Teams (non-voice)
  • Power Platform
  • Microsoft Fabric and/or Power BI
  • Experience contributing to architecture, executing roadmaps, and leading multi-team delivery.
  • Experience managing or coordinating offshore teams.
  • Strong communication skills and a demonstrated commitment to ethical leadership.
  • Experience in healthcare or other highly regulated environments.
  • Microsoft certifications
  • Experience supporting endpoint, clinical, or shared services platforms.
  • Familiarity with Agile or product-based delivery models.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's or 4 years of work experience above the minimum qualification
  • 5 Years of Experience

title: Data Strategy Manager
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The manager leads the data strategy, architecture, reporting and AI agenda for Business Intelligence & Analytics (BI&A) in Brazil. The role turns data into a trusted asset that teams can reuse. It supports commercial and medical decisions and helps the business adopt new ways of working with data.

In partnership with global BI&A, GCDP, Tech@Lilly and Brazil leadership, the role sets the data roadmap, guides platform choices and keeps governance simple and enforceable. The Manager leads a team across data architecture, reporting and advanced analytics, plus vendor and offshore partners.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

Data strategy and governance

  • Define and run the Brazil data strategy, aligned with global BI&A priorities and the enterprise data platform.
  • Build a multi-year data roadmap with clear priorities, owners, funding needs and measurable outcomes.
  • Set up data governance: ownership, definitions, quality rules, access controls and compliance with LGPD and Lilly policies.
  • Standardize KPIs and metric definitions so every report tells the same story.
  • Manage internal and external data sources, including contracts, costs and refresh rules.

Data architecture and platforms

  • Own the Brazil data architecture, from ingestion and storage to modeling and serving layers.
  • Work with Tech@Lilly to choose platforms and tools that meet enterprise standards and can scale.
  • Lead adoption of the Enterprise Data Backbone, and retire local pipelines and duplicate data stores when a standard option exists.
  • Keep pipelines reliable, documented, monitored and cost aware.
  • Prepare data foundations for AI: clean, well described, secure and easy to find.
  • Decide what to build locally and what to reuse from global teams.

Reporting and insight delivery

  • Lead the redesign and consolidation of dashboards into a small set of enterprise-standard reporting products.
  • Retire legacy reports and set clear rules for when a new dashboard is justified.
  • Define service levels for reporting, including refresh times, data quality, support and release cycles.
  • Translate complex data into clear insights for Commercial, Medical, Finance, Corporate Affairs and Operations.
  • Enable self-service analytics with certified datasets, shared semantic models and simple guidance.
  • Represent data and reporting topics in Brazil leadership forums and planning cycles.

AI and advanced analytics

  • Define the AI and advanced analytics agenda for Brazil, tied to real business use cases and value targets.
  • Rank use cases by value, feasibility and data readiness, and stop those that do not deliver.
  • Partner with global teams and Tech@Lilly to bring approved AI tools and models into daily work.
  • Set guardrails for responsible AI, including data privacy, model validation, human review and audit trails.
  • Track adoption and business impact of each AI solution, not only delivery.
  • Test new methods in small pilots and scale only what works.

Change management and capability building

  • Lead a change plan for each major data initiative, with stakeholder mapping, communication, training and adoption tracking.
  • Guide teams and business partners through the move from legacy tools to new platforms and ways of working.
  • Build data literacy programs for commercial, medical and corporate teams.
  • Name data champions in each area and run regular feedback loops.
  • Measure adoption with clear indicators, such as active users, retired reports and use of certified data.

Team, vendors and partners

  • Lead, coach and develop a team across data architecture, reporting and advanced analytics.
  • Manage vendor and offshore teams for quality, timing and cost.
  • Manage budget, capacity and priorities across the data portfolio.
  • Align roadmaps with global BI&A, GCDP, Tech@Lilly, OCE, CRM and Digital Business Hub teams.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in data, analytics, BI or commercial operations.
  • Minimum 3 years leading data strategy, architecture or platform work.
  • Minimum 3 years of people leadership experience (direct reports and/or matrix leadership).
  • Proven delivery of data and IT projects on modern cloud and BI platforms.
  • Solid knowledge of data modeling, governance, data quality and security.
  • Working knowledge of AI and machine learning, and how to bring them to production responsibly.
  • Strong vendor, budget and portfolio management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across commercial and medical functions.
  • Fluent in English and Portuguese (written and spoken).

ADDITIONAL PREFERENCES

  • Change-management experience, with a track record of guiding teams through platform and process transitions.
  • Experience in pharma or another regulated industry.
  • Global or multi-market data program experience.
  • Understanding of pharma commercial, medical and omnichannel data, such as CRM, sales and market data.
  • Hands-on knowledge of BI tools, SQL and cloud data platforms.

title: Sr. Engineer, Automation Engineering, Controls Hardware - Lilly Medicine Foundry
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


The Senior Engineer - Automation Engineering will work as a member of the Automation Engineering Department at Eli Lilly, Foundry. The engineer will provide automation support for one or more operating areas across site and/or for capital projects, with primary focus on Instrumentation and Control Hardware. Process Automation is core to delivering the right first-time facility start up and continued support of ongoing manufacturing operations into the future.


The Senior Engineer will collaborate and partner with cross-functional peers to support successful delivery of robust control systems and instrumentation.

In the project delivery phase and startup phase of the project (startup expected 2026 to 2028), automation engineering roles will be fluid and dynamic as we endeavor to support the project delivery, build a new organization, develop and implement the necessary systems and business processes required to support GMP operations, and build the site culture. This will require significant collaboration, creativity and resilience as the site grows to a full scale GMP manufacturing through start up.


Key Objectives/Deliverables:

  • Experience working with DeltaV Distributed Control System, Batch Process Automation.
  • Experience working with Rockwell Allen Bradley PLC’s, FactoryTalk View.
  • Experience working with DeltaV control panels, DeltaV Remote I/O panels and Rockwell I/O’s.
  • Experience in performing automation engineering activities including design, Development and Commissioning Process Automation projects using DeltaV DCS and/or Rockwell Allen Bradley PLC.
  • Experience with tuning and troubleshooting of control loops and Field Instruments.
  • Hands-on experience in configuration and troubleshooting of Variable Frequency Drives (VFD’s).
  • Thorough understanding of P&ID’s and Instrument loop drawings.
  • Understanding various process control communication protocols.

Operational Excellence

  • Site operation runtime support, enhance control system reliability and lifecycle management, in a GMP regulated environment.
  • Support capital project execution, Commissioning and Qualification.
  • Demonstrated ability in resolving complex technical challenges with instrument and control system hardware.
  • Work with Site Area leads and System Integrators.
  • Develop and Review Functional Requirements, Design Specifications and Test Specifications.
  • Demonstrated experience utilizing Master maintenance plans.
  • Familiarity with 21CFR Part 11, GMP processes.
  • Participate in design reviews and Site system hardware reviews, attend equipment FATs.
  • Provide periodic status updates to Project Management.
  • Support electronic systems (such as plant historians) used to capture process automation related production data.
  • Maintain the validated state of the site control system hardware in line with Lilly quality standards including the development and execution of validation strategies and associated documentation.
  • Good planning and organizational skills, ability to prioritize tasks, commitment to task completion and timelines.

Organizational Capability

  • In coordination with automation and compliance consultants, set and reinforce standards for appropriate rigor in automation work products.
  • Engage with cross-functional peers to strengthen technical capabilities and adopt best practices to enhance system reliability and business continuity.

Basic Requirements:

  • Minimum B.S. in Engineering or related degree and experience in Automation Engineering
  • 2+ years working experience in Pharmaceutical or highly regulated environment
  • Knowledge of GMP, regulatory requirements, computer system validation
  • Available to participate in a rotational on-call schedule
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience working in highly automated facility, using DeltaV DCS, Rockwell Allen Bradley PLC, Veeva, PI, and/or BMS Warehouse Monitoring from design through Startup.
  • Possess a keen technical curiosity and has demonstrated strong problem-solving skills and a desire for continuous improvement
  • Good written and verbal communication skills for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Hands-on experience working directly with automation control panel hardware and wiring.

title: Director, Learning Technology Strategy & Innovation
description:
Posting Date

10/29/20262000 16th St, Denver, Colorado, 80202-5117, United States of America

Director, Learning Technology Strategy & Innovation

Location: Remote or Denver Hybrid (Preferred)

The Opportunity

DaVita is elevating learning capabilities for 70,000+ teammates across the Village. Within Wisdom, our enterprise learning organization, the Learning Technology function owns the platforms (LMS/LXP) and associated architecture and integrations that power everything from clinical onboarding to leadership development, and an expanding ecosystem of experience, workflow, and AI-enabled technologies.


We are seeking a Director of Learning Technology to own and evolve that learning ecosystem to keep pace with our Village ambitions. This is not a platform administration or vendor-management role. It is a transformational leadership role to envision a bold future and chart the path to reach it. This leader will be a decision-maker at the intersection of technology architecture, learning strategy, user experience, and enterprise execution.


The ideal candidate brings a rare combination: enough technical depth to own architecture and integration decisions without translation, enough learning domain expertise to create and inspire a vision for the future, and enough executive presence and strategic thinking to effectively advise and influence senior leaders and partners.



Your Impact

As the leader of Learning Technology, you will:

  • Own the Decisions: Serve as the accountable owner for learning technology architecture, platform strategy, and implementation direction. Make consequential technical and strategic decisions with incomplete information, defend them with senior stakeholders, and change course when the evidence warrants — without escalating every judgment call.
  • Architect the Ecosystem: Define where DaVita's learning technology is going — platform architecture, integration strategy, data flows, and the roadmap for emerging capabilities including AI-enabled learning — and lead the product management team that operationalizes it.
  • Lead Enterprise Delivery: Direct high-complexity, high-visibility technology implementations in partnership with enterprise Technology, People Services, and external implementation partners, holding the line on scope, sequencing, and teammate experience through sprint-based delivery.
  • Partner at the Executive Level: Serve as the trusted technology voice for VP- and C-level sponsors — bringing them real risk, real tradeoffs, and real recommendations rather than status updates. Navigate priorities of multiple teams and stakeholders and work with and between teams to get work delivered.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities


Technology Strategy & Architecture

Own the strategic platform evolution across the enterprise learning ecosystem. Define the multi-year learning technology strategy and architecture for the enterprise, including platform consolidation decisions, integration patterns, identity and data flows, governance models, and build-versus-buy evaluation. Establish the intake and prioritization discipline that determines which technologies enter the ecosystem and which do not. Champion teammate-centric discovery—translating business priorities and clinical/operational workflows into high-impact technology solutions; working closely with our product and technology teams.


Decision Ownership & Vendor Partnership

Serve as the decision authority in vendor and implementation-partner engagements — evaluating proposed technical approaches, understanding downstream cost and timeline implications, negotiating scope, and rendering decisions at the pace delivery requires. Own commercial relationships, statements of work, and total cost of ownership across the learning technology portfolio.


Enterprise Program Leadership

Lead the delivery of complex, cross-functional technology programs from design through adoption, working alongside enterprise Technology, People Services, operations, and external partners. Ensure that what gets built serves the teammate experience, not just the delivery schedule. Establish objective adoption, engagement, and value-realization metrics to measure the enterprise impact of technology investments.


Team Leadership & Capability Building

Lead and develop a team of learning technology product and program managers. Build bench strength and continuity across business-critical platforms, and grow the team's capability from platform operation toward product ownership and strategic influence.



Risk, Continuity & Governance

Ensure the reliability, security posture, compliance, and continuity of learning systems that the enterprise depends on, in partnership with operational support functions. Effectively problem solve when things go wrong.



Minimum Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience required; Master's Degree in a related field (such as technology management or adult learning) preferred.
  • Technical Depth: 8+ years in learning technology, enterprise HR/talent technology, or adjacent enterprise platform leadership, including direct ownership of platform architecture and integration decisions. You can speak credibly and specifically about integration patterns and APIs, identity and access architecture, HRIS-to-learning data flows, reporting and data warehouse strategy, and the practical tradeoffs between single-platform and best-of-breed ecosystems. Must demonstrate proficiency in AI-enablement and use of LLMs.
  • Decision Ownership: Demonstrated track record of owning consequential technology decisions — not just recommending them. title: MEAL Manager
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Program Brief


The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solution driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

Since 2017, IRC has supported Rohingya Refugees and Bangladeshi nationalities communities in Cox's Bazar, Khulna, Barisal, and Chittagong with integrated services. The organization also addresses climate change impacts by building resilience and promoting economic recovery, education, and protection.

Purpose of the Role

Reporting directly to the Head of MEAL and Program Quality, you will strengthen the MEAL efforts, approaches, and systems to foster learning and accountability for our clients; support IRC’s global and measurement ambitions of Strategy 100 and the Country Strategic Action Plan. You will oversee the MEAL functions of the sector program(s) to which you are assigned — which may include Education, Health, Protection, Economic Recovery and Development, and/or Emergency Preparedness and Response — within the Bangladesh MEAL team. As this is a generic job description, the specific sector(s) or program area(s) assigned to the jobholder will be determined by the Head of MEAL and Program Quality based on organizational needs, and the jobholder may be reassigned across sectors over time.

Highlights of Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership and Partnership

  • Manage all technical aspects and actions of MEAL; respond to program needs; foster high standards and practices for quality data, analysis, and reports. Enable accountability to clients, partners, and donors.
  • Improve MEAL systems and approaches and foster learning.
  • Represent IRC at technical meetings, forums, and other events & build partnership within IRC and other areas of expertise.
  • Champion design, access, and use of data by leaders and partners for shared learning and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Collaborate with MEAL teams within and outside IRC to support harmonization of MEAL systems and approaches, sharing capacity and experiences.

Technical Oversight

  • Lead the MEAL system and processes for the programs in harmony with the MEAL Country and Global Strategy throughout the project cycle by:
  • Using learning, evidence, and data from previous projects to inform project proposal design.
  • Working with the Head of MEAL and Program Quality to develop logical frameworks and MEAL plans, and with the MIS Manager to develop digital data collection tools, and processes for online data management.
  • Establishing and ensuring timely data flow, quality checks, and audits, and updating of data visualization.
  • Supervising routine MEAL field activities.
  • Conducting periodic field monitoring visits to assess program quality as per agreed upon checklists and benchmarks.
  • Undertaking regular analysis of monitoring data and working closely with program coordinators and managers to facilitate decision-making for real-time program adaptation.
  • Producing quality reports and updating dashboards with key findings that foster learning and decision-making and share in project cycle management meetings and team meetings.
  • Working with the Accountability and Knowledge Management Specialist to identify, detail, and share lessons learned to improve services and results for our clients.
  • Coordinating with relevant partners to ensure that they can collect data and provide their inputs as per agreed upon timelines.
  • Provide data and programming inputs to the Head of MEAL and Program Quality to support the design, method, and conduct of surveys such as baseline and end line, and the commission of evaluations in coordination with colleagues and partners.
  • Advocate for and support the expansion of standard mobile data technology and online dashboard to enhance timeliness and quality of data collection, analysis, and visualization.
  • Join and contribute to IRC's effort in meeting its internal and external accountability commitments through the implementation of sound accountability, client feedback, and response mechanisms.

Team Management

  • Coordinate, lead, mentor and support a dynamic small team of MEAL staff; foster timely and high-quality achievement, and an inclusive and respectful team climate.
  • Promote the growth and development of others in IRC teams and partners in MEAL: Lead and craft high-quality technical training and learning materials for partners, colleagues, and junior staff.
  • Participate in the recruitment and onboarding of country MEAL officers, assistants, and relevant partner staff.

Other

  • Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion and cohesion in IRC [team/office]
  • Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies.

Working Relationships

  • Internally, reports to Head of MEAL and Program Quality, supervises Senior MEAL Officer(s), and liaises with technical Coordinators/Managers throughout the country program.
  • Externally, supports partner MEAL staff, and ensures account

Required Experience

  • A Minimum 5 years of working experience in MEAL related functions.
  • A University degree in statistics & data management, social science, public health, development economics, or a related subject area.
  • Technical skills in setting up quality MEAL processes and creating logical frameworks and data analysis that leads to learning and action.
  • Proficiency and experience with mobile data collection such as Kobo, Commcare, ODK Collect is vital as well as proficiency with Microsoft Excel, SPSS, STATA or other similar software. Knowledge of Tableau, PowerBi, or GIS software tools are additional assets.
  • Demonstrated analytical, systematic-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proven ability to transfer knowledge to diverse audiences through training, mentoring, and other formal and non-formal methods together with presentation and reporting skills are a strong asset.
  • Confirmed ability to lead, mentor and empower a small to medium professional team.
  • Self-motivated with good organization, planning skills, including prioritizing work and multi-tasking.
  • A strong understanding of accountability and proven ability to build Client Feedback Systems.
  • Willingness to travel to various field-level offices.
  • Ability to communicate in English, with strong English writing skills; knowledge of Bangla and/or Chittagonian is an asset.
  • Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply.

Specific Educational Qualification

  • A University degree in statistics & data management, social science, public health, development economics, or a related subject area.

Professional Degree/ Certification

  • N/A

Standard of Professional Conduct

The IRC and the IRC workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the IRC Way – our Code of Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability, and Equality. In accordance with these values the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding (including PSEAH, Adult Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding), Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti Retaliation.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

  • Ability to obtain a NV2 security clearance is essential for this role

A Defence security clearance is required for this role, applicants must be Australian citizens and eligible to obtain and maintain an appropriate clearance.

Additional information with regards to clearances is available from the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency website http://www.defence.gov.au/AGSVA/. In some cases, individuals who hold a current clearance from a foreign government may be eligible to have this clearance recognised by the Australian Government and be eligible for this role.The Australian Defence Trade Controls Act (DTCA) is applicable and as such, your nationality may be a factor in determining your suitability for this role.

  • Personal Development and Career Progression
  • A Culture Built on Trust, Respect, and Empowerment

Be part of a company that values your contribution and invests in your future.

What You’ll Be Doing…

The Senior Business Intelligence Architect is a hands-on technical leader who will shape Fenner’s data and analytics strategy and help reinforce the 3 pillars of Fenner’s Digital Transformation – Tools+Data+People. This role will turn complex business challenges into scalable solutions using Azure, Databricks, Power BI, automation, and AI, while setting technical direction, strengthening data governance, and coaching the BI team.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Architecture and Strategy

  • Lead the design and evolution of Fenner’s enterprise BI, data warehouse, and analytics architecture.
  • Develop scalable architecture that supports structured and unstructured data from multiple business systems.
  • Establish technical roadmaps, architecture standards, and design patterns for data ingestion, transformation, storage, modeling, and visualization.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend solutions that improve scalability, reliability, security, and business value.
  • Ensure analytics architecture aligns with broader IT, cybersecurity, and business strategies.

Data Engineering and Platform Management

  • Provide technical oversight for the daily operation, performance, and reliability of the Fenner Data Warehouse and analytics ecosystem.
  • Architect and develop robust data pipelines that integrate ERP, manufacturing, financial, commercial, supply chain, and other enterprise data sources.
  • Design, optimize, and govern ETL and ELT processes across Azure, Databricks, SQL Server, and related platforms.
  • Lead performance tuning, troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and platform optimization.
  • Implement monitoring and controls that support accurate, complete, secure, and timely data delivery.

Data Modeling and Analytics Solutions

  • Design dimensional, semantic, and enterprise data models that provide consistent definitions and high-performance analytics.
  • Translate complex business needs into technical requirements, solution designs, and actionable implementation plans.
  • Lead the development of advanced reports, dashboards, data products, and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • Establish standards for Power BI development, including data models, DAX, security, performance, usability, and deployment.
  • Ensure analytics solutions deliver clear, meaningful, and actionable business insights.

Data Governance, Quality, and Security

  • Partner with business and technology leaders to establish data ownership, stewardship, governance, and accountability.
  • Define and enforce standards for data quality, documentation, lineage, access, retention, and security.
  • Ensure compliance with internal requirements, applicable regulations, and data-protection practices.
  • Develop testing and validation frameworks that support reliable and consistent analytics solutions.
  • Ensure adherence to configuration management, change control, release management, and development standards.

Technical Leadership and Mentorship

  • Serve as a senior technical resource for BI Analysts, data professionals, application teams, and business users.
  • Mentor team members in data modeling, pipeline development, visualization, testing, documentation, and BI best practices.
  • Lead architecture reviews and provide guidance on complex technical and functional decisions.
  • Promote consistent development practices, reusable solutions, and knowledge sharing across the organization.
  • Build trust in data and analytics by communicating technical concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

Digital Transformation

  • Be a force for change, driving data elements of Fenner's Digital Transformation initiative.
  • Partner with business leaders to understand, challenge, and redesign business processes, not simply automate the way they work today.
  • Identify opportunities to use data, analytics, automation, AI, and modern digital technologies to improve business performance.
  • Turn business problems into practical digital solutions, from idea and architecture through implementation and adoption.
  • Act as a bridge between business and technology, helping users understand what is possible and translating opportunities into actionable solutions.
  • Champion self-service analytics and data-driven decision-making, while maintaining appropriate data architecture, governance, and standards.
  • Help drive adoption of new technologies by educating, demonstrating, prototyping, and influencing, not simply delivering technical solutions.
  • Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, and continuous improvement around data and digital technology.

Business Partnership and Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, Commercial, Quality, HR, and other functions to understand business processes and analytics needs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve data capture, automate manual processes, and accelerate access to actionable information.
  • Lead discovery sessions and translate business challenges into prioritized analytics use cases.
  • Measure the effectiveness and adoption of BI solutions and recommend opportunities for improvement.
  • Support Lean Continuous Improvement through data-driven analysis and scalable digital solutions.

General

  • Perform additional responsibilities as assigned.
  • Model and uphold Fenner Precision Polymers’ Values and Behaviors at all times.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Analytics, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in a related discipline is preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience may be considered.

Experience

  • 7 or more years of progressive experience in business intelligence, data architecture, data engineering, analytics, or enterprise data warehousing.
  • At least 3 years of experience leading complex BI architecture or data engineering initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience designing scalable enterprise data models, data pipelines, and analytics platforms.
  • Experience mentoring technical professionals and influencing cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing, supply chain, finance, or other enterprise business functions is strongly preferred.

Technical Qualifications

  • Advanced experience with Microsoft Azure data and analytics services.
  • Strong experience with Databricks, data lakes, lakehouse architecture, or comparable modern data platforms.
  • Expert-level SQL development and performance tuning capabilities.
  • Advanced experience with Power BI, semantic modeling, DAX, data visualization, and enterprise deployment practices.
  • Experience with Microsoft SQL Server technologies, including SSIS, SSAS, and SSRS.
  • Strong knowledge of dimensional modeling, data warehouse architecture, ETL/ELT design, and data integration.
  • Experience implementing data governance, quality, lineage, security, and access-control standards.
  • Familiarity with DevOps, source control, automated testing, deployment pipelines, and change-management practices.
  • Experience integrating ERP, manufacturing, financial, and other enterprise systems is preferred.

Leadership Competencies

  • Ability to establish technical direction and execute against it.
  • Strong coaching skills to help less-experienced team members grow.
  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to explain complex technical concepts to business stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions without direct authority.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Collaborative, customer-focused approach with a commitment to quality and continuous improvement.

Growth Opportunities…

This role offers a clear path for advancement. High-performing individuals will have the opportunity to grow at Fenner Precision Polymers, taking on greater responsibility, strategic influence, and leadership within the IT team.

title: Automation Architect
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Automation Architect



Role summary: Security Architecture & Engineering needs an architect to own how the team automates its work, and to manage the engineers who build it. This person designs the automation approach, sets the patterns and standards it is built to, and leads a small team delivering against it.


Key responsibilities: Own the automation architecture and roadmap for the team; design and build automation that holds up over time; set the harness strategy for agentic workflows; contribute technical input to cloud security and application security direction; and manage and develop a small team of automation engineers.


Team and collaboration: This role manages a small team of automation engineers and works across the full Security Architecture & Engineering team, as well as with platform owners and engineering partners whose systems the automation touches.


What You'll Be Doing

As Automation Architect on the Security Architecture & Engineering team, you will own how the team automates its work. You will decide what gets automated and in what order, design the approach, and set the standards the work is built to so it stays reliable as it grows. You will set the harness strategy for how agentic workflows are built, and contribute technical input to the team's direction in cloud security and application security. You will stay hands-on in the code while managing a small team of engineers—setting their direction, reviewing their work, developing their skills, and accounting for what the team delivers.


How You'll Succeed


Engineering depth: You will write production-quality Python and build systems rather than scripts—with error handling, logging, tests, and documentation sufficient for someone else to pick the work up. You will integrate systems through APIs with attention to authentication, rate limiting, pagination, and failure modes.

Security fluency: You will understand the security data you are working with well enough to judge whether the output is sound, and you will recognize when an automated result looks wrong.

AI-augmented workflow design: You will design and operate AI and agentic workflows and own the harness strategy behind them—how agents are scaffolded, what context and tooling they are given, and how their output is evaluated. You will exercise sound judgment on where automation is appropriate and where human review needs to stay in the loop.

Reliability and maintainability: You will build for the long run. What you deliver will be documented, tested, and structured so other engineers can extend it, and you will improve the existing codebase rather than layering new work on top of fragile foundations.

Identifying the right work: You will spot where automation returns the most, make the case for it clearly, and sequence the work so value lands early rather than all at the end.

Strategic input beyond automation: You will bring a technical perspective to the team's broader direction in cloud security and application security, where automation and tooling choices shape what is practical.


Leading engineers: You will manage a small team, setting direction, reviewing code, and developing people. You will stay hands-on enough to hold technical credibility with the engineers you lead, and you will give them room to own work rather than routing everything through yourself.


Key Responsibilities

  • Own the automation architecture and roadmap for the team, sequencing work against where it returns the most.
  • Design and build automation in Python, including integrations with the platforms and systems the team depends on.
  • Design and operate AI-augmented and agentic workflows, keeping human judgment in the loop where the decision warrants it.
  • Set the harness strategy for agentic workflows — how agents are scaffolded, what context and tooling they are given, and how their output is evaluated.
  • Set and uphold engineering standards for automation work, including code review, version control practice, testing, and deployment.
  • Maintain and improve the existing codebase so it stays reliable and extensible.
  • Identify candidates for automation across the team and work with process owners to design the replacement.
  • Contribute technical input to the team's direction in cloud security and application security.
  • Manage a small team of automation engineers — setting priorities, reviewing work, conducting performance and development conversations, and supporting their growth.
  • Hire for and onboard into the automation team as it grows, and account for what the team delivers.
  • Document what is built so the team can operate, extend, and troubleshoot it without the original author.

What You Should Bring

  • Strong Python skills applied to real systems — data manipulation, API clients, error handling, logging, testing, and packaging. Able to design a system rather than only write a script.
  • Experience integrating systems through REST APIs, including authentication patterns, pagination, rate limiting, and retry logic.
  • Enough security depth to interpret the data the automation handles and judge whether the output is sound. Background can come from security engineering, security review and architecture work, cloud or application security, or a software engineering path that moved into security.
  • Working knowledge of cloud security and application security concepts, and familiarity with the categories of tooling that produce findings in each.
  • Experience with AI or agentic workflows applied to real work, or demonstrated aptitude and interest in building them.
  • Git and version control fluency, with experience working in a shared codebase through pull requests and code review.
  • Experience leading engineers — as a direct manager, or as a technical lead ready to step into people management. Setting direction, reviewing work, and developing others should be familiar territory.
  • Clear written communication — able to document a system, explain a design decision, and write up what an automation does for a non-engineer.
  • Judgment on where automation belongs and where it does not, and willingness to say so.



Basic Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma/equivalent with 4+ years of experience in Cyber Security, Information Technology, or related field.
  • 5+ years of professional experience across security, software engineering, or a combination, including hands-on development work.
  • Experience leading engineers, whether as a direct manager or as a technical lead ready to take on people management.
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor's Degree (example in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Technology)
  • Strong practical engineering skill, with fluency in Python and comfort integrating systems through APIs. Enough security depth to understand the data the automation handles and to judge whether the output is sound.
  • Experience designing and operating AI-augmented or agentic workflows, or a clear aptitude and interest in doing so.

General Purpose of the Job


The ROPS Specialist I (Lab) performs essential duties within various teams of Revenue Operations. Works to develop and improve skills and knowledge. Generates creative solutions, collaborating with others where needed to explore alternative approaches. Identifying conflicts or roadblocks on assigned work, escalates concerns, support and collaborate with others to resolve issues is imperative. Actively seeks out new insights in functional area and communicates findings. Communicates by leveraging communication tools appropriately for team and business needs, adapting tone and language for audience. This position reports to the Supervisor Revenue Operations (Lab).


Essential Duties and Responsibilities


Functions and responsibilities may include, but not limited to:
• Generates and submits claims for electronic payers by utilizing the A/R system and clearinghouse to ensure proper and timely submission of all claim files
• Resolves errors associated with claim submission rejections via the appropriate payer by researching and/or calling the payer and facilitating corrections by another department if necessary
• Maintains payer billing and clinic demographic system tables timely and accurately
• Tracks medical record requests, perform periodic billing audits
• Maintains insurance records including but not limited to the patient’s eligibility and the calculation of coordination of benefits related to outpatient kidney dialysis lab testing. Teammates will utilize the patient insurance information provided by DKC ROPS, the facilities, and ancillary means to complete the registration process
• Resolves multiple discrepancies/errors in the A/R system to ensure timely claim submission
• Applies payments and/or denials to the appropriate patient claim accurately based on supporting documentation. Interprets non-cash denial line items accurately by selecting the closest related denial code in the AR system. When all efforts are exhausted, post unidentified items to unapplied cash and continues to seek resolution and perform adjustments within established department timeframes.
• Balances all posted amounts to check and batch amount; troubleshoot as necessary; resolve any out-of-balance conditions by posting adjustments and corrections for reconciliation purposes.
• Researches difficult Remittance Advices for resolution to avoid posting to the unapplied cash account by communicating with the insurance company and collections team for resolution assistance.
• Update cash batch tracking, prioritize workload, resolves work queues, and adjusts misapplied payments timely
• Takes appropriate steps to resolve credit balances, including but not limited to preparing the necessary documentation for processing a refund check from the Accounts Payable Department (Lab), requesting a recoupment from the payer, or completing an adjustment for false credits
• Evaluate credit balances in the A/R system to determine whether or not a refund is due, or an adjustment is needed
• Document pertinent information for the refund on the reversal tracking spreadsheet and address all returned checks and reprocess where applicable
• Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

  • Minimum of 6 months medical office or data entry experience preferred.

POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Assistant Registrar - Academic Records & Graduation, this position is responsible for maintaining accurate student records and supporting all aspects of the Institute’s six annual commencement ceremonies in Hyde Park, NY. Key duties include producing transcripts and diplomas, reviewing graduation applications and degree audits in Ellucian Colleague, and ensuring compliance with institutional policies and FERPA regulations. The role serves as a primary resource for students, departments, and external agencies regarding academic progress, graduation eligibility, and degree completion.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Processes academic probation and dismissal correspondence.
  • Maintains student records in both digital and paper formats.
  • Processes grade changes and corrections.
  • Updates and maintains student demographic information.
  • Produces and mails official and unofficial transcripts.
  • Verifies degrees and/or attendance to third parties and outside agencies.
  • Prepares Apostilles (authenticated graduation documents for alumni from non-US countries).
  • Maintains accuracy of commencement website.
  • Prompts students to complete the required graduation application prior to each Hyde Park, NY ceremony. Communicates directly with students regarding eligibility.
  • Confirms ceremony dates, diploma names, mailing addresses, etc.
  • Interacts with Student Financial and Registration Services regarding ceremony fees and financial holds.
  • Communicates participant list with related departments including Student Financial and Registration Services, Alumni Relations, Student Affairs, and Career and Academic Advising, and others.
  • Coordinates with commencement organizers in the creation of printed and digital communications including the commencement program and tickets.
  • Works with regalia vendors and others. Receives regalia shipments and prepares them for distribution.
  • Following the receipt of all final grades, assists the Assistant Registrar with final degree audits in preparation for the conferral of degrees. Verifies graduation honors.
  • Corresponds with students having outstanding degree requirements.
  • Prints and mails diplomas. Maintains inventory of diploma and related materials.
  • Creates reports as needed.
  • Assists with data cleanup projects.
  • Follows policies established by the college and external agencies to ensure compliance with state, federal and national accreditation standards, including FERPA.
