Position Summary:

Under the supervision of the SECR Security Supervisor, protect the assets of the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe including vendors, entertainers, patrons, employees, and structures. This is a seasonal/temporary position.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Manage emergency evacuation procedures in the event of a man-made or natural disaster.
  • Handle irate, disorderly, or intoxicated patrons professionally.
  • Respond to medical emergencies utilizing proper procedures.
  • Observe for any possible criminal activity such as larcenies, weapons, and disputes between patrons or associates and report them.
  • Patrol parking lots for any possible safety or security concerns, criminal activity, or anything out of the ordinary as needed.
  • Provide excellent customer service for all internal and external customers of the operations at all times. Provide solutions for customer concerns and continually focus on customer service as our top priority.
  • Must maintain strict confidentiality and present a positive, professional demeanor and image at all times.
  • The above duties and responsibilities are not an all-inclusive list but rather a general representation of the duties and responsibilities associated with this position. The duties and responsibilities will be subject to change based on organizational needs and/or deemed necessary by the supervisor.


Contacts/Purpose of Contacts:

  • Contact with associates within the organization, including Tribal Police, Surveillance, Tribal Fire, Mobile Medical Response, other agencies, and the general public.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Must be able to work weekends, holidays, and emergency shifts.


Desired Qualifications:

  • First Aid and CPR certification.


License, Certification, or Special Requirements:

  • Native American preference shall apply to all positions.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of safety operations and procedures, safety methods and practices, and public/customer service skills.
  • Knowledge of applicable Tribal, federal, state, county, and local laws, regulations, and requirements.
  • Skill in customer service and verbal communication.
  • Skill in sensing or spotting disruptive guests or situations.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to establish and maintain professional relationships with individuals of varying social and cultural backgrounds and with co-workers at all levels.
  • Ability to follow instructions in verbal and written format
  • Ability to demonstrate moral character, honesty, tact, fairness, lack of prejudice, and desire to help when dealing with people.
  • Ability to analyze situations and adopt appropriate courses of action.
  • Ability to exercise independent judgment.
  • Ability to use good judgment and foresight.
  • Ability to handle irate, disorderly, or intoxicated guests professionally.
  • Ability to use reasoning words to defuse verbal and physical altercations.


Physical Demands:

  • Frequent standing and walking throughout the facilities and outdoor areas.
  • Required to walk, sit, and/or stand for long periods of time.
  • Must be able to safely climb up and downstairs and a man-made hill.
  • Occasionally is required to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.


Work Environment:

  • Frequent walking and standing in a smoking environment and contact with the general public. Must possess sufficient stamina to work under all types of weather conditions including extreme hot/cold and to lift, carry, push, or pull a variety of tools, equipment, and materials.
  • Required to monitor hundreds to thousands of guests gathered in a designated area where shoulder to shoulder confined space is common. Disruptive behavior and physical altercations may occur.
  • Exposure to hazards associated with first responder duties, including smoke, noxious odors, fumes, chemicals, solvents, oils, and rendering emergency medical services with potential exposure to blood borne pathogens and communicable diseases.
  • Extended hours and irregular shifts may be required.

Store - PORT-VANCOUVER, WAThe Sales Manager leads and champions a high-performing selling culture across the store, driving strong sales results and an engaging customer experience. This role oversees front-end and service operations, ensuring consistent execution of selling behaviors, brand standards, and operational expectations. The Sales Manager supports the achievement of key sales and service KPIs through effective leadership, customer-focused coaching, and efficient day-to-day execution.

Major Activities

  • Assist Store Manager in leading and managing adherence to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Company programs to ensure compliance with applicable laws and requirements.
  • Ensure execution of Company policies and standards, holding team accountable for store conditions and results.
  • Model and coach best-in-class Customer Experience and ART of Selling behaviors, driving conversion and customer satisfaction.
  • Provide Manager-on-Duty (MOD) coverage, maintaining floor leadership, service standards, and operational continuity.
  • Ensure accurate and efficient use of POS and Self-Checkout systems, supporting smooth transactions and customer support.
  • Oversee Balloons business, birthday party operations, and other in-store programs and events
  • Promote and enroll customers in the Loyalty Rewards Program, driving retention and repeat visits through consistent execution.
  • Champion MCC/Extend services (US only), ensuring team awareness and customer adoption of protection plans and offerings.
  • Drive sales and operational excellence in the Knit & Sew Shop, including expertise and oversight of the Cut Bar experience.
  • Ensure efficient execution of BOPIS and Same Day Delivery, delivering timely order fulfillment and strong omni-channel service.
  • Support Custom Framing operations, including customer consultations and coordination with the frame shop (in select volume frame shops).
  • Train, coach, and develop team members through structured TM onboarding and ongoing skill-building across assigned departments.
  • Partner in maintaining strong Asset Protection practices, reducing shrink through awareness, compliance, and safe operations.

Other duties as assigned

Minimum Type of Experience Required

  • 3+ years retail leadership experience

Work Environment

  • Ability to remain standing for long periods of time
  • Ability to move throughout the store
  • Regular bending, lifting, carrying, reaching, and stretching
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull merchandise and fixtures, up to 25-50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Ability to climb ladders or step stools to stock and retrieve products.
  • Ability to perform repetitive motions, including scanning items, stocking shelves, and operating POS equipment.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with frequent customer interactions.
  • Work hours include nights, weekends and early mornings

Applicants in the U.S. must satisfy federal, state, and local legal requirements of the job.

Total Base Pay Range for this Position:

$18.00 - $23.20This position may be eligible for overtime compensation in accordance with state and local laws.

title: Senior Director, Portfolio Strategy, Analytics & Enablement, Cardiometabolic Research
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


The Portfolio Strategy, Analytics, & Enablement Lead for Cardiometabolic Research (CMR) will play a critical role in shaping & implementing CMR’s long-term vision, and will drive high-impact initiatives that foster growth, innovation, and operational excellence. As a strategic leader with vision, this individual will develop and implement initiatives that align therapeutic areas & cross-functional teams, ensuring seamless execution of organizational priorities while anticipating and responding to industry trends. Partnering closely with the CMR Lead Team (LT), they will own the portfolio fact base, regularly assess portfolio health, frame and run priority strategic projects, and support initiatives to improve communications, culture, and capabilities across CMR. This individual will also support efforts to communicate CMR portfolio status and progress across the broader organization, including to senior leadership.


Key Responsibilities


Portfolio strategy

  • Lead portfolio-level strategy projects for CMR from the initial framing of the question through analysis, synthesis, and a recommendation to the Core Leadership Team. This includes assembling the working team, driving discussions, and delivering actionable outputs.
  • Develop & maintain an integrated view of the CMR portfolio across therapeutic pillars, covering development stage, therapeutic modality, target novelty, risk-reward profile, and resource load. Use this view to evaluate portfolio health & make recommendations on improvements. This assessment will characterize the portfolio’s risk / reward distribution and project its expected shape as new pillars mature.
  • Partner with therapeutic area leaders to keep program strategies and learning plans current, and surface cross-portfolio issues such as shared scientific risks, resourcing conflicts, and unexplored white space.
  • Support the long-range planning cycle by translating CMR strategic priorities into plans, metrics, and dashboards that the Core Leadership Team can manage against through the year.
  • Own the metrics and dashboards that track progress against CMR strategic objectives and establish them as the shared reference point in leadership discussions.
  • Track the external landscape relevant to cardiometabolic research, including competitive, scientific, and regulatory developments, and bring the implications into portfolio and planning discussions.

Organizational enablement

  • Support CMR's organizational communications, including monthly CMR updates to senior leadership, and development of content & execution of CMR-wide town halls in conjunction with therapeutic area leads.
  • Drive program management and change management for CMR-wide capability initiatives. One example is the Strategic Thinking program, which trains scientists to clarify program strategy, identify and prioritize key issues, and design experiments that resolve them.
  • Manage recurring organizational processes and campaigns, including the President's Award proposal process.


Basic Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in a life science, quantitative, or business field
  • 6+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology R&D with roles involving portfolio strategy, portfolio management, decision analytics, or strategy consulting serving those functions.
  • Experience leading cross-functional strategy projects from framing through to a leadership decision.

Additional Skills and Preferences

  • An advanced degree (PhD, PharmD, MS, or MBA)
  • Working knowledge of drug discovery and early development in cardiometabolic disease (diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular disease, and their complications)
  • Hands-on experience with portfolio analytics, including risk-adjusted valuation, probability of technical success, and resource and scenario modeling. The strongest candidates will be comfortable partnering with scientists on the quantitative work while owning the strategic framing themselves.
  • A track record of designing metrics and dashboards that senior leaders rely on
  • The ability to draw out diverse opinions in a matrixed organization and synthesize them into a recommendation that leadership will act on
  • Clear written and spoken communication to scientific and non-scientific audiences, including governance committees
  • A self-motivated individual who combines scientific curiosity with an enterprise mentality and a strong grasp of business concepts

  • PhD with specialization in Virology, Biochemistry, Biology, Molecular Biology, or related scientific field
  • 2+ years of industry experience

Additional Skills/Preferences:

  • Direct experience and good understanding in gene therapy or gene editing technologies
  • Hand on experience in NGS / PacBio
  • Experience in Virology, Cell Biology, Genetics, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Systems Biology, Immunology, or related scientific field
  • Experience in hiring and managing a team
  • Demonstrated proficiency and ability to deliver goals
  • Experience in timeline management and resource planning
  • Understanding of quality control processes

  • Excellent organizational, documentation, and communication skills; adaptive learning, critical thinking, and the ability to work well in a team

description:
About Us

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.

Our Core Values are:

  • We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
  • We never settle by constantly striving for better.
  • We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
  • We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.

Benefits

Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:

  • Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
  • 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • PTO accrual beginning Day 1

Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.

Job Summary

The Financial Counselor performs financial clearance tasks like verifying insurance and providing price estimates. This role resolves disputed billing issues through patient interaction. It also serves as an expert in financial assistance policies and facility collections, and supports special projects.

Essential Functions of the Role

  • Works closely with facility leadership to ensure all patients are financially cleared and screened.
  • Conducts patient interviews to obtain demographic and financial data for registration, insurance verification, pre-certification and billing.
  • Records accurate patient demographic information when reviewing previous accounts and accounts with future dates of service.
  • Follows and acts on several complex system policies (financial assistance, limited plan, point of service, out of network, etc.)
  • Obtains and screens guarantor financial information for financial assistance and or refers patient to appropriate resource for public assistance programs.
  • Provides estimates of procedures and services, calculates payment requirements, and negotiates pre-service payments according to financial clearance requirements.
  • Establishes payment arrangements for future and previous services.
  • Reviews future schedule to ensure pre-authorization and pre-payments have been collected.
  • Assists with contacting the physician's office and patient to ensure pre-authorization and referral requirements are met before the service date.
  • Reviews and interprets explanation of benefits from payers. This helps patients and guarantors understand claims processing or denial of services.

Key Success Factors

  • 3 years of healthcare experience or education equivalency required.
  • Proven ability to problem-solve, perform critical thinking.
  • Requires good listening, interpersonal and communication skills, and professional, pleasant and respectful telephone etiquette.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor in stressful and emotional environments. This includes crime, behavioral health, suffering patients, and life-or-death situations.
  • Must exhibit high empathy and communicate effectively with patients and families during traumatic events, while showing exceptional customer service skills.
  • Demonstrates ability to manage multiple, changing priorities in an effective and organized manner.
  • Excellent data entry, numeric, typing and computer navigational skills.
  • Basic computer skills and Microsoft Office and Excel.

Belonging Statement

We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • EDUCATION - H.S. Diploma/GED Equivalent
  • EXPERIENCE - 3 Years of Experience

title: Director of Critical Care, Clinical Education and Professional Practice - Full Time Days
description:
Director of Critical Care, Clinical Education and Professional Practice

Valley Presbyterian Hospital

Leading Clinical Excellence, Advancing Patient Care, and Empowering Our People

At Valley Presbyterian Hospital, we are committed to delivering exceptional, safe, and compassionate patient care to the communities we serve. We are seeking an experienced and visionary Director of Critical Care, Clinical Education and Professional Practice to provide strategic leadership, clinical oversight, and operational direction for critical care services and clinical education across the organization. This role is ideal for an accomplished nursing leader who is passionate about advancing evidence-based practice, developing clinical teams, driving quality improvement, and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous learning.

What You'll Do

  • Provide strategic leadership and operational oversight for critical care and clinical practice, ensuring safe, evidence-based, and patient-centered care.
  • Partner with the Vice President/Chief Nursing Officer and executive leadership to implement organizational strategies, advance hospital initiatives, and support the mission, vision, and values of Valley Presbyterian Hospital.
  • Drive clinical quality, patient safety, operational efficiency, and performance improvement initiatives to achieve organizational and national benchmarks.
  • Develop, implement, and evaluate clinical policies, procedures, and standards of practice in collaboration with clinical leaders, subject matter experts, and medical staff.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, accreditation requirements, and professional standards, including DNV and the California Nurse Practice Act.
  • Develop, monitor, and manage departmental budgets, ensuring responsible stewardship of hospital resources and achievement of financial and operational targets.
  • Foster a culture of recruitment, retention, professional development, recognition, and engagement for clinical staff, educators, and managers.
  • Oversee the development, implementation, and evaluation of evidence-based clinical education programs that address the learning needs of employees and support excellent patient outcomes.
  • Provide leadership and mentorship to clinical educators, supporting professional growth, competency development, and effective educational practices.
  • Establish and maintain processes for tracking mandatory education, competency validation, orientation, revalidation, and ongoing professional development.
  • Standardize educational programs and clinical competencies across Nursing, Allied Health, and Support Services based on roles, responsibilities, and licensure requirements.
  • Oversee the organization's Learning Management System (LMS) and Simulation Laboratory, ensuring effective utilization and alignment with organizational learning goals.
  • Develop and manage the Department of Education budget, including personnel, supplies, capital, and operational needs.
  • Evaluate educational program effectiveness, monitor expenditures, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with nursing schools and clinical programs to evaluate student placement, educational partnerships, and outreach opportunities.
  • Promote evidence-based practice, research, clinical transformation, and the integration of best practices into patient care.
  • Provide oversight of clinical information technology initiatives, including evidence-based workflows, order sets, forms, and clinical documentation tools.
  • Facilitate collaboration among clinicians, IT, and operational leaders to enhance clinical systems, productivity, and patient outcomes.
  • Partner with hospital leadership, medical staff, and interdisciplinary teams to identify opportunities for process improvement, resolve operational challenges, and advance patient safety.
  • Provide timely, constructive feedback and support professional accountability, clinical excellence, and organizational effectiveness.

What You'll Bring

  • Minimum of five (5) years of acute care clinical nursing experience.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of management or director-level leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, develop, and inspire diverse clinical teams.
  • Strong knowledge of clinical operations, nursing practice, regulatory requirements, and healthcare accreditation standards.
  • Proven ability to drive quality improvement, patient safety, operational efficiencies, and measurable clinical outcomes.
  • Experience developing and managing budgets, evaluating financial performance, and allocating resources effectively.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage complex projects and competing priorities.
  • Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments.
  • Experience with clinical education, competency validation, staff development, and evidence-based practice initiatives.
  • Proficiency with clinical information technology systems, learning management systems, and Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships with physicians, hospital leadership, clinical teams, vendors, and external partners.
  • Innovative and forward-thinking leadership approach with a commitment to continuous improvement and professional excellence.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree required, preferably in Nursing (BSN) or another healthcare-related field.
  • Master's degree in Nursing (MSN) or another healthcare-related field required.

Licensure & Certifications

  • Current and active Registered Nurse (RN) license with the California Board of Registered Nursing required.
  • Must successfully obtain and maintain LA City Fire Card certification at the time of hire or within the first 30 days of employment.

Required Training & Compliance

  • Must maintain all required licensures, certifications, mandatory education, and annual occupational health screenings in accordance with hospital policy.
  • Must comply with applicable regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and professional nursing practice guidelines.
  • Must maintain patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and Valley Presbyterian Hospital policies and procedures.
  • Must participate in required Environment of Care, emergency preparedness, infection prevention, workplace safety, and patient safety training.
  • Must actively participate in the Patient Safety Program, including event reporting, identification of near misses, and implementation of improvement initiatives.

Why Join Valley Presbyterian Hospital?

At Valley Presbyterian Hospital, you'll join a team where people feel connected to a meaningful mission, supported by their colleagues, and empowered to make a difference. Employees consistently report strong teamwork, a sense of belonging, and pride in serving our community. Our culture emphasizes respect, collaboration, inclusion, and compassionate care, creating an environment where people can grow professionally while making a lasting impact.

Apply today and help advance clinical excellence, strengthen professional practice, and elevate patient care at Valley Presbyterian Hospital.

title: Director - Product Management and MarTech
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


About Lilly

At Lilly, everything we do starts with patients.

We unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world.

Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our global team of over 50,000 employees work with urgency and purpose to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve.

We bring our best to this work because people depend on it.

If you’re driven by purpose and determined to make a meaningful difference for patients, we invite you to bring your skill and your commitment to Lilly.

About Lilly’s India Affiliate

Few careers offer the opportunity to work directly for the people your work is ultimately meant to serve.

Lilly’s India affiliate is one of them.

Whether you are building brand strategies, developing sales capabilities, creating market access, or enabling the teams that do — the work you do here ensures that Lilly’s medicines reach the people who need them.

Purpose of the Job

The Director – Product Management and MarTech leads the digital and marketing technology agenda for the CMO organisation. The role drives digitization initiatives across Strategic Capabilities and the enterprise-wide technology transformation agenda.

Additionally, the role will also help in shaping the user personalization strategy for AFL so that it is aligned with broader brand and commercial objectives. The role impacts across multiple functions.

The incumbent also acts as strategic digital partner to the team leads across CMO organisation capabilities: designing the product vision, translating it into user experience and interface design, running digital products that attract and retain users, and building a strong digital environment that the whole organisation can use. The role combines Digital Product Management, media, ad tech, digital and retention marketing expertise with the ability to lead technology-enabled change within strict medical, ethical and regulatory guardrails.

Regular interaction with CMO organisation leaders, Medical, Business Technology, E&C, Legal, Data Privacy, and IBU / global digital counterparts, and with external agencies and technology partners.

Recognised as an expert in the area, with strong ability to influence senior leaders, internal customers and external partners on key decisions.

Anticipates, identifies and solves complex technical and business problems affecting the functional area.

Roles and Responsibilities

Digital Vision & Product Strategy

  • Design the product vision and roadmap for MedMarTech, aligned with the CMO organisation’s brand, commercial and capability priorities.
  • Translate the vision into clear product requirements, user journeys and design specifications that engineering, design and agency teams, from build and launch through adoption, so that products are delivered on time, within budget and to quality standards.
  • Anticipate long- and short-term digital, customer and competitive trends and shape the strategy accordingly.

Digitization & Technology Transformation

  • Lead digitization initiatives across Strategic Capabilities, driving the enterprise-wide technology transformation agenda for the CMO organisation.
  • Partner with Business Technology, IBU and global digital teams to align local initiatives with global platforms, standards and roadmaps.
  • Identify and prioritise opportunities to improve processes, products and services through technology, and lead their delivery from concept to scale.

Digital Media Strategy & Ad Tech

  • Shape the digital media strategy jointly with CMO Functions and Tech leadership for AFL, ensuring alignment with broader brand and commercial objectives.
  • Define and govern the ad tech and media technology approach (e.g., programmatic buying, audience data, tracking and measurement), and guide agencies on channel mix, targeting and optimisation.
  • Ensure media effectiveness through measurement frameworks, attribution and continuous optimisation based on performance data.

Digital Product Management, UX & UI

  • Own digital products end to end as a digital product manager, with a focus on attracting and retaining users: discovery, design, launch, adoption and continuous improvement.
  • Set UX and UI standards and drive user research, journey mapping and usability testing so digital experiences are simple, engaging and consistent.
  • Use product analytics and user feedback to prioritise the backlog and improve engagement and retention.

Digital & Retention Marketing

  • Lead digital and retention marketing capabilities, including lifecycle journeys, personalisation and always-on engagement that bring users back and deepen their engagement.
  • Enable brand teams with reusable journeys, content frameworks and campaign playbooks; track retention, engagement and conversion outcomes.
  • Build capability in test-and-learn approaches to continuously improve channel and content performance.

MedMarTech Platforms & Digital Environment

  • Build and maintain a strong, integrated digital environment: marketing technology stack, content and experience platforms, data and analytics tools that work together.
  • Ensure platform architecture, data flows, integrations, security and scalability meet business needs, working with Business Technology and vendors.
  • Evaluate and introduce emerging technologies (including AI-enabled tools) through structured pilots and scale-up decisions.

Strategic Digital Partner to CMO Organisation

  • Partner with team leads across CMO organisation capabilities as their trusted digital and technology partner: understand their priorities, co-create solutions and prioritise requests against organisational objectives.
  • Define a clear MedMarTech offering (what is provided, how teams engage, how requests are prioritised and expected turnaround) so team leads know what to expect and can plan with confidence.
  • Deliver digital solutions, tools and support that make each team more effective; track and report the value delivered and use feedback to improve the offering continuously.

Vendor & Partner Ecosystem

  • Scout, select and manage agencies, technology vendors and ad tech partners; negotiate terms within budget and policy guidelines and hold partners accountable for performance.
  • Build a scalable partner ecosystem and governance model that improves speed, quality and cost efficiency.

Compliance, Data Privacy & Governance

  • Ensure digital products, media and marketing activities comply with Lilly policies, applicable regulations and industry codes, partnering with Medical, E&C, Legal and Data Privacy.
  • Embed governance for approved content and medical-legal-regulatory review, consent and data privacy, and digital security into product and campaign workflows.
  • Ensure adverse event and product complaint reporting requirements are built into digital channels and partner operations.

Analytics, Performance & Insights

  • Define KPIs and dashboards for digital media, product and retention performance; take ownership of reporting on adoption, engagement, retention and return on investment.
  • Turn data into insights and recommendations for CMO organisation leaders and use them to shape strategy and investment decisions.

Program & Budget Management

  • Lead large-scale programs with significant risk, resource and complexity to achieve critical business objectives, including the enterprise technology transformation agenda.
  • Manage resources and budgets for programs and operations, including forecasting, prioritisation and vendor spend.

Required Qualifications

  • MBA with Bachelor’s degree in Engineering.
  • 13–15 years of extensive experience in digital marketing, digital product management or marketing technology, with a track record of leading large digital transformation programs.
  • Specialised depth and breadth across digital media and ad tech, UX / UI and product design, and digital and retention marketing.
  • Experience partnering with business leaders as an internal service provider or digital solutions partner.
  • Experience managing agencies, technology vendors and budgets for large programs.

Additional Preferences

  • Experience in the pharmaceutical or healthcare industry, including working within promotional compliance, medical-legal-regulatory review and data privacy requirements.
  • Working knowledge of the marketing technology landscape: content and experience platforms, marketing automation, data and analytics tools.
  • Ability to translate a product vision into clear requirements, designs and delivery plans.
  • Ability to make complex technical and business decisions within functional, company and industry guidelines.
  • Awareness of emerging technologies, including AI, and how they can improve customer engagement and productivity.
  • Strong communication, storytelling and stakeholder management skills; sensitivity towards confidential data.
  • Strong people leadership: coaching and developing team members.

Additional Information

  • Expected to be based in the office 4 days a week.
  • May require domestic and international travel.
  • Must be legally allowed to work in India.
  • Incumbent must be based in Gurugram (Delhi NCR).

At Lilly, caring is not only what we do for patients.

It is how we work.

We believe the people who dedicate themselves to making medicines better deserve an environment that makes their lives better too, one where they are supported, respected, and given the space to do their best work.

This is not just a policy.

It is who we are.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


About Lilly

At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to create medicines that make life better for people around the world. The Digital Engagement Tech@Lilly team builds solutions and capabilities for Marketing, Corporate Affairs and Medical organizations globally, and owns the consumer platforms and the governance around them.


This role exists because the hardest problems in our space are not solved from a ticket queue. As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you will sit with business, medical and marketing teams, understand how they actually work, and build working AI-enabled software with them, fast. You will go from a vague problem to a live product in weeks, then take what you learned and turn it into reusable patterns for the rest of the organization.


Role Overview

A forward deployed engineer is a senior, hands-on builder who works at the point where technology meets the business problem. You will be embedded with stakeholder teams, own outcomes end to end (discovery, design, build, deploy, adoption), and stay close enough to users to see what works and what does not.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. You will spend most of your time building, across the front end, back end and AI layer, while working directly with product owners, system custodians, architects and compliance partners. You will operate with minimal supervision, set patterns and standards for others to follow, and mentor developers and engineers around you. Success means shipping reliable, well-governed solutions that people use, and that move a business metric.


What You Will Build

  • Customer-facing and internal web applications in React, Nuxt or Vue, backed by Node.js APIs, built directly with business teams and shipped on short cycles.
  • Agentic and LLM-powered workflows for content, engagement and medical use cases: multi-agent orchestration, tool use and intelligent automation of manual work.
  • RAG and semantic search solutions over enterprise content and data, including embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and Text2SQL where it fits.
  • Production AI services and APIs that integrate with enterprise data platforms, content systems and downstream product workflows.
  • Reusable patterns, templates, and accelerators that turn a one-off solution into something other teams can adopt.

Key Responsibilities

Embed and discover

  • Embed with business, medical and marketing teams to understand their workflows, pain points and constraints first-hand.
  • Frame ambiguous problems, decide what is worth building, and be direct about what is not feasible.
  • Prototype quickly, put working software in front of users early, and iterate on their feedback.

Build and deliver end to end

  • Design and build full-stack solutions: responsive front ends, API integrations, Node.js services and the data layer behind them.
  • Integrate LLMs, RAG, agents and AI services into products, with evaluation, guardrails and monitoring for quality, latency and cost.
  • Own the delivery lifecycle: scoping and estimation, development, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, monitoring and support handover.
  • Work with the technical lead and system custodian to keep what you ship maintainable, observable, and secure.

Architecture and standards

  • Make architectural decisions that improve efficiency and maintain compliance in a regulated space.
  • Turn what you learn in the field into reusable components, templates, and reference implementations for cross-functional teams.
  • Set and uphold coding standards, review practices and engineering patterns across teams.

Responsible AI, security and governance

  • Apply secure-by-design and privacy-by-design principles, and build in traceability, grounding, auditability and human oversight.
  • Work with quality, compliance and risk partners, so solutions meet regulatory and enterprise requirements, including content review processes.
  • Maintain clear architecture, design, and support documentation for everything you put into production.

Mentoring and influence

  • Provide hands-on technical guidance to developers and engineers, review designs and code, and raise the bar through practical examples.
  • Communicate trade-offs, risks and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leaders.
  • Bring practical feasibility, scalability, and value considerations into roadmap planning.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping production systems end to end.
  • 4+ years building customer-facing or business-facing solutions in close partnership with stakeholders, such as forward deployed, solutions engineering, consulting engineering or embedded product engineering roles.
  • Expert in HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/TypeScript and React, with Nuxt or Vue a plus; strong in responsive design and web standards.
  • Strong back-end experience with Node.js (Express, Koa or Hapi) and API design and integration (REST, GraphQL).
  • 2+ years of hands-on generative AI delivery: LLMs, prompt and context engineering, RAG, embeddings, agentic workflows, and evaluation of model outputs.
  • Working proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with frameworks such as LangChain, DSPy or Hugging Face.
  • Strong experience with unit and integration testing frameworks such as Jest, Mocha, Chai or Jasmine.
  • Experience designing, deploying and operating services on a major cloud (AWS preferred), with CI/CD, containers and monitoring.
  • Strong system design and architecture fundamentals: version control (GitHub), code reviews, and secure, maintainable, observable code.
  • Experience working in Agile teams, including scoping, estimation and backlog ownership.
  • Proven ability to turn ambiguous business problems into scalable solutions with measurable value, and to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Pharmaceutical, healthcare or other regulated-industry experience, including working within content review, privacy and compliance processes.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems, tool use, Text2SQL, semantic search, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and LLM evaluation.
  • Experience with vector databases, lakehouse platforms (such as Databricks), and enterprise AI platforms (such as SageMaker or Azure ML).
  • Experience fine-tuning or adapting models, and optimizing AI systems for quality, latency, throughput and cost.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, GitHub Actions and MLflow, or equivalent LLMOps tooling.
  • Experience working across multiple concurrent projects and with stakeholders in different countries and time zones.
  • Experience building developer tooling, internal platforms or accelerators that other teams adopt.
  • Familiarity with web experience platforms, CMS and content operations.

Professional Skills and Education

  • Comfortable in ambiguity: you move without a spec, make sound calls with incomplete information, and know when to ask.
  • High ownership and self-direction, with the maturity to work with minimal supervision.
  • Strong communicator, written and verbal, who can earn trust quickly with senior business stakeholders.
  • Pragmatic builder who favors working software and fast feedback over perfect plans.
  • Curious and quick to learn new technologies, with a drive to improve existing business and technical processes.
  • Strong coordination skills and the ability to balance several projects at once.
  • Demonstrated leadership, teamwork, and collaboration in a professional setting.

Education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, Engineering or a related technical field. A master's degree is preferred. Equivalent practical experience is considered.

title: Multimodality Tech PRN
description:
Schedule: PRN - Days, Evening, Nights and Weekends available-

Requirement: Min of 3 shifts per month plus 1 holiday per year

JOB SUMMARY

The Multimodality Technologist, under general supervision of a Radiologist, performs imaging procedures in two or more disciplines, such as XR, MG, US, CT, MR, Nuc Med or IR, on ambulatory and hospital patients as requested by a physician or other licensed provider for the diagnosis of disease and injury in accordance with established protocols.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE ROLE
ESSENTIAL FUNCTION OF THE JOB

Performs high quality multimodality procedures, according to exam protocol in a timely manner. Maintains production and quality of imaging procedures by following established standards and procedures.

Demonstrates an understanding of radiation dose reference levels, radiation dose monitoring, actions to be taken if the estimated dose exceeds set dose reference levels, and actions to be taken for cases when the reference level was exceeded which may include patient follow-up.

Demonstrates and understands proper use of iSTAT point of care testing for obtaining creatinine levels, if applicable.

Utilizes AIDET when communicating with patients to: identify patient service requirements, ensure correct exam is performed on the correct patient, and establish rapport with patients and others. Communicates clearly and calmly with patients and their family regarding the test to be performed and assesses patient's ability to tolerate exam.

Prepares patient and area for procedure by positioning patient, utilizing immobilization devices, moving equipment into specified position, while using appropriate settings and exposure factors.

Protects patients and employees by adhering to safety requirements, infection-control, drug and radiation policies, protocols, and techniques. Uses proper sterile techniques when preparing and performing invasive multimodality procedures and maintains hand hygiene requirements.

Maintains equipment and work area to meet quality and cleanliness standards. Works with engineers and physicists to ensure optimal operational capabilities of equipment. Reports issues to management or appropriate department. Assists in maintaining supplies inventory. Ensures individuals are safe to enter the department by screening them according to approved policies and procedures.

Obtains, verifies, and maintains all relevant documentation such as requisition/chart, patient history, pregnancy status, policies, and procedures, etc.

Maintains medical imaging records in appropriate systems, according to department policies and procedures.

KEY SUCCESS FACTORS

Able to perform high quality multimodality procedures according to exam protocol in a timely manner.

Able to explain the procedure and put patients at ease.

Able to provide services timely, accurately, and cost-efficient in compliance with established System and regulatory standards, policies, and procedures.

Able to perform tasks independently without need for routine oversight.

Able to maintain a calm and helpful attitude, even under times of stress, and take appropriate and reasonable steps to resolve issues.

Able to effectively administer first aid and use emergency cart.

Able to ensure customer satisfaction by limiting wait times, providing courteous service, remaining professional, reviewing patient satisfaction scores, and developing action plans when required.

Demonstrates and maintains current knowledge, continued education, and skills appropriate care for all age groups.

Able to serve as preceptor by providing quality training to new team members or current teams about new services and initiatives.

Able to take call, if required.

BENEFITS

Our competitive benefits package includes the following
- Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
- 401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
- Tuition Reimbursement
- PTO accrual beginning Day 1
Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level

QUALIFICATIONS

- EDUCATION - Grad of an Accredited Program

- EXPERIENCE - Less than 1 Year of Experience

- CERTIFICATION/LICENSE/REGISTRATION -
Medical Radiologic Tech (MRT)

Computed Tomography (NMTB-CT)

Radiation Safety (NMTB-RS)

Nuclear Cardiology Tech (NMTC-NCT)

Positron Emission Tomography (PET)

Basic Life Support (BLS): BLS within 30 days of hire or transfer.

American Reg MRI Tech (ARMRIT), ARRT-BS Breast Sonography (ARRT-BS), ARRT-CT Computed Tomography (ARRT-CT), ARRT-M Mammography (ARRT-M), ARRT-MR Magnetic Res Imaging (ARRT-MR), ARRT-N Nuclear Medicine Tech (ARRT-N), ARRT-R Radiography (ARRT-R), ARRT-S Sonography (ARRT-S), ARRT-VI Interventional Rad (ARRT-VI), Cert Nuclear Med Tech (CNMT), Reg Diag Med Sono-Abdomen (AB) (RDMS-AB), Reg Diag Med Sono-Breast (BR) (RDMS-BR), RDMS Fetal Echocardiograpy (RDMS-FE), Reg Diag Med Sono-OB/GYN (OB) (RDMS-OB), RDMS-Pediatric Sonography (PS) (RDMS-PS), Registered Vascular Tech (RVT): Certified by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists, Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board, or the American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonography in TWO imaging modalities and works routinely in both modalities. Approved modalities: ARRT-R, ARRT-CT, ARRT-CV,
ARRT-M, ARRT-MR, ARRT-N, ARRT-S, ARRT-VI, ARRT-BS,
ARRT-CI, RDMS-AB, RDMS-BR, RDMS-FE,
RDMS-OB, RDMS-PS, RVT, CNMT,
NMTCB-CT, RS, NCT, PET or ARMRIT.

ARRT-CI Cardiac-Interventional (ARRT-CI), ARRT-CV Cardiovasc-Inter Rad (ARRT-CV): Licensed by the State of Texas Medical Board as a Medical
Radiologic Technologist (MRT), unless the role is MRI and
Ultrasound.

title: Pre-Access Scheduling Specialist - Full-time With Benefits
description:

title: Technical Advisor for Clinical Lab
description:
Date Posted:

2026-11-06

County Line Rd Office

WHY JOIN FCS

At Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute, we believe our people are our strength and we invest in them. Offering competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits packages to include tuition reimbursement, 401-K match, pet and legal insurance.

A LITTLE BIT ABOUT FCS

Since 1984, Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute & Research Institute (FCS) has built a national reputation for excellence. With over 250 physicians, 220 nurse practitioners and physician assistants and nearly 100 locations in our network. Utilizing innovative clinical research, cutting-edge technologies, and advanced treatments, we are committed to providing world-class cancer care. We are recognized by the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) with a national Clinical Trials Participation Award, FCS offers patients access to more clinical trials than any private oncology practice in Florida. Our patients have access to ground-breaking therapies, in a community setting, and may participate in national clinical research studies of drugs and treatment protocols. In the past five years, the majority of new cancer drugs approved for use in the U.S. were studied in clinical trials with FCS participation prior to approval.

Through our partnership with Sarah Cannon, we are one of the largest clinical research organizations in the United States. Often, FCS leads the nation in initiating research studies and offering ground-breaking new therapies to patients.

Come join us today!

Summary:

Responsible for the technical and scientific oversight of the clinical laboratory, the Technical Advisor provides timely consultation and direction to ensure laboratory quality programs and services are implemented at the highest standards according to regulatory standards and established policies and procedures. The Technical Advisor ensures policies and procedures are followed and align with regulatory updates as well as coordinate and implement the lab quality management and quality improvement programs.

PRIMARY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Collaborate with laboratory leadership to maintain standardized laboratory workflows according to the regulatory requirements and company standard operating procedures and methods of practice.
  • Perform quality assurance functions to accomplish coordination, monitoring, and reporting of quality assurance actions and issues.
  • Review Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Proficiency testing, and equipment/analyzer service and preventive maintenance records at defined frequencies.
  • Remain regularly accessible to clinic lab personnel to provide on-site, telephone, or electronic meetings/consultation.
  • Prepare the clinic laboratory for COLA and CLIA validation surveys to include facilitating all surveys.
  • Coordinate and organize inspection information/documentation in addition to appropriate data gathering mechanisms, procedures, etc.
  • Identify gaps in understanding and provide in-service education, when needed.
  • Directly evaluate the competency and proficiency of all testing personnel, ensuring clinic lab staff perform test procedures, tasks, and report test results promptly and accurately.
  • Perform direct observation competency assessments at frequencies outlined by laboratory regulatory requirements; initial, semi-annual, annual, and annually thereafter.
  • Resolve technical problems ensuring that corrective actions are taken whenever test systems deviate from the clinic laboratory's established performance specifications.
  • Under the direction of laboratory leadership ensure specified quality indicators are monitored and correctly measured, providing appropriate and timely feedback to staff.
  • Support the financial goals of the company by being fiscally responsible in all areas, including Inventory management.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert to represent laboratory services in cross departmental presentations and other related projects.
  • Demonstrate working knowledge of all facets of role, regulatory standards, and organizational and departmental policies and procedures.
  • Support laboratory services in all other necessary duties, including but not limited to supporting new clinical and pathology test offerings, technology enhancements/improvements, workflow processes or system changes, and analyzer/ equipment upgrades.
  • Complete all duties required to keep laboratory in compliance with state and federal regulatory agencies.
  • Comply with all Federal laws and regulations pertaining to patient care, patients’ rights, safety, confidentiality, billing, and collections. Adhere to all FCS and departmental policies and procedures, including IT policies and procedures and Disaster Recovery Plan.
  • Will be expected to work at any location to help meet company business needs.
  • Will be expected to work overtime when given sufficient notice of required overtime.
  • Perform other duties and projects as assigned.

EDUCATION/CERTIFICATIONS & LICENSES:

Minimum education requirement to successfully perform in role (high school diploma or equivalent being the minimum requirement across all positions within FCS).

  • Bachelor’s degree in a Chemical, Biological, Physical, Medical Technology or Clinical Laboratory Science from an accredited institution required
  • Current State of Florida Medical/Clinical Laboratory Technologist license required
  • Current National Medical Technologist or Medical Laboratory Scientist certification required
  • Valid Florida driver’s license for travel to other FCS offices is required
  • BLS certification preferred

EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum of four (4) years of experience in a clinical laboratory setting.

CORE COMPETENCIES, KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES:

Essential competencies and KSAs targeted to successfully performing in role:

  • Critical thinking skills including solid problem solving, analysis, decision-making, planning, time management and organizational skills. Must be detailed oriented with the ability to exercise independent judgment.
  • Developed interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, diplomacy, tact, conflict management, delegation skills, and diversity awareness.
  • Able to work effectively with sensitive and confidential material and sometimes emotionally charged matters.
  • Good command of the English language.
  • Effective communication skills (oral, written, presentation), an active listener, and effectively provides balanced feedback.
  • Strong customer focus. Ability to build an engaging culture of quality, performance effectiveness and operational excellence through best practices, strong business and political acumen, collaboration, and partnerships, as well as a positive employee, physician, and community relations.
  • Effectively manages own time, conflicting priorities, self, stress, and professional development.
  • Self-motivated and self-starter with ability work independently with limited supervision. Ability to work remotely effectively as required.
  • Must be able to work effectively in a fast-paced, multi-site environment with demonstrated ability to balance competing priorities and demands from a variety of stakeholders and sites. Solid time management with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks.
  • Proficient in MS Office Word, Excel, Power Point, and Outlook required.

VALUES:

  • Patient First – Keeping the patient at the center of everything we do
  • Accountability – Taking responsibility for our actions
  • Commitment & Care – Upholding FCS vision through every action
  • Team – Working together, one team, one mission

Expectations for all Employees

Every FCS employee is expected to regularly conduct themselves in a professional and respectful manner, to comply with all labor laws, workplace policy and workplace practices. Employees are expected to bring issues of any forms of workplace harassment, discrimination, or other potential improprieties to the attention of their management or the human resources department.

SCREENINGS – Background and drug screens

Safeguarding our patients and each other is an important part of how we deliver the best care possible to the communities we serve. All offers of employment at Florida Cancer Specialists & Research Institute are contingent upon clear results of a thorough background screening. Additionally, as a condition of employment, FCS requires all new hires to receive various vaccinations, including the influenza vaccine, barring an approved exemption. In addition, FCS is a drug-free workplace, and all new hires will be subject to drug testing. Medical Marijuana cards are not recognized.

It is a high-impact role with strong visibility, helping the business anticipate issues, support timely decisions and continuously improve execution across projects and product lines.

• Balance needs, supply, capacity and critical resources across projects and product lines, including rough-cut capacity and resource planning.

• Identify constraints, bottlenecks and future capability needs and support scenario analysis, trade-offs, risk mitigation and recovery plans.

• Provide planning visibility and continuous improvement through KPIs, alignment between strategic and short-term planning and effective use of ERP/MRP/APS tools.

Education & Qualifications

Skills & Experience


Essential

• Strong capability in capacity planning and balancing needs and constraints.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, communication and teamwork skills.

• Advanced English, written and spoken.

Desirable

• Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken.


Key competencies


We are looking for someone who is:

• Strategic and structured thinker, comfortable managing complexity and competing priorities effectively.

• Strong leader and team developer with a collaborative cross-functional approach.

• High level of ownership and accountability

• Sound judgement under constraints, with a proactive, resilient and solution-oriented mindset.

• Committed to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

title: Retail Merchandise Manager (Full Time)
description:

title: Advisor, Analytical Chemistry
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Organization Overview:


At Lilly, we serve an extraordinary purpose — we make a difference for people around the globe by discovering, developing, and delivering medicines that help them live longer, healthier, more active lives. The Radiopharmaceuticals (RLT) Chemistry, Manufacturing & Controls (CM&C) group is at the forefront of advancing therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals from clinical development through commercial launch.


Position Overview:

The Advisor, Analytical Chemist is a critical technical role within the RLT CM&C Technical Operations function. Reporting to the Senior Director, Technical Operations, this position leads the technical transfer, development, optimization, and validation of analytical methods to support phase 1b to phase 3 radiopharmaceutical programs. The Advisor serves as the primary analytical chemistry subject matter expert (SME), driving scientifically sound, phase-appropriate method strategies that meet GMP, ICH, USP, and regulatory expectations.


This role operates at the intersection of analytical science, regulatory compliance, and cross-functional program delivery — collaborating closely with QC, CMC Regulatory, manufacturing, and external CDMO partners to ensure analytical readiness for late-phase development milestones and regulatory submissions.


Key Responsibilities:


Analytical Method Development & Optimization

  • Lead the design, development, and optimization of analytical methods for radiopharmaceutical API and drug products, including small molecules, peptides, and radiolabeled compounds.
  • Develop and optimize chromatographic methods (HPLC, UPLC, TLC, GC) and spectroscopic methods (gamma spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, UV/Vis, NMR) as appropriate for late-phase programs.
  • Apply phase-appropriate development strategies aligned with ICH Q14, ICH Q2(R2), and applicable USP/EP compendial requirements for late clinical phase through commercial programs.
  • Identify and implement analytical technology improvements and method modernization initiatives to support continuous improvement and commercial readiness.
  • Troubleshoot complex analytical method performance issues and implement robust, validated solutions.

Analytical Method Validation & Transfer

  • Author method validation protocols and reports in full compliance with ICH Q2(R2), USP <1225>, and applicable regulatory guidance for late-phase and commercial programs.
  • Lead analytical method qualification and validation activities at internal sites and external CDMOs/partners.
  • Perform or oversee technology transfer of validated methods to QC release and stability testing laboratories.
  • Prepare and review method transfer protocols, comparability studies, and qualification/validation reports.
  • Ensure validation data packages are complete, defensible, and ready for regulatory submission.

Regulatory & Documentation

  • Author analytical sections of CMC regulatory submissions (INDs, CTAs, NDA/BLA, MAA), including method descriptions, validation summaries, and specification justifications.
  • Develop and justify release and stability specifications for starting materials, intermediates, and drug products in collaboration with CMC Regulatory and QA.
  • Prepare responses to regulatory agency inquiries related to analytical methods and specifications.
  • Author and review standard test methods, SOPs, change controls, and technical reports in accordance with GMP and Good Documentation Practices.
  • Support internal and external GMP audits, providing technical analytical expertise as required.

GMP Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure all analytical activities are conducted in compliance with cGMP, cGLP, applicable FDA, EMA, Health Canada, ICH, USP, PDA, and Lilly quality standards.
  • Review and approve experimental data from internal labs and external CDMOs/vendors; interpret results and document conclusions accurately.
  • Lead or support investigations of out-of-specification (OOS) results, analytical deviations, and aberrant data using robust root cause analysis methodology.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & External Partnerships

  • Serve as the analytical chemistry SME for late-phase RLT programs, providing technical direction to cross-functional CMC teams.
  • Build and maintain productive working relationships with internal, external CDMOs, analytical service providers, and regulatory partners.
  • Collaborate with QC, CMC Regulatory, Manufacturing Sciences, and Supply Chain to ensure seamless analytical readiness for clinical and commercial supply.
  • Represent analytical capabilities in project team meetings, technical reviews, and governance forums.

Basic Requirements:

  • Earned Bachelor's degree in chemistry, analytical chemistry, or organic chemistry
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in analytical development, analytical validation, and/or analytical testing in a GMP setting.
  • Demonstrated expertise in the development and full ICH Q2(R2)-compliant validation of chromatographic (HPLC, UPLC, GC, TLC) and spectroscopic (MS, UV/Vis, gamma) analytical methods.
  • Functional knowledge of GMP regulations and applicable FDA, EMA, ICH, USP, and PDA guidelines relevant to analytical testing.
  • Proven ability to operate effectively in a cross-functional environment with strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Proficiency in analytical data systems and laboratory informatics (e.g., Empower, Chromeleon, MassLynx).
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to present technical data to diverse audiences including senior leadership and regulatory agencies.
  • Must be a Canadian citizen to be selected for this position.

Additional Preferences:

  • Master's degree in chemistry field with 5+ years of relevant experience, OR PhD in chemistry field with 2+ years of relevant experience
  • Experience working hands-on within the biotech or pharmaceutical industry
  • Experience with radiopharmaceutical analytical testing, including HPLC with radiometric detection, TLC (radiometric), and gamma spectroscopy for PET (F-18) and/or theranostic radioisotopes (Lu-177, Ac-225).
  • Hands-on experience authoring CMC regulatory submissions and method validation packages for late-phase (Phase 3) or commercial programs.
  • Experience with CDMO/external partner analytical qualification and method transfer in a GMP context.
  • Familiarity with regulatory expectations for late-phase radiopharmaceutical analytical control strategies (ICH Q14, Q8/Q9/Q10 pharmaceutical quality system principles).

Other Information:

  • Standard PPE and radiological safety protocols apply in RLT manufacturing and laboratory areas.
  • Estimated travel: 5-15% domestically and internationally (CDMOs, partner sites, conferences). A valid passport and eligibility to travel within North America and Europe are required.
  • Monday through Friday, standard business hours; periodic off-hours responsiveness may be required in support of GMP manufacturing or regulatory timelines.

title: Engineer - Drug Substance Synthetic Molecule Design and Development
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Synthetic Molecule Design and Development (SMDD) is involved in key activities for the development of synthetic active pharmaceutical ingredients from pre-clinical phases through commercialization of drug substances and drug products. Our scientists and engineers develop key technical and business solutions across the portfolio using their deep technical expertise to accelerate testing of the clinical hypothesis and overall drug development. SMDD delivers on these responsibilities by recognizing diverse talent and cultures are necessary to bring the next generation of life changing medicines to patients.


Our team is looking for creative and energetic candidates to facilitate unit operation development and process optimization of synthetic drug candidates to support clinical trials, regulatory submission, and product commercialization. The position presents an opportunity to work on dynamic teams comprised of process chemists, analytical chemists, formulation scientists, and engineers.


Position Responsibilities

  • Generate process design and unit operation knowledge based on engineering principles for small molecules, and other emerging therapeutic modalities.
  • Ensure successful scale-up of processes through fundamental engineering principles and equipment knowledge.
  • Design and execute laboratory experiments, including manual and automated high- and low-throughput reactors, in support of crystallization process design and optimization.
  • Develop drug substance processes and manufacturing technologies, with a focus on defining the physical properties of the API required for the drug product and designing crystallization processes to fulfill physical property and chemical purity requirements.
  • Leverage and develop process analytical technology (PAT), continuous processing, mechanistic models, and novel formulation platforms to develop well-understood and robust crystallization processes capable of enhancing or tailoring API physical properties.
  • Apply fundamental engineering and business principles to design and characterize synthetic processes. Use numerical engineering modeling tools to characterize reaction kinetics, reaction mechanisms, and process separations.
  • Engage in generating creative solutions for improving existing processes and the creation of novel ones.
  • Transfer process technical information to internal and external manufacturing sites. Provide technical oversight to external collaboration partners for laboratory and manufacturing activities.
  • Author and maintain documentation such as laboratory notebooks and technical reports.
  • Design effective and efficient process and equipment flow strategies, ensuring equipment is selected which is suitable and appropriate for its intended use, given the specific needs of the process.
  • Stay informed about new technology and best practices. Propose, justify, evaluate, and implement new equipment, processing techniques, and technologies.
  • Utilize technology to improve safety, quality, and productivity, both in development and manufacturing.
  • Publish and share original research externally through peer-reviewed articles and conferences.

​Minimum Qualifications:

  • B.S or M.S. in chemical engineering or closely related engineering field.
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Additional Skills/Preferences

  • Strong technical skills in synthetic organic chemistry with experience as a hands-on technical contributor in a laboratory environment.
  • Utilization of chemical engineering fundamentals towards crystallization process design: heat and mass transfer, thermodynamics, crystallization and precipitation kinetics, solid–liquid separations, drying, particle size reduction (milling), mixing theory, and experimental design.
  • Experience with online and offline analytical techniques and PAT such as image analysis tools, IR, Raman, FBRM, and solid-state characterization techniques such as XRPD, DSC, TGA, particle size analysis, and microscopy.
  • Demonstrated problem solving skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills and ability to collaborate in a team environment.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple activities and handle ambiguity.

Additional Information

  • Travel: 0 to 10%.
  • Location: Indianapolis, IN; Lilly Technology Center – North (LTC-N)

description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our 45,000 employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.


Organization Overview

Lilly Small Molecule Discovery is an organization purpose-built to create molecules that make life better for people. We focus on using cutting edge science to unlock new approaches that can treat people suffering from diseases with poor treatment options. We continually challenge ourselves to deliver molecules that can provide breakthrough efficacy with the highest possible safety margins. We are dedicated to optimizing our mindset, technology, and processes for faster, more nimble execution. Our success is built on a culture that empowers innovative problem solving through open collaboration and individual accountability.

Discovery Technology and Platforms is a newly established function within this organization. Its mission is to accelerate molecule discovery by building highly optimized foundational platforms, streamlining lab operations through advanced technologies and data connectivity, and intentionally investing in novel technologies and capabilities.


Frontier AI is a purpose-built team that fuses scientific agentic AI, lab automation, and unified data platforms to autonomously design, run, and refine experiments—accelerating molecule discovery.


Job Title: Agent Automation, Frontier AI

Position Summary

We are rebuilding the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle by integrating agentic AI, cloud-based orchestration, and LIMS infrastructure to connect experimental readouts with tools that accelerate laboratory science.

You will engineer the connective tissue between Agentic AI and physical lab systems building practical integrations with robotic platforms, analytical instruments, and data pipelines. You'll design agent workflows that reason over experimental data, trigger automated actions, and surface insights to scientists. This is a hands-on engineering role: you'll prototype rapidly, productionize what works, and collaborate with chemists, biologists, and automation engineers to deploy intelligent systems that accelerate molecule discovery tasks.


Research & Innovation

  • Build multi-agent systems with robust orchestration, state management, error recovery, and tool integration
  • Prototype and iterate rapidly on agent planning strategies, memory systems, and human-in-the-loop patterns
  • Design agent architectures that interface with lab automation platforms (Hamilton, Tecan, Opentrons) for closed-loop experimental execution

Solution Deployment

· Partner with automation engineers and scientists to transition prototypes into reliable lab operations

· Deploy and maintain containerized services using Docker and Kubernetes with GitOps and CI/CD practices

· Integrate cloud-based orchestration frameworks such as Argo on Kubernetes with laboratory control systems


External Engagement

  • Represent Frontier AI in the broader AI@Lilly and external AI research community: publish, give talks, review papers, and scout emerging trends.
  • Evaluate external vendors, open-source projects, and academic collaborations for strategic fit.

What Success Looks Like

  • Autonomous agents reliably execute experiments on physical laboratory instruments
  • Measurable reduction in DMTA turnaround through autonomous planning and execution
  • Agents you build become indispensable to the automation engineering community

· Frontier AI platforms scale from pilot deployments to production lab environments


Basic Qualifications

  • MS + 1 yr or BS + 3 yrs equivalent experience in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or related discipline with demonstrated wet-lab automation experience
  • Demonstrated experience with laboratory automation systems and LIMS/ELN integration
  • Direct experience integrating software control and/or AI systems with lab automation platforms (e.g., liquid handlers, analytical instruments, robotic workflows, high-throughput experimentation, flow chemistry)
  • Experience with containerization (Docker) and Kubernetes-based orchestration in cloud or production environments
  • Experience building scalable and production-level Python applications using tools like LangChain/LangGraph, AutoGen, OpenTelemetry, etc. (GitHub portfolio a plus)
  • Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1

Preferred

  • Experience with LLM post-training, fine-tuning, or RLHF
  • Experience deploying closed-loop autonomous experimentation, where agents plan, execute, and analyze experiments on physical instruments with minimal human intervention
  • Proven ability to build and maintain the translation layer between high-level planning logic and low-level instrument control
  • Demonstrable research experience, evidenced by contributions to projects, and ideally through publications in relevant ML/NLP venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR)
